docs.title: Q: What are the security best practices for Apex development?
docs.text:
A: Secure Apex development requires attention to multiple security layers: CRUD/FLS enforcement, SOQL injection prevention, XSS protection, and proper sharing model implementation. Following security best practices protects data and prevents vulnerabilities.

CRUD and FLS Enforcement:

// ❌ WRONG: No security checks
public class UnsafeAccountController {
    public static List<Account> getAccounts() {
        return [SELECT Id, Name, AnnualRevenue FROM Account];
    }

    public static void updateAccount(Account acc) {
        update acc;
    }
}

// ✅ CORRECT: Enforce CRUD and FLS
public class SecureAccountController {

    public static List<Account> getAccounts() {
        // Check object access
        if (!Schema.sObjectType.Account.isAccessible()) {
            throw new SecurityException('No access to Account object');
        }

        // Check field access
        if (!Schema.sObjectType.Account.fields.Name.isAccessible() ||
            !Schema.sObjectType.Account.fields.AnnualRevenue.isAccessible()) {
            throw new SecurityException('No access to required fields');
        }

        return [SELECT Id, Name, AnnualRevenue FROM Account];
    }

    public static void updateAccount(Account acc) {
        // Check update permission
        if (!Schema.sObjectType.Account.isUpdateable()) {
            throw new SecurityException('No update access to Account');
        }

        // Check field update permission
        if (!Schema.sObjectType.Account.fields.AnnualRevenue.isUpdateable()) {
            acc.AnnualRevenue = null; // Remove field user can't edit
        }

        update acc;
    }
}

Security Utility Class:

public class SecurityUtils {

    // Check object CRUD permissions
    public static Boolean hasObjectAccess(
        String objectName, 
        String operationType
    ) {
        Schema.SObjectType sObjType = Schema.getGlobalDescribe().get(objectName);
        if (sObjType == null) return false;

        Schema.DescribeSObjectResult describeResult = sObjType.getDescribe();

        switch on operationType.toLowerCase() {
            when 'create' {
                return describeResult.isCreateable();
            }
            when 'read' {
                return describeResult.isAccessible();
            }
            when 'update' {
                return describeResult.isUpdateable();
            }
            when 'delete' {
                return describeResult.isDeletable();
            }
            when else {
                return false;
            }
        }
    }

    // Check field-level security
    public static Boolean hasFieldAccess(
        String objectName,
        String fieldName,
        String accessType
    ) {
        Schema.SObjectType sObjType = Schema.getGlobalDescribe().get(objectName);
        if (sObjType == null) return false;

        Map<String, Schema.SObjectField> fields = 
            sObjType.getDescribe().fields.getMap();

        if (!fields.containsKey(fieldName)) return false;

        Schema.DescribeFieldResult fieldDescribe = 
            fields.get(fieldName).getDescribe();

        switch on accessType.toLowerCase() {
            when 'read' {
                return fieldDescribe.isAccessible();
            }
            when 'create' {
                return fieldDescribe.isCreateable();
            }
            when 'update' {
                return fieldDescribe.isUpdateable();
            }
            when else {
                return false;
            }
        }
    }

    // Strip inaccessible fields from query results
    public static List<SObject> stripInaccessible(
        List<SObject> records,
        AccessType accessType
    ) {
        if (records == null || records.isEmpty()) {
            return records;
        }

        SObjectAccessDecision decision = Security.stripInaccessible(
            accessType,
            records
        );

        return decision.getRecords();
    }
}

Using WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED:

public class SecureQueryController {

    // Enforce FLS with WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED
    public static List<Account> getAccountsSecure() {
        try {
            return [
                SELECT Id, Name, Industry, AnnualRevenue
                FROM Account
                WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED
                LIMIT 100
            ];
        } catch (System.QueryException e) {
            // Handle insufficient access
            System.debug('FLS violation: ' + e.getMessage());
            return new List<Account>();
        }
    }

    // Alternative: Use Security.stripInaccessible
    public static List<Account> getAccountsStripped() {
        List<Account> accounts = [
            SELECT Id, Name, Industry, AnnualRevenue
            FROM Account
            LIMIT 100
        ];

        SObjectAccessDecision decision = Security.stripInaccessible(
            AccessType.READABLE,
            accounts
        );

        // Returns only fields user has access to
        return decision.getRecords();

        // Check which fields were removed
        Map<String, Set<String>> removedFields = decision.getRemovedFields();
        System.debug('Removed fields: ' + removedFields);
    }
}

SOQL Injection Prevention:

// ❌ WRONG: Vulnerable to SOQL injection
public class UnsafeSearchController {
    public static List<Account> searchAccounts(String searchTerm) {
        String query = 'SELECT Id, Name FROM Account WHERE Name LIKE \'%' + 
                      searchTerm + '%\'';
        return Database.query(query);
    }
}

// ✅ CORRECT: Use bind variables
public class SafeSearchController {
    public static List<Account> searchAccounts(String searchTerm) {
        // Bind variable prevents injection
        String searchPattern = '%' + searchTerm + '%';
        return [
            SELECT Id, Name 
            FROM Account 
            WHERE Name LIKE :searchPattern
        ];
    }

    // For dynamic SOQL, use String.escapeSingleQuotes()
    public static List<SObject> dynamicSearch(
        String objectName,
        String fieldName,
        String searchTerm
    ) {
        // Validate object and field names (whitelist approach)
        if (!isValidObject(objectName) || !isValidField(objectName, fieldName)) {
            throw new SecurityException('Invalid object or field');
        }

        // Escape search term
        String safeTerm = String.escapeSingleQuotes(searchTerm);

        // Build query safely
        String query = 'SELECT Id, ' + fieldName + 
                      ' FROM ' + objectName +
                      ' WHERE ' + fieldName + ' LIKE \'%' + safeTerm + '%\'';

        return Database.query(query);
    }

    private static Boolean isValidObject(String objectName) {
        return Schema.getGlobalDescribe().containsKey(objectName);
    }

    private static Boolean isValidField(String objectName, String fieldName) {
        Schema.SObjectType sObjType = Schema.getGlobalDescribe().get(objectName);
        if (sObjType == null) return false;

        Map<String, Schema.SObjectField> fields = 
            sObjType.getDescribe().fields.getMap();
        return fields.containsKey(fieldName);
    }
}

XSS Prevention in Visualforce:

<!-- ❌ WRONG: Vulnerable to XSS -->
<apex:page controller="AccountController">
    <div>
        Account Name: {!accountName}
    </div>
</apex:page>

<!-- ✅ CORRECT: Use escape attribute -->
<apex:page controller="AccountController">
    <div>
        Account Name: <apex:outputText value="{!accountName}" escape="true"/>
    </div>

    <!-- For HTML output, sanitize first -->
    <div>
        <apex:outputText value="{!HTMLENCODE(accountName)}" escape="false"/>
    </div>
</apex:page>

XSS Prevention in LWC:

// ✅ CORRECT: LWC automatically escapes by default
import { LightningElement, api } from 'lwc';

export default class AccountDisplay extends LightningElement {
    @api accountName;

    // This is automatically escaped when rendered in template
    get displayName() {
        return this.accountName;
    }
}

// Template - safe by default
<template>
    <div>
        Account Name: {displayName}
    </div>

    <!-- For rendering HTML, sanitize first -->
    <div lwc:dom="manual"></div>
</template>

// In JavaScript, sanitize HTML before inserting
connectedCallback() {
    const container = this.template.querySelector('[lwc:dom="manual"]');
    // Use DOMPurify or similar library
    container.innerHTML = this.sanitizeHTML(this.htmlContent);
}

Sharing Model in Apex:

// Default: With Sharing (respects user sharing)
public with sharing class AccountController {
    public List<Account> getAccounts() {
        // Returns only accounts user has access to
        return [SELECT Id, Name FROM Account];
    }
}

// Without Sharing (ignores sharing, returns all records)
public without sharing class AccountReportController {
    public List<Account> getAllAccountsForReport() {
        // Returns all accounts regardless of sharing
        // Use carefully - requires business justification
        return [SELECT Id, Name FROM Account];
    }
}

// Inherited Sharing (uses sharing context of caller)
public inherited sharing class AccountUtility {
    public List<Account> getAccounts() {
        // Sharing behavior depends on caller
        return [SELECT Id, Name FROM Account];
    }
}

// Mixed Sharing Example
public with sharing class SecureAccountService {

    // This method respects sharing
    public List<Account> getUserAccounts() {
        return [SELECT Id, Name FROM Account];
    }

    // Call without sharing for specific operation
    public Integer getTotalAccountCount() {
        return new AccountCountHelper().getCount();
    }

    // Inner class without sharing
    private without sharing class AccountCountHelper {
        public Integer getCount() {
            return [SELECT COUNT() FROM Account];
        }
    }
}

Secure Remote Methods:

// Secure @AuraEnabled methods
public class SecureAuraController {

    @AuraEnabled(cacheable=true)
    public static List<Account> getAccounts() {
        // Enforce FLS
        if (!Schema.sObjectType.Account.isAccessible()) {
            throw new AuraHandledException('No access to Accounts');
        }

        try {
            return [
                SELECT Id, Name, Industry
                FROM Account
                WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED
                LIMIT 50
            ];
        } catch (Exception e) {
            throw new AuraHandledException('Error: ' + e.getMessage());
        }
    }

    @AuraEnabled
    public static void updateAccount(Id accountId, String newName) {
        // Validate input
        if (String.isBlank(accountId) || String.isBlank(newName)) {
            throw new AuraHandledException('Invalid parameters');
        }

        // Check permissions
        if (!Schema.sObjectType.Account.isUpdateable()) {
            throw new AuraHandledException('No update access');
        }

        // Sanitize input
        String safeName = String.escapeSingleQuotes(newName);

        // Update record
        Account acc = new Account(
            Id = accountId,
            Name = safeName
        );

        try {
            update acc;
        } catch (DmlException e) {
            throw new AuraHandledException('Update failed: ' + e.getMessage());
        }
    }
}

Governor Limits:

⚠️ Security checks (describe calls) count toward CPU time

⚠️ WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED may slightly impact query performance

⚠️ Security.stripInaccessible creates a new list (memory impact)

Best Practices:

  • ✅ Always enforce CRUD and FLS in Apex
  • ✅ Use WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED or Security.stripInaccessible
  • ✅ Default to "with sharing" unless specific requirement
  • ✅ Use bind variables to prevent SOQL injection
  • ✅ Escape user input for dynamic SOQL
  • ✅ Sanitize HTML output in Visualforce
  • ✅ Validate and sanitize all user inputs
  • ✅ Use SecurityUtils helper class for consistency
  • ✅ Document why "without sharing" is needed
  • ✅ Test with different user profiles
  • ✅ Use Custom Exceptions for security violations
  • ✅ Log security exceptions for monitoring

Common Mistakes:

  • ❌ Assuming all users have the same permissions
  • ❌ Using "without sharing" without justification
  • ❌ Not checking CRUD/FLS before DML operations
  • ❌ Building dynamic SOQL without input validation
  • ❌ Outputting unescaped user input in Visualforce
  • ❌ Not testing with restricted user profiles
  • ❌ Exposing sensitive data through @AuraEnabled methods

See Also:

  • Security.stripInaccessible() method
  • WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED clause
  • Sharing Keywords (with sharing, without sharing, inherited sharing)
  • Custom Exceptions for security violations

docs.title: Q: How do I implement a comprehensive security audit strategy?
docs.text:
A: A comprehensive security audit strategy involves regular reviews of user access, permission configurations, data security settings, and compliance with security policies. This ensures your Salesforce org maintains a strong security posture.

Security Audit Components:

1. User Access Audit
   - Active user review
   - Profile assignments
   - Permission set assignments
   - Role hierarchy placement
   - Last login dates

2. Permission Audit
   - Object permissions
   - Field-level security
   - System permissions
   - Administrative access

3. Sharing Audit
   - OWD settings
   - Sharing rules
   - Manual sharing
   - Apex managed sharing

4. Data Security Audit
   - Encryption status
   - Sensitive data identification
   - Data classification

5. Authentication Audit
   - 2FA compliance
   - Password policies
   - Session settings
   - Login hours/IP restrictions

6. Integration Security
   - Connected apps
   - API access
   - OAuth tokens
   - Named credentials

7. Compliance Audit
   - Regulatory requirements
   - Industry standards
   - Internal policies

Automated Security Health Check:

public class SecurityHealthChecker {

    public class SecurityReport {
        public List<String> criticalIssues = new List<String>();
        public List<String> warnings = new List<String>();
        public List<String> recommendations = new List<String>();
        public Integer riskScore = 0;
    }

    public static SecurityReport runSecurityAudit() {
        SecurityReport report = new SecurityReport();

        // Check user access
        report = checkUserAccess(report);

        // Check permissions
        report = checkPermissions(report);

        // Check sharing settings
        report = checkSharing(report);

        // Check authentication
        report = checkAuthentication(report);

        // Check integrations
        report = checkIntegrations(report);

        // Calculate risk score
        report.riskScore = calculateRiskScore(report);

        return report;
    }

    private static SecurityReport checkUserAccess(SecurityReport report) {
        // Check for inactive users with access
        List<User> inactiveUsers = [
            SELECT Id, Name, LastLoginDate
            FROM User
            WHERE IsActive = true
            AND LastLoginDate < LAST_N_DAYS:90
        ];

        if (!inactiveUsers.isEmpty()) {
            report.warnings.add(inactiveUsers.size() + 
                              ' active users haven\'t logged in for 90+ days');
        }

        // Check for users without roles
        Integer usersWithoutRoles = [
            SELECT COUNT()
            FROM User
            WHERE IsActive = true
            AND UserRoleId = null
            AND Profile.Name != 'System Administrator'
        ];

        if (usersWithoutRoles > 0) {
            report.warnings.add(usersWithoutRoles + ' users without roles');
        }

        // Check for excessive admin accounts
        Integer adminCount = [
            SELECT COUNT()
            FROM User
            WHERE IsActive = true
            AND Profile.Name = 'System Administrator'
        ];

        if (adminCount > 10) {
            report.warnings.add('High number of System Administrators: ' + adminCount);
        }

        return report;
    }

    private static SecurityReport checkPermissions(SecurityReport report) {
        // Check for "View All Data" permission
        Integer viewAllDataUsers = [
            SELECT COUNT()
            FROM PermissionSetAssignment
            WHERE PermissionSet.PermissionsViewAllData = true
            AND Assignee.IsActive = true
        ];

        if (viewAllDataUsers > 5) {
            report.criticalIssues.add(viewAllDataUsers + 
                                    ' users have View All Data permission');
        }

        // Check for "Modify All Data" permission
        Integer modifyAllDataUsers = [
            SELECT COUNT()
            FROM PermissionSetAssignment
            WHERE PermissionSet.PermissionsModifyAllData = true
            AND Assignee.IsActive = true
        ];

        if (modifyAllDataUsers > 3) {
            report.criticalIssues.add(modifyAllDataUsers + 
                                    ' users have Modify All Data permission');
        }

        return report;
    }

    private static SecurityReport checkSharing(SecurityReport report) {
        // This would query sharing settings metadata
        // Simplified example

        report.recommendations.add('Review OWD settings quarterly');
        report.recommendations.add('Audit sharing rules for necessity');

        return report;
    }

    private static SecurityReport checkAuthentication(SecurityReport report) {
        // Check 2FA compliance
        Integer totalUsers = [SELECT COUNT() FROM User WHERE IsActive = true];
        Integer usersWithMFA = [
            SELECT COUNT()
            FROM User
            WHERE IsActive = true
            AND (SELECT COUNT() FROM TwoFactorInfo) > 0
        ];

        Decimal mfaPercentage = (usersWithMFA * 100.0) / totalUsers;

        if (mfaPercentage < 100) {
            report.criticalIssues.add('Only ' + mfaPercentage.setScale(1) + 
                                    '% of users have 2FA enabled');
        }

        return report;
    }

    private static SecurityReport checkIntegrations(SecurityReport report) {
        // Check connected apps
        List<ConnectedApplication> apps = [
            SELECT Id, Name, CreatedDate
            FROM ConnectedApplication
        ];

        report.recommendations.add('Review ' + apps.size() + 
                                 ' connected apps for necessity');

        return report;
    }

    private static Integer calculateRiskScore(SecurityReport report) {
        Integer score = 0;
        score += report.criticalIssues.size() * 10;
        score += report.warnings.size() * 5;
        return score;
    }
}

User Access Review:

public class UserAccessReviewer {

    public class UserAccessReport {
        public User user;
        public Profile profile;
        public List<PermissionSet> permissionSets;
        public UserRole role;
        public List<GroupMember> groups;
        public DateTime lastLogin;
        public List<String> accessNotes;
    }

    public static List<UserAccessReport> generateAccessReports() {
        List<UserAccessReport> reports = new List<UserAccessReport>();

        List<User> users = [
            SELECT Id, Name, Email, Profile.Name, UserRole.Name, LastLoginDate
            FROM User
            WHERE IsActive = true
        ];

        for (User u : users) {
            UserAccessReport report = new UserAccessReport();
            report.user = u;
            report.lastLogin = u.LastLoginDate;
            report.accessNotes = new List<String>();

            // Get permission sets
            List<PermissionSetAssignment> assignments = [
                SELECT PermissionSet.Name, PermissionSet.Label
                FROM PermissionSetAssignment
                WHERE AssigneeId = :u.Id
            ];

            report.permissionSets = new List<PermissionSet>();
            for (PermissionSetAssignment psa : assignments) {
                // Build permission set list
            }

            // Analyze access
            analyzeUserAccess(report);

            reports.add(report);
        }

        return reports;
    }

    private static void analyzeUserAccess(UserAccessReport report) {
        // Check for stale access
        if (report.lastLogin < DateTime.now().addDays(-90)) {
            report.accessNotes.add('User inactive for 90+ days');
        }

        // Check for excessive permissions
        if (report.permissionSets.size() > 10) {
            report.accessNotes.add('User has ' + report.permissionSets.size() + 
                                 ' permission sets - review for necessity');
        }
    }

    public static void generateAccessReviewEmail() {
        List<UserAccessReport> reports = generateAccessReports();

        // Build email content
        String emailBody = 'Security Access Review\n\n';

        for (UserAccessReport report : reports) {
            if (!report.accessNotes.isEmpty()) {
                emailBody += 'User: ' + report.user.Name + '\n';
                for (String note : report.accessNotes) {
                    emailBody += '  - ' + note + '\n';
                }
                emailBody += '\n';
            }
        }

        // Send email to security team
        sendSecurityEmail(emailBody);
    }

    private static void sendSecurityEmail(String body) {
        Messaging.SingleEmailMessage mail = new Messaging.SingleEmailMessage();
        mail.setToAddresses(new String[]{'security@company.com'});
        mail.setSubject('Monthly Security Access Review');
        mail.setPlainTextBody(body);

        Messaging.sendEmail(new Messaging.SingleEmailMessage[]{mail});
    }
}

Security Metrics Dashboard:

public class SecurityMetrics {

    public class Metrics {
        public Integer activeUsers;
        public Decimal mfaCompliance;
        public Integer adminUsers;
        public Integer inactiveUsers;
        public Integer excessivePermissions;
        public Integer securityIncidents;
    }

    public static Metrics getSecurityMetrics() {
        Metrics m = new Metrics();

        // Active users
        m.activeUsers = [SELECT COUNT() FROM User WHERE IsActive = true];

        // MFA compliance
        Integer usersWithMFA = [
            SELECT COUNT()
            FROM User
            WHERE IsActive = true
            AND (SELECT COUNT() FROM TwoFactorInfo) > 0
        ];
        m.mfaCompliance = (usersWithMFA * 100.0) / m.activeUsers;

        // Admin users
        m.adminUsers = [
            SELECT COUNT()
            FROM User
            WHERE IsActive = true
            AND Profile.Name = 'System Administrator'
        ];

        // Inactive users (no login in 90 days)
        m.inactiveUsers = [
            SELECT COUNT()
            FROM User
            WHERE IsActive = true
            AND LastLoginDate < LAST_N_DAYS:90
        ];

        // Users with excessive permissions
        m.excessivePermissions = [
            SELECT COUNT()
            FROM PermissionSetAssignment
            WHERE PermissionSet.PermissionsModifyAllData = true
            AND Assignee.IsActive = true
        ];

        return m;
    }
}

Audit Trail Review:

public class AuditTrailReviewer {

    public static void reviewSetupAuditTrail() {
        // Review recent setup changes
        List<SetupAuditTrail> changes = [
            SELECT Action, CreatedBy.Name, CreatedDate, Section
            FROM SetupAuditTrail
            WHERE CreatedDate = LAST_N_DAYS:7
            ORDER BY CreatedDate DESC
        ];

        for (SetupAuditTrail change : changes) {
            // Analyze critical changes
            if (isCriticalChange(change)) {
                flagForReview(change);
            }
        }
    }

    private static Boolean isCriticalChange(SetupAuditTrail change) {
        Set<String> criticalActions = new Set<String>{
            'Profile Changed',
            'User Activated',
            'User Deactivated',
            'Permission Set Changed',
            'Sharing Rule Changed'
        };

        return criticalActions.contains(change.Action);
    }

    private static void flagForReview(SetupAuditTrail change) {
        System.debug('Critical change detected: ' + change.Action + 
                    ' by ' + change.CreatedBy.Name);
        // Create task for security team review
    }
}

docs.title: Q: How do I troubleshoot "Insufficient Access Rights" errors?
docs.text:
A: "Insufficient Access Rights" errors occur when a user attempts an operation they don't have permission to perform. Troubleshooting requires checking multiple security layers: object permissions, field-level security, record-level access, and specific operation permissions.

Common Causes:

1. Object-Level Access
   - User doesn't have Read/Create/Edit/Delete permission on object
   - Profile lacks CRUD permissions
   - Permission sets haven't been assigned

2. Record-Level Access
   - OWD is Private and user doesn't own record
   - User not in role hierarchy above record owner
   - No sharing rules grant access
   - Manual sharing not configured

3. Field-Level Security
   - Field is hidden via FLS
   - Field is read-only for user
   - User can see record but not specific fields

4. Special Permissions
   - "Transfer Records" permission missing
   - "Delete Activities" permission missing
   - "Edit Tasks" permission missing

Diagnostic Approach:

public class AccessDiagnostics {

    public class AccessReport {
        public Boolean hasObjectAccess;
        public Boolean hasFieldAccess;
        public Boolean hasRecordAccess;
        public String diagnosis;
        public List<String> issues = new List<String>();
    }

    public static AccessReport diagnoseAccess(
        Id userId,
        Id recordId,
        String operation
    ) {
        AccessReport report = new AccessReport();

        // Get record details
        SObject record = Database.query(
            'SELECT Id, OwnerId FROM ' + recordId.getSObjectType() + 
            ' WHERE Id = :recordId'
        );

        String objectName = String.valueOf(recordId.getSObjectType());

        // Check object access
        report.hasObjectAccess = checkObjectAccess(
            userId, 
            objectName, 
            operation
        );

        if (!report.hasObjectAccess) {
            report.issues.add('User lacks ' + operation + 
                            ' permission on ' + objectName);
        }

        // Check record access
        report.hasRecordAccess = checkRecordAccess(userId, recordId);

        if (!report.hasRecordAccess) {
            report.issues.add('User cannot access this specific record');
            analyzeRecordAccess(userId, record, report);
        }

        // Generate diagnosis
        report.diagnosis = generateDiagnosis(report);

        return report;
    }

    private static Boolean checkObjectAccess(
        Id userId,
        String objectName,
        String operation
    ) {
        // Get user's profile and permission sets
        User u = [
            SELECT Id, ProfileId 
            FROM User 
            WHERE Id = :userId
        ];

        // Check profile permissions
        String query = 'SELECT PermissionsCreate, PermissionsRead, ' +
                      'PermissionsEdit, PermissionsDelete ' +
                      'FROM ObjectPermissions ' +
                      'WHERE ParentId = :u.ProfileId ' +
                      'AND SObjectType = :objectName';

        List<ObjectPermissions> perms = Database.query(query);

        if (perms.isEmpty()) return false;

        ObjectPermissions perm = perms[0];

        switch on operation.toLowerCase() {
            when 'create' { return perm.PermissionsCreate; }
            when 'read' { return perm.PermissionsRead; }
            when 'edit' { return perm.PermissionsEdit; }
            when 'delete' { return perm.PermissionsDelete; }
            when else { return false; }
        }
    }

    private static Boolean checkRecordAccess(Id userId, Id recordId) {
        try {
            UserRecordAccess ura = [
                SELECT RecordId, HasReadAccess, HasEditAccess, HasDeleteAccess
                FROM UserRecordAccess
                WHERE UserId = :userId
                AND RecordId = :recordId
            ];

            return ura.HasReadAccess;
        } catch (QueryException e) {
            return false;
        }
    }

    private static void analyzeRecordAccess(
        Id userId,
        SObject record,
        AccessReport report
    ) {
        // Check if user owns record
        if (record.get('OwnerId') == userId) {
            report.issues.add('User owns record but still lacks access');
            report.issues.add('Check object-level permissions');
        } else {
            report.issues.add('User does not own record');

            // Check role hierarchy
            Boolean hasRoleAccess = checkRoleHierarchyAccess(
                userId, 
                (Id)record.get('OwnerId')
            );

            if (!hasRoleAccess) {
                report.issues.add('User is not above owner in role hierarchy');
            }

            // Check sharing rules
            report.issues.add('Check if sharing rules grant access');
        }
    }

    private static Boolean checkRoleHierarchyAccess(Id userId, Id ownerId) {
        User currentUser = [SELECT UserRoleId FROM User WHERE Id = :userId];
        User owner = [SELECT UserRoleId FROM User WHERE Id = :ownerId];

        if (currentUser.UserRoleId == null || owner.UserRoleId == null) {
            return false;
        }

        // Simplified - actual implementation would check hierarchy
        return currentUser.UserRoleId == owner.UserRoleId;
    }

    private static String generateDiagnosis(AccessReport report) {
        if (report.issues.isEmpty()) {
            return 'User has full access';
        }

        String diagnosis = 'Access Issues Found:\n';
        for (String issue : report.issues) {
            diagnosis += '- ' + issue + '\n';
        }

        return diagnosis;
    }
}

Quick Resolution Steps:

Step 1: Verify Object Permissions
- Check user's profile
- Check assigned permission sets
- Verify CRUD permissions enabled

Step 2: Check Record Ownership
- Who owns the record?
- Is user in role hierarchy above owner?
- Does OWD allow access?

Step 3: Review Sharing
- Check sharing rules
- Look for manual shares
- Verify team membership (for objects with teams)

Step 4: Check Field-Level Security
- Are required fields hidden?
- Can user edit the fields being updated?

Step 5: Special Permissions
- Check for special permission requirements
- Verify "Modify All" or "View All" if needed

Testing Access as Different User:

public class AccessTester {

    // Test if operation would succeed for user
    public static Boolean testUserAccess(
        Id userId,
        Id recordId,
        String operation
    ) {
        // This requires running as System Administrator

        // Get user
        User testUser = [SELECT Id, Name FROM User WHERE Id = :userId];

        // Attempt operation in user context
        Boolean hasAccess = false;

        System.runAs(testUser) {
            try {
                if (operation == 'read') {
                    SObject record = Database.query(
                        'SELECT Id FROM ' + recordId.getSObjectType() + 
                        ' WHERE Id = :recordId'
                    );
                    hasAccess = true;
                } else if (operation == 'edit') {
                    SObject record = recordId.getSObjectType().newSObject(recordId);
                    update record;
                    hasAccess = true;
                }
            } catch (Exception e) {
                System.debug('Access test failed: ' + e.getMessage());
                hasAccess = false;
            }
        }

        return hasAccess;
    }
}

Debug Log Analysis:

// Add this to your Apex to log access issues
public class AccessLogger {

    public static void logAccessAttempt(
        String operation,
        String objectType,
        Id recordId,
        Boolean success
    ) {
        String logMessage = 'Access Attempt: ' + operation + 
                          ' on ' + objectType;

        if (recordId != null) {
            logMessage += ' (Record: ' + recordId + ')';
        }

        logMessage += ' - ' + (success ? 'SUCCESS' : 'FAILED');

        System.debug(LoggingLevel.INFO, logMessage);

        if (!success) {
            // Log additional diagnostic info
            System.debug('User: ' + UserInfo.getUserId());
            System.debug('Profile: ' + UserInfo.getProfileId());
        }
    }
}

Common Scenarios and Solutions:

Scenario 1: User can see record but can't edit
Solution:
- Check OWD is "Public Read Only"
- Grant Read/Write via sharing rule
- Or assign to user with edit access

Scenario 2: User can't see child records
Solution:
- Check Controlled By Parent setting
- Grant access to parent record
- Parent access automatically grants child access

Scenario 3: Trigger failing with insufficient access
Solution:
- Use "without sharing" for trigger helper class
- Or ensure trigger runs in system context
- Check if trigger needs to respect sharing

Scenario 4: User can't delete record they own
Solution:
- Check Delete permission on profile
- Verify no validation rules block deletion
- Check for related records preventing deletion

Scenario 5: API user gets access errors
Solution:
- Check API Enabled permission
- Verify profile has object access
- Check field-level security
- Use integration user profile

Sharing Debug Helper:

public class SharingDebugger {

    public static void debugSharing(Id recordId) {
        String objectType = String.valueOf(recordId.getSObjectType());
        String shareObjectName = objectType + 'Share';

        // Query sharing records
        String query = 'SELECT Id, UserOrGroupId, ' + objectType + 'AccessLevel, ' +
                      'RowCause FROM ' + shareObjectName + 
                      ' WHERE ' + objectType + 'Id = :recordId';

        List<SObject> shares = Database.query(query);

        System.debug('=== Sharing Debug for ' + recordId + ' ===');
        System.debug('Total sharing records: ' + shares.size());

        for (SObject share : shares) {
            String userOrGroupId = (String)share.get('UserOrGroupId');
            String accessLevel = (String)share.get(objectType + 'AccessLevel');
            String rowCause = (String)share.get('RowCause');

            System.debug('Shared with: ' + userOrGroupId + 
                        ' | Access: ' + accessLevel + 
                        ' | Reason: ' + rowCause);
        }
    }
}

Salesforce Edition Requirements:

  • ✅ Access debugging available in all editions
  • ✅ UserRecordAccess object available in Professional Edition and above
  • ✅ Advanced sharing features require Enterprise Edition and above

Best Practices:

  • ✅ Enable debug logs for users experiencing issues
  • ✅ Use "Login As" feature to reproduce user experience (with user permission)
  • ✅ Document permission requirements for custom processes
  • ✅ Test with users from different profiles
  • ✅ Check all security layers systematically
  • ✅ Use UserRecordAccess object to check record access
  • ✅ Review Setup Audit Trail for recent permission changes

Common Mistakes:

  • ❌ Only checking profile permissions (forgetting permission sets)
  • ❌ Not considering record-level security
  • ❌ Assuming role hierarchy always grants access
  • ❌ Forgetting about field-level security
  • ❌ Not testing with actual user accounts

See Also:

  • UserRecordAccess object (check record access)
  • System.runAs() method (test as different user)
  • Sharing Settings (review sharing configuration)
  • Security Health Check (identify permission issues)

docs.title: Q: How do I troubleshoot sharing rule performance issues?
docs.text:
A: Sharing rule performance issues typically manifest as slow record access, long-running sharing calculations, or timeouts during data loads. These issues often occur in orgs with large data volumes, complex sharing rules, or frequent ownership changes.

Common Performance Symptoms:

Performance Issues:
- Slow page loads
- Timeout errors during data import
- Long-running sharing recalculations
- "Unable to lock row" errors
- Slow queries on shared records
- Apex CPU time limit exceptions

Diagnostic Queries:

public class SharingPerformanceAnalyzer {

    public class PerformanceMetrics {
        public Integer totalSharingRules;
        public Integer criteriaBasedRules;
        public Integer ownerBasedRules;
        public Map<String, Integer> rulesByObject;
        public Long avgSharingRecords;
        public List<String> performanceIssues;
    }

    public static PerformanceMetrics analyzeSharingPerformance() {
        PerformanceMetrics metrics = new PerformanceMetrics();
        metrics.rulesByObject = new Map<String, Integer>();
        metrics.performanceIssues = new List<String>();

        // Note: Sharing rules are metadata, query approach is simplified
        // In practice, use Metadata API or Tooling API

        // Check Account sharing records
        Integer accountShares = [SELECT COUNT() FROM AccountShare];

        if (accountShares > 100000) {
            metrics.performanceIssues.add(
                'High number of Account sharing records: ' + accountShares
            );
        }

        // Check for deep role hierarchies
        Integer roleCount = [SELECT COUNT() FROM UserRole];
        if (roleCount > 500) {
            metrics.performanceIssues.add(
                'Large role hierarchy may impact performance: ' + roleCount + ' roles'
            );
        }

        return metrics;
    }

    // Find objects with most sharing records
    public static Map<String, Integer> getSharingRecordCounts() {
        Map<String, Integer> counts = new Map<String, Integer>();

        counts.put('Account', [SELECT COUNT() FROM AccountShare]);
        counts.put('Opportunity', [SELECT COUNT() FROM OpportunityShare]);
        counts.put('Case', [SELECT COUNT() FROM CaseShare]);
        counts.put('Contact', [SELECT COUNT() FROM ContactShare]);

        return counts;
    }

    // Identify slow sharing recalculations
    public static void identifySlowRecalculations() {
        // Query async apex jobs for sharing recalculations
        List<AsyncApexJob> jobs = [
            SELECT Id, Status, CreatedDate, CompletedDate, 
                   ExtendedStatus, ApexClass.Name
            FROM AsyncApexJob
            WHERE JobType = 'SharingRecalculation'
            AND CreatedDate = LAST_N_DAYS:7
            ORDER BY CreatedDate DESC
        ];

        for (AsyncApexJob job : jobs) {
            if (job.CompletedDate != null) {
                Long duration = job.CompletedDate.getTime() - 
                              job.CreatedDate.getTime();
                Long minutes = duration / (1000 * 60);

                if (minutes > 30) {
                    System.debug('Slow sharing recalculation: ' + 
                                minutes + ' minutes');
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

Performance Optimization Strategies:

Strategy 1: Optimize Criteria-Based Rules
- Use indexed fields in criteria
- Avoid formula fields in criteria
- Consolidate similar rules
- Use owner-based rules instead when possible

Strategy 2: Reduce Sharing Records
- Review and remove unnecessary sharing rules
- Use role hierarchy instead of sharing rules
- Consolidate groups used in sharing rules
- Remove manual sharing when no longer needed

Strategy 3: Optimize Role Hierarchy
- Keep hierarchy as flat as possible
- Limit to 500 roles or fewer
- Use territories for geographic structures

Strategy 4: Data Volume Management
- Archive old records
- Consider data retention policies
- Use separate objects for historical data

Optimizing Criteria-Based Rules:

// ❌ SLOW: Non-indexed field in criteria
// Rule criteria: Custom_Text_Field__c = 'Value'

// ✅ FASTER: Indexed field in criteria
// Rule criteria: Industry = 'Technology'

// ❌ SLOW: Formula field in criteria
// Rule criteria: Formula_Field__c > 100

// ✅ FASTER: Standard field in criteria
// Rule criteria: AnnualRevenue > 1000000

public class SharingRuleOptimizer {

    // Create indexed checkbox for sharing criteria
    public static void optimizeSharingCriteria() {
        // Instead of using complex formula or non-indexed fields
        // Create an indexed checkbox field that's set by workflow/process

        // Example: Create "High_Value_Account__c" checkbox
        // Update via Process Builder when AnnualRevenue > 1000000
        // Use checkbox in sharing rule criteria

        // This converts slow formula evaluation to fast indexed lookup
    }
}

Defer Sharing Calculation:

public class BulkDataLoader {

    // For large data loads, defer sharing calculation
    public static void loadDataWithDeferredSharing(List<Account> accounts) {
        // Suspend sharing calculation
        Database.setSavepoint();

        try {
            // Enable deferred sharing (admin must enable in setup first)
            // This prevents immediate sharing recalculation

            // Perform bulk insert
            Database.insert(accounts, false);

            // Sharing will recalculate asynchronously
            // Monitor in Setup → Sharing Settings → Recalculate Sharing

        } catch (Exception e) {
            System.debug('Load failed: ' + e.getMessage());
        }
    }

    // Manually trigger sharing recalculation
    public static void recalculateSharing(String objectName) {
        // Note: This is typically done through Setup UI
        // Setup → Security → Sharing Settings → [Object] → Recalculate

        // For Apex, you can update records to trigger recalculation
        // But this should be done carefully in batches
    }
}

Batch Sharing Recalculation:

public class SharingRecalculationBatch implements Database.Batchable<sObject> {

    private String objectName;
    private String whereClause;

    public SharingRecalculationBatch(String objectName, String whereClause) {
        this.objectName = objectName;
        this.whereClause = whereClause;
    }

    public Database.QueryLocator start(Database.BatchableContext bc) {
        String query = 'SELECT Id, OwnerId FROM ' + objectName;
        if (String.isNotBlank(whereClause)) {
            query += ' WHERE ' + whereClause;
        }
        return Database.getQueryLocator(query);
    }

    public void execute(Database.BatchableContext bc, List<sObject> scope) {
        // Force sharing recalculation by updating records
        // (update with same values triggers recalculation)

        List<sObject> toUpdate = new List<sObject>();
        for (sObject record : scope) {
            sObject updateRecord = record.getSObjectType().newSObject(record.Id);
            toUpdate.add(updateRecord);
        }

        if (!toUpdate.isEmpty()) {
            Database.update(toUpdate, false);
        }
    }

    public void finish(Database.BatchableContext bc) {
        System.debug('Sharing recalculation batch complete');
    }
}

Monitoring Sharing Performance:

public class SharingMonitor {

    public static void monitorSharingCalcJobs() {
        // Query sharing recalculation jobs
        List<AsyncApexJob> jobs = [
            SELECT Id, Status, NumberOfErrors, JobItemsProcessed,
                   TotalJobItems, CreatedDate, CompletedDate
            FROM AsyncApexJob
            WHERE JobType = 'SharingRecalculation'
            AND CreatedDate = TODAY
            ORDER BY CreatedDate DESC
        ];

        for (AsyncApexJob job : jobs) {
            System.debug('Sharing Job: ' + job.Status + 
                        ' | Processed: ' + job.JobItemsProcessed + '/' + job.TotalJobItems);

            if (job.Status == 'Failed' || job.NumberOfErrors > 0) {
                // Alert administrators
                sendAlert('Sharing calculation failed or has errors');
            }
        }
    }

    private static void sendAlert(String message) {
        System.debug('ALERT: ' + message);
        // Send email or create case for admin
    }
}

Troubleshooting Lock Errors:

public class LockErrorHandler {

    public static void handleRecordWithRetry(Id recordId) {
        Integer maxRetries = 3;
        Integer retryCount = 0;
        Boolean success = false;

        while (retryCount < maxRetries && !success) {
            try {
                // Attempt operation
                Account acc = new Account(Id = recordId, Name = 'Updated');
                update acc;
                success = true;

            } catch (DmlException e) {
                if (e.getMessage().contains('UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW')) {
                    retryCount++;

                    if (retryCount < maxRetries) {
                        // Wait before retry (simulated with sleep in tests)
                        System.debug('Lock error, retrying... Attempt ' + retryCount);
                    } else {
                        throw new LockException('Failed after ' + maxRetries + ' retries');
                    }
                } else {
                    throw e;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    public class LockException extends Exception {}
}

Performance Best Practices:

Sharing Rule Design:
✅ Use owner-based rules instead of criteria-based when possible
✅ Use indexed fields in criteria (standard fields, external IDs)
✅ Limit number of rules per object (under 50 recommended)
✅ Consolidate similar rules using public groups
✅ Avoid using formula fields in sharing criteria

Data Management:
✅ Archive old records that don't need active sharing
✅ Use separate objects for historical/archive data
✅ Implement data retention policies

Role Hierarchy:
✅ Keep hierarchy shallow (fewer levels = better performance)
✅ Keep hierarchy wide (more roles at same level)
✅ Limit total roles to under 500

Ownership Changes:
✅ Minimize frequent ownership transfers
✅ Batch ownership updates
✅ Schedule ownership updates during off-peak hours

Large Data Loads:
✅ Use deferred sharing calculation
✅ Load data in smaller batches
✅ Schedule loads during off-peak hours
✅ Consider parallel processing with care

Common Mistakes:

  • ❌ Using non-indexed fields in sharing rule criteria
  • ❌ Creating too many granular sharing rules
  • ❌ Deep role hierarchies (10+ levels)
  • ❌ Frequent ownership changes on records with many children
  • ❌ Not monitoring sharing calculation job completion
  • ❌ Loading large data volumes without deferring sharing

Salesforce Edition Requirements:

  • ✅ Deferred sharing calculation available in Enterprise Edition and above
  • ✅ Advanced sharing monitoring available with Event Monitoring

Governor Limits:

⚠️ Sharing calculations can take hours for large data volumes

⚠️ Maximum 300 sharing rules per object

⚠️ Lock errors more common during sharing recalculations

See Also:

  • Deferred Sharing Calculation (for data loads)
  • Territory Management (alternative to complex sharing)
  • Async Apex Jobs (monitor sharing recalculations)

Sample Exam Questions:

Question 1 (Administrator):
An organization has a Private OWD on Opportunities. Sales Managers need to 
view all opportunities for their team. What should you configure?

A) Create a sharing rule
B) Change OWD to Public Read Only
C) Assign managers to roles above sales reps
D) Grant View All permission

Answer: C
Explanation: Role hierarchy automatically grants access to records owned by 
subordinates when OWD is Private or Public Read Only.

---

Question 2 (Developer):
What happens when you use "with sharing" in an Apex class?

A) All SOQL queries are automatically filtered by sharing rules
B) The class respects the user's record-level access
C) Field-level security is automatically enforced
D) Object-level permissions are checked

Answer: B
Explanation: "with sharing" enforces record-level access based on user's 
sharing rules. FLS and object permissions must be checked explicitly.

---

Question 3 (Architect):
A financial services company needs to encrypt sensitive customer data at rest 
with customer-controlled keys. What should you recommend?

A) Classic Encryption
B) Shield Platform Encryption with BYOK
C) Field-level encryption in Apex
D) Database-level encryption

Answer: B
Explanation: Shield Platform Encryption with Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) 
allows customer control over encryption keys.
