docs.title: Q: When should I use Flow versus Apex for automation?
docs.text:
A: Choosing between Flow (declarative) and Apex (programmatic) depends on complexity, maintainability, and specific requirements. Modern Salesforce development emphasizes "clicks before code."

Use Flow When:

  • Simple to Moderate Logic: Standard automation patterns
  • No Code Required: Admins can maintain without developers
  • Screen Flows: Guided user interactions needed
  • Declarative Best Practices: Salesforce recommends Flow first
  • Rapid Development: Faster to build and deploy
  • Record-Triggered Actions: Before/after save logic
  • Schedule-Based Automation: Time-based processes

Use Apex When:

  • Complex Business Logic: Advanced algorithms or calculations
  • Bulk Processing: Large data volumes (10,000+ records)
  • Governor Limit Optimization: Need fine-grained control
  • External Integration: Complex API calls with error handling
  • Dynamic SOQL: Query logic determined at runtime
  • Recursion Control: Complex trigger patterns
  • Performance Critical: CPU-intensive operations
  • Third-Party Libraries: Need to use external code

Flow Capabilities & Limitations:

Capabilities:

  • Record-triggered flows (before/after save)
  • Screen flows for user input
  • Autolaunched flows for background processing
  • Scheduled flows for time-based automation
  • Platform Events integration
  • Apex Actions can be called from Flow
  • Subflows for reusability

Limitations:

⚠️ SOQL Queries: 100 per flow interview (same as Apex)

⚠️ DML Statements: 150 per flow interview

⚠️ CPU Time: 10 seconds (same as Apex)

⚠️ Bulkification: Automatic but less control than Apex

⚠️ Complex Logic: Can become hard to maintain

⚠️ Debugging: More difficult than Apex debug logs

Example: Flow vs Apex Decision

Scenario: Update Account Rating Based on Opportunity Amount

Flow Solution (Recommended for this scenario):

Record-Triggered Flow on Opportunity (After Save)
├── Get Records: Query related Account
├── Decision: Check total Opportunity amount
│   ├── If Total > $1M: Set Rating = "Hot"
│   ├── If Total > $500K: Set Rating = "Warm"
│   └── Else: Set Rating = "Cold"
└── Update Records: Update Account with new rating

Apex Solution (For complex scenarios):

trigger OpportunityTrigger on Opportunity (after insert, after update) {
    OpportunityTriggerHandler.updateAccountRatings(Trigger.new, Trigger.oldMap);
}

public class OpportunityTriggerHandler {

    public static void updateAccountRatings(
        List<Opportunity> newOpps, 
        Map<Id, Opportunity> oldMap
    ) {
        // Collect Account IDs
        Set<Id> accountIds = new Set<Id>();
        for (Opportunity opp : newOpps) {
            if (opp.AccountId != null) {
                // Only process if amount changed or new opportunity
                if (oldMap == null || 
                    opp.Amount != oldMap.get(opp.Id).Amount) {
                    accountIds.add(opp.AccountId);
                }
            }
        }

        if (accountIds.isEmpty()) return;

        // Aggregate opportunity amounts by account
        Map<Id, Decimal> accountTotals = new Map<Id, Decimal>();
        for (AggregateResult ar : [
            SELECT AccountId, SUM(Amount) totalAmount
            FROM Opportunity
            WHERE AccountId IN :accountIds
            AND StageName != 'Closed Lost'
            GROUP BY AccountId
        ]) {
            accountTotals.put(
                (Id)ar.get('AccountId'), 
                (Decimal)ar.get('totalAmount')
            );
        }

        // Update accounts
        List<Account> accountsToUpdate = new List<Account>();
        for (Id accId : accountIds) {
            Decimal total = accountTotals.get(accId);
            if (total != null) {
                Account acc = new Account(Id = accId);
                if (total > 1000000) {
                    acc.Rating = 'Hot';
                } else if (total > 500000) {
                    acc.Rating = 'Warm';
                } else {
                    acc.Rating = 'Cold';
                }
                accountsToUpdate.add(acc);
            }
        }

        if (!accountsToUpdate.isEmpty()) {
            update accountsToUpdate;
        }
    }
}

Hybrid Approach (Best Practice):

// Apex Action called from Flow
public class FlowAccountActions {

    @InvocableMethod(
        label='Calculate Account Score' 
        description='Complex scoring logic for accounts'
    )
    public static List<Result> calculateAccountScore(List<Request> requests) {
        List<Result> results = new List<Result>();

        for (Request req : requests) {
            Result result = new Result();
            result.score = performComplexCalculation(
                req.accountId, 
                req.industry, 
                req.revenue
            );
            results.add(result);
        }

        return results;
    }

    private static Decimal performComplexCalculation(
        Id accountId, 
        String industry, 
        Decimal revenue
    ) {
        // Complex algorithm that would be difficult in Flow
        Decimal score = 0;

        // Industry multiplier
        Map<String, Decimal> industryWeights = new Map<String, Decimal>{
            'Technology' => 1.5,
            'Healthcare' => 1.3,
            'Finance' => 1.4,
            'Manufacturing' => 1.1
        };

        Decimal baseScore = revenue / 100000;
        Decimal multiplier = industryWeights.get(industry) != null ? 
                            industryWeights.get(industry) : 1.0;

        score = baseScore * multiplier;

        // Additional complex logic...

        return score;
    }

    public class Request {
        @InvocableVariable(required=true)
        public Id accountId;

        @InvocableVariable
        public String industry;

        @InvocableVariable
        public Decimal revenue;
    }

    public class Result {
        @InvocableVariable
        public Decimal score;
    }
}

Decision Framework:

Criteria Flow Apex Complexity Simple to Moderate Moderate to Complex Maintenance Admin-maintainable Developer-required Performance Good for <2000 records Optimized for bulk Debugging Flow logs, harder Debug logs, easier Testing Manual testing Automated test classes Version Control Metadata deployment Git/version control Reusability Subflows Classes/methods

Best Practices by Role:

For Administrators:

✅ Start with Flow for most automation

✅ Use Apex Actions when needed

✅ Document complex flows thoroughly

✅ Test flows with realistic data volumes

For Developers:

✅ Provide Invocable Apex Actions for admins

✅ Use Apex for bulk operations

✅ Implement proper trigger frameworks

✅ Write comprehensive test coverage

For Architects:

✅ Define automation strategy (Flow-first approach)

✅ Establish governance for when to use Apex

✅ Design for scalability from the start

✅ Plan for hybrid Flow + Apex solutions

Salesforce Recommendations:

✅ Flow First: Use Flow unless Apex is required

✅ Deprecation: Workflow Rules and Process Builder (use Flow)

✅ Migration: Migrate legacy automation to Flow

✅ Future-Proof: Flow receives the most investment from Salesforce

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Q: What is the proper way to bulkify Apex code?
docs.text:
A: Bulkification is the practice of writing Apex code that efficiently handles multiple records in a single transaction. This is essential for avoiding governor limits and ensuring optimal performance.

Why Bulkification Matters:

  • Salesforce processes records in batches (up to 200 per transaction)
  • Triggers must handle multiple records efficiently
  • Governor limits apply per transaction, not per record
  • Poor bulkification leads to limit exceptions in production

Common Bulkification Mistakes:

❌ WRONG: SOQL Inside Loop

trigger ContactTrigger on Contact (after insert) {
    for (Contact con : Trigger.new) {
        // ANTI-PATTERN: SOQL query inside loop
        Account acc = [SELECT Id, Name FROM Account WHERE Id = :con.AccountId];
        System.debug('Account: ' + acc.Name);
    }
}
// Problem: Hits 100 SOQL limit with only 100 contacts

✅ CORRECT: Query Outside Loop

trigger ContactTrigger on Contact (after insert) {
    // Collect all Account IDs first
    Set<Id> accountIds = new Set<Id>();
    for (Contact con : Trigger.new) {
        if (con.AccountId != null) {
            accountIds.add(con.AccountId);
        }
    }

    // Single SOQL query for all accounts
    Map<Id, Account> accountMap = new Map<Id, Account>(
        [SELECT Id, Name FROM Account WHERE Id IN :accountIds]
    );

    // Use the map in the loop
    for (Contact con : Trigger.new) {
        if (con.AccountId != null) {
            Account acc = accountMap.get(con.AccountId);
            System.debug('Account: ' + acc.Name);
        }
    }
}
// Benefit: Only 1 SOQL query regardless of record count

❌ WRONG: DML Inside Loop

trigger OpportunityTrigger on Opportunity (after insert) {
    for (Opportunity opp : Trigger.new) {
        // ANTI-PATTERN: DML inside loop
        Task t = new Task(
            Subject = 'Follow up on opportunity',
            WhatId = opp.Id
        );
        insert t; // Separate DML for each record
    }
}
// Problem: Hits 150 DML limit with only 150 opportunities

✅ CORRECT: Bulk DML

trigger OpportunityTrigger on Opportunity (after insert) {
    List<Task> tasksToInsert = new List<Task>();

    for (Opportunity opp : Trigger.new) {
        Task t = new Task(
            Subject = 'Follow up on opportunity',
            WhatId = opp.Id,
            ActivityDate = Date.today().addDays(7)
        );
        tasksToInsert.add(t);
    }

    // Single DML operation for all tasks
    if (!tasksToInsert.isEmpty()) {
        insert tasksToInsert;
    }
}
// Benefit: Only 1 DML statement regardless of record count

Complete Bulkification Pattern:

trigger AccountTrigger on Account (after insert, after update) {
    AccountTriggerHandler.createHighValueAccountTasks(Trigger.new, Trigger.oldMap);
}

public class AccountTriggerHandler {

    public static void createHighValueAccountTasks(
        List<Account> newAccounts,
        Map<Id, Account> oldAccountMap
    ) {
        // Step 1: Collect Account IDs that meet criteria
        Set<Id> highValueAccountIds = new Set<Id>();

        for (Account acc : newAccounts) {
            // Check if revenue threshold crossed
            Boolean isNew = (oldAccountMap == null);
            Boolean revenueCrossedThreshold = false;

            if (!isNew) {
                Account oldAcc = oldAccountMap.get(acc.Id);
                revenueCrossedThreshold = (
                    acc.AnnualRevenue >= 1000000 && 
                    (oldAcc.AnnualRevenue == null || oldAcc.AnnualRevenue < 1000000)
                );
            } else if (acc.AnnualRevenue >= 1000000) {
                revenueCrossedThreshold = true;
            }

            if (revenueCrossedThreshold) {
                highValueAccountIds.add(acc.Id);
            }
        }

        if (highValueAccountIds.isEmpty()) {
            return; // Early exit if no work to do
        }

        // Step 2: Query related data (if needed)
        Map<Id, Account> accountsWithContacts = new Map<Id, Account>(
            [SELECT Id, Name, OwnerId,
                    (SELECT Id, Name, Email FROM Contacts WHERE Email != null LIMIT 5)
             FROM Account 
             WHERE Id IN :highValueAccountIds]
        );

        // Step 3: Query existing tasks to avoid duplicates
        Set<Id> accountsWithExistingTasks = new Set<Id>();
        for (Task existingTask : [
            SELECT WhatId 
            FROM Task 
            WHERE WhatId IN :highValueAccountIds 
            AND Subject = 'Review high-value account'
            AND CreatedDate = TODAY
        ]) {
            accountsWithExistingTasks.add(existingTask.WhatId);
        }

        // Step 4: Build records to insert
        List<Task> tasksToInsert = new List<Task>();
        List<ContentVersion> documentsToCreate = new List<ContentVersion>();

        for (Id accountId : highValueAccountIds) {
            // Skip if task already exists
            if (accountsWithExistingTasks.contains(accountId)) {
                continue;
            }

            Account acc = accountsWithContacts.get(accountId);

            // Create task
            Task t = new Task(
                Subject = 'Review high-value account',
                WhatId = accountId,
                OwnerId = acc.OwnerId,
                ActivityDate = Date.today().addDays(1),
                Priority = 'High',
                Status = 'Not Started',
                Description = 'Account revenue crossed $1M threshold. Review and update strategy.'
            );
            tasksToInsert.add(t);
        }

        // Step 5: Perform DML operations
        if (!tasksToInsert.isEmpty()) {
            insert tasksToInsert;
        }

        // Step 6: Handle errors gracefully
        if (!documentsToCreate.isEmpty()) {
            Database.SaveResult[] results = Database.insert(documentsToCreate, false);

            for (Integer i = 0; i < results.size(); i++) {
                if (!results[i].isSuccess()) {
                    System.debug('Error creating document: ' + results[i].getErrors());
                    // Log error to custom object or send email notification
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

Advanced Bulkification: Collection Processing

public class BulkificationExamples {

    // Pattern 1: Using Maps for O(1) lookup
    public static Map<Id, Contact> getContactsByAccountId(Set<Id> accountIds) {
        Map<Id, List<Contact>> contactsByAccount = new Map<Id, List<Contact>>();

        for (Contact con : [
            SELECT Id, FirstName, LastName, Email, AccountId
            FROM Contact
            WHERE AccountId IN :accountIds
        ]) {
            if (!contactsByAccount.containsKey(con.AccountId)) {
                contactsByAccount.put(con.AccountId, new List<Contact>());
            }
            contactsByAccount.get(con.AccountId).add(con);
        }

        return contactsByAccount;
    }

    // Pattern 2: Aggregate queries for efficiency
    public static Map<Id, Decimal> getTotalOpportunityAmountsByAccount(Set<Id> accountIds) {
        Map<Id, Decimal> totals = new Map<Id, Decimal>();

        for (AggregateResult ar : [
            SELECT AccountId, SUM(Amount) totalAmount
            FROM Opportunity
            WHERE AccountId IN :accountIds
            AND StageName != 'Closed Lost'
            GROUP BY AccountId
        ]) {
            totals.put(
                (Id)ar.get('AccountId'),
                (Decimal)ar.get('totalAmount')
            );
        }

        return totals;
    }

    // Pattern 3: Set operations for filtering
    public static Set<Id> getActiveAccountIds(List<Account> accounts) {
        Set<Id> activeIds = new Set<Id>();

        for (Account acc : accounts) {
            if (acc.Active__c == 'Yes') {
                activeIds.add(acc.Id);
            }
        }

        return activeIds;
    }
}

Testing Bulkification:

@isTest
private class AccountTriggerHandlerTest {

    @isTest
    static void testBulkAccountInsert() {
        // Test with 200 records (trigger batch size)
        List<Account> accounts = new List<Account>();

        for (Integer i = 0; i < 200; i++) {
            accounts.add(new Account(
                Name = 'Test Account ' + i,
                AnnualRevenue = 1500000
            ));
        }

        Test.startTest();
        insert accounts;
        Test.stopTest();

        // Verify tasks created
        List<Task> tasks = [
            SELECT Id, WhatId 
            FROM Task 
            WHERE Subject = 'Review high-value account'
        ];

        System.assertEquals(200, tasks.size(), 
            'Should create one task per account');

        // Verify no governor limit issues
        System.debug('SOQL Queries Used: ' + Limits.getQueries() + '/' + Limits.getLimitQueries());
        System.debug('DML Statements Used: ' + Limits.getDmlStatements() + '/' + Limits.getLimitDmlStatements());
    }

    @isTest
    static void testPerformanceWithLargeDataset() {
        // Create 200 accounts with related data
        List<Account> accounts = TestDataFactory.createAccounts(200, true);

        Test.startTest();

        // Simulate bulk update
        for (Account acc : accounts) {
            acc.AnnualRevenue = 2000000;
        }
        update accounts;

        Test.stopTest();

        // Performance assertions
        System.assert(Limits.getQueries() < 10, 
            'Should use less than 10 SOQL queries');
        System.assert(Limits.getDmlStatements() < 5, 
            'Should use less than 5 DML statements');
    }
}

Governor Limits to Remember:

⚠️ SOQL Queries: 100 per transaction

⚠️ SOQL Query Rows: 50,000 per transaction

⚠️ DML Statements: 150 per transaction

⚠️ DML Rows: 10,000 per transaction

⚠️ Heap Size: 6 MB (synchronous), 12 MB (asynchronous)

⚠️ CPU Time: 10 seconds (synchronous), 60 seconds (asynchronous)

Best Practices Checklist:

✅ Never put SOQL queries inside loops

✅ Never put DML statements inside loops

✅ Use collections (Sets, Maps, Lists) efficiently

✅ Query only the fields you need

✅ Use aggregate queries when possible

✅ Test with 200+ records

✅ Monitor governor limits in test classes

✅ Use asynchronous processing for large volumes

✅ Implement proper error handling

✅ Document complex bulkification logic

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Q: What is the recommended Apex Trigger Framework pattern?
docs.text:
A: Implementing a proper trigger framework is essential for maintainability, testing, and avoiding common pitfalls like recursion. The recommended pattern separates concerns and provides a clear structure.

Trigger Framework Components:

1. Trigger (One Per Object):

trigger AccountTrigger on Account (
    before insert, before update, before delete,
    after insert, after update, after delete, after undelete
) {
    new AccountTriggerHandler().run();
}

2. TriggerHandler Base Class:

public virtual class TriggerHandler {

    // Static map to prevent recursion
    private static Map<String, LoopCount> loopCountMap;
    private static Set<String> bypassedHandlers;

    static {
        loopCountMap = new Map<String, LoopCount>();
        bypassedHandlers = new Set<String>();
    }

    // Constructor
    public TriggerHandler() {
        this.setMaxLoopCount(5); // Default max iterations
    }

    // Main execution method
    public void run() {

        // Check if handler is bypassed
        if (bypassedHandlers.contains(getHandlerName())) {
            return;
        }

        // Check for recursive calls
        if (!validateRun()) {
            return;
        }

        addToLoopCount();

        // Route to appropriate method based on context
        if (Trigger.isBefore) {
            if (Trigger.isInsert) {
                this.beforeInsert();
            } else if (Trigger.isUpdate) {
                this.beforeUpdate();
            } else if (Trigger.isDelete) {
                this.beforeDelete();
            }
        } else if (Trigger.isAfter) {
            if (Trigger.isInsert) {
                this.afterInsert();
            } else if (Trigger.isUpdate) {
                this.afterUpdate();
            } else if (Trigger.isDelete) {
                this.afterDelete();
            } else if (Trigger.isUndelete) {
                this.afterUndelete();
            }
        }
    }

    // Virtual methods to be overridden
    protected virtual void beforeInsert() {}
    protected virtual void beforeUpdate() {}
    protected virtual void beforeDelete() {}
    protected virtual void afterInsert() {}
    protected virtual void afterUpdate() {}
    protected virtual void afterDelete() {}
    protected virtual void afterUndelete() {}

    // Recursion prevention
    private Boolean validateRun() {
        if (!loopCountMap.containsKey(getHandlerName())) {
            loopCountMap.put(getHandlerName(), new LoopCount());
        }

        LoopCount lc = loopCountMap.get(getHandlerName());

        if (lc.max < 0) return true;

        if (lc.count >= lc.max) {
            String errorMessage = 'Maximum loop count of ' + 
                String.valueOf(lc.max) + ' reached in ' + getHandlerName();
            throw new TriggerHandlerException(errorMessage);
        }

        return true;
    }

    private void addToLoopCount() {
        loopCountMap.get(getHandlerName()).increment();
    }

    public void setMaxLoopCount(Integer max) {
        if (!loopCountMap.containsKey(getHandlerName())) {
            loopCountMap.put(getHandlerName(), new LoopCount(max));
        } else {
            loopCountMap.get(getHandlerName()).max = max;
        }
    }

    public void clearMaxLoopCount() {
        this.setMaxLoopCount(-1);
    }

    public static void bypass(String handlerName) {
        bypassedHandlers.add(handlerName);
    }

    public static void clearBypass(String handlerName) {
        bypassedHandlers.remove(handlerName);
    }

    public static void clearAllBypasses() {
        bypassedHandlers.clear();
    }

    private String getHandlerName() {
        return String.valueOf(this).substring(0, String.valueOf(this).indexOf(':'));
    }

    // Inner class for loop counting
    private class LoopCount {
        private Integer max;
        private Integer count;

        public LoopCount() {
            this(5);
        }

        public LoopCount(Integer max) {
            this.max = max;
            this.count = 0;
        }

        public void increment() {
            this.count++;
        }
    }

    public class TriggerHandlerException extends Exception {}
}

3. Object-Specific Handler:

public class AccountTriggerHandler extends TriggerHandler {

    private List<Account> newAccounts;
    private List<Account> oldAccounts;
    private Map<Id, Account> newAccountMap;
    private Map<Id, Account> oldAccountMap;

    public AccountTriggerHandler() {
        super();
        this.newAccounts = (List<Account>) Trigger.new;
        this.oldAccounts = (List<Account>) Trigger.old;
        this.newAccountMap = (Map<Id, Account>) Trigger.newMap;
        this.oldAccountMap = (Map<Id, Account>) Trigger.oldMap;
    }

    protected override void beforeInsert() {
        AccountTriggerHelper.setDefaultValues(this.newAccounts);
        AccountTriggerHelper.validateIndustry(this.newAccounts);
    }

    protected override void beforeUpdate() {
        AccountTriggerHelper.preventRatingDecrease(this.newAccounts, this.oldAccountMap);
        AccountTriggerHelper.updateModifiedFields(this.newAccounts, this.oldAccountMap);
    }

    protected override void afterInsert() {
        AccountTriggerHelper.createWelcomeTask(this.newAccounts);
        AccountTriggerHelper.sendNotificationToOwner(this.newAccounts);
    }

    protected override void afterUpdate() {
        AccountTriggerHelper.updateRelatedContacts(this.newAccounts, this.oldAccountMap);
        AccountTriggerHelper.logSignificantChanges(this.newAccounts, this.oldAccountMap);
    }

    protected override void afterDelete() {
        AccountTriggerHelper.archiveDeletedAccounts(this.oldAccounts);
    }
}

4. Helper Class (Business Logic):

public class AccountTriggerHelper {

    // Before Insert Logic
    public static void setDefaultValues(List<Account> accounts) {
        for (Account acc : accounts) {
            if (String.isBlank(acc.Industry)) {
                acc.Industry = 'Other';
            }
            if (String.isBlank(acc.Type)) {
                acc.Type = 'Prospect';
            }
        }
    }

    public static void validateIndustry(List<Account> accounts) {
        Set<String> validIndustries = new Set<String>{
            'Technology', 'Healthcare', 'Finance', 'Manufacturing', 'Retail', 'Other'
        };

        for (Account acc : accounts) {
            if (!validIndustries.contains(acc.Industry)) {
                acc.Industry.addError('Please select a valid industry');
            }
        }
    }

    // Before Update Logic
    public static void preventRatingDecrease(
        List<Account> newAccounts, 
        Map<Id, Account> oldAccountMap
    ) {
        for (Account acc : newAccounts) {
            Account oldAcc = oldAccountMap.get(acc.Id);

            if (oldAcc.Rating == 'Hot' && acc.Rating != 'Hot') {
                acc.Rating.addError('Cannot decrease rating from Hot. Please contact manager.');
            }
        }
    }

    public static void updateModifiedFields(
        List<Account> newAccounts,
        Map<Id, Account> oldAccountMap
    ) {
        for (Account acc : newAccounts) {
            Account oldAcc = oldAccountMap.get(acc.Id);

            // Track significant changes
            if (acc.AnnualRevenue != oldAcc.AnnualRevenue ||
                acc.Industry != oldAcc.Industry) {
                acc.Last_Significant_Change__c = System.now();
            }
        }
    }

    // After Insert Logic
    public static void createWelcomeTask(List<Account> accounts) {
        List<Task> tasksToInsert = new List<Task>();

        for (Account acc : accounts) {
            Task t = new Task(
                Subject = 'Welcome new account: ' + acc.Name,
                WhatId = acc.Id,
                OwnerId = acc.OwnerId,
                ActivityDate = Date.today().addDays(1),
                Priority = 'Normal',
                Status = 'Not Started'
            );
            tasksToInsert.add(t);
        }

        if (!tasksToInsert.isEmpty()) {
            insert tasksToInsert;
        }
    }

    public static void sendNotificationToOwner(List<Account> accounts) {
        Set<Id> ownerIds = new Set<Id>();
        for (Account acc : accounts) {
            ownerIds.add(acc.OwnerId);
        }

        Map<Id, User> owners = new Map<Id, User>(
            [SELECT Id, Email FROM User WHERE Id IN :ownerIds]
        );

        List<Messaging.SingleEmailMessage> emails = new List<Messaging.SingleEmailMessage>();

        for (Account acc : accounts) {
            User owner = owners.get(acc.OwnerId);
            if (owner != null && owner.Email != null) {
                Messaging.SingleEmailMessage email = new Messaging.SingleEmailMessage();
                email.setToAddresses(new List<String>{ owner.Email });
                email.setSubject('New Account Assigned: ' + acc.Name);
                email.setPlainTextBody(
                    'A new account has been assigned to you:\n\n' +
                    'Account Name: ' + acc.Name + '\n' +
                    'Industry: ' + acc.Industry + '\n\n' +
                    'Please review and take appropriate action.'
                );
                emails.add(email);
            }
        }

        if (!emails.isEmpty()) {
            Messaging.sendEmail(emails);
        }
    }

    // After Update Logic
    public static void updateRelatedContacts(
        List<Account> newAccounts,
        Map<Id, Account> oldAccountMap
    ) {
        Set<Id> accountsWithBillingChanges = new Set<Id>();

        for (Account acc : newAccounts) {
            Account oldAcc = oldAccountMap.get(acc.Id);

            if (acc.BillingCity != oldAcc.BillingCity ||
                acc.BillingState != oldAcc.BillingState) {
                accountsWithBillingChanges.add(acc.Id);
            }
        }

        if (accountsWithBillingChanges.isEmpty()) return;

        List<Contact> contactsToUpdate = [
            SELECT Id, AccountId, MailingCity, MailingState
            FROM Contact
            WHERE AccountId IN :accountsWithBillingChanges
            AND Sync_Address_With_Account__c = true
        ];

        Map<Id, Account> accountMap = new Map<Id, Account>(
            [SELECT Id, BillingCity, BillingState 
             FROM Account 
             WHERE Id IN :accountsWithBillingChanges]
        );

        for (Contact con : contactsToUpdate) {
            Account acc = accountMap.get(con.AccountId);
            con.MailingCity = acc.BillingCity;
            con.MailingState = acc.BillingState;
        }

        if (!contactsToUpdate.isEmpty()) {
            update contactsToUpdate;
        }
    }

    public static void logSignificantChanges(
        List<Account> newAccounts,
        Map<Id, Account> oldAccountMap
    ) {
        List<Account_Change_Log__c> logsToInsert = new List<Account_Change_Log__c>();

        for (Account acc : newAccounts) {
            Account oldAcc = oldAccountMap.get(acc.Id);

            if (acc.AnnualRevenue != oldAcc.AnnualRevenue) {
                logsToInsert.add(new Account_Change_Log__c(
                    Account__c = acc.Id,
                    Field_Changed__c = 'AnnualRevenue',
                    Old_Value__c = String.valueOf(oldAcc.AnnualRevenue),
                    New_Value__c = String.valueOf(acc.AnnualRevenue),
                    Changed_By__c = UserInfo.getUserId(),
                    Change_Date__c = System.now()
                ));
            }
        }

        if (!logsToInsert.isEmpty()) {
            insert logsToInsert;
        }
    }

    // After Delete Logic
    public static void archiveDeletedAccounts(List<Account> deletedAccounts) {
        List<Deleted_Account_Archive__c> archiveRecords = new List<Deleted_Account_Archive__c>();

        for (Account acc : deletedAccounts) {
            archiveRecords.add(new Deleted_Account_Archive__c(
                Account_Name__c = acc.Name,
                Industry__c = acc.Industry,
                Annual_Revenue__c = acc.AnnualRevenue,
                Deleted_Date__c = System.now(),
                Deleted_By__c = UserInfo.getUserId()
            ));
        }

        if (!archiveRecords.isEmpty()) {
            insert archiveRecords;
        }
    }
}

5. Test Class:

@isTest
private class AccountTriggerHandlerTest {

    @TestSetup
    static void setupTestData() {
        List<Account> accounts = new List<Account>();
        for (Integer i = 0; i < 200; i++) {
            accounts.add(new Account(
                Name = 'Test Account ' + i,
                Industry = 'Technology',
                AnnualRevenue = 500000
            ));
        }
        insert accounts;
    }

    @isTest
    static void testBeforeInsertDefaultValues() {
        Test.startTest();
        Account acc = new Account(Name = 'Test Account');
        insert acc;
        Test.stopTest();

        acc = [SELECT Industry, Type FROM Account WHERE Id = :acc.Id];
        System.assertEquals('Other', acc.Industry);
        System.assertEquals('Prospect', acc.Type);
    }

    @isTest
    static void testAfterInsertTaskCreation() {
        Integer initialTaskCount = [SELECT COUNT() FROM Task];

        Test.startTest();
        insert new Account(Name = 'Test Account', Industry = 'Technology');
        Test.stopTest();

        Integer finalTaskCount = [SELECT COUNT() FROM Task];
        System.assertEquals(initialTaskCount + 1, finalTaskCount);
    }

    @isTest
    static void testBulkInsert() {
        List<Account> newAccounts = new List<Account>();
        for (Integer i = 0; i < 200; i++) {
            newAccounts.add(new Account(
                Name = 'Bulk Test ' + i,
                Industry = 'Finance'
            ));
        }

        Test.startTest();
        insert newAccounts;
        Test.stopTest();

        System.assertEquals(200, [SELECT COUNT() FROM Task WHERE Subject LIKE 'Welcome new account%']);
    }

    @isTest
    static void testRecursionPrevention() {
        Account acc = [SELECT Id FROM Account LIMIT 1];

        // Set max loop count to 2
        AccountTriggerHandler handler = new AccountTriggerHandler();
        handler.setMaxLoopCount(2);

        Test.startTest();

        // This should work (first update)
        acc.Industry = 'Healthcare';
        update acc;

        // This should work (second update)
        acc.Industry = 'Finance';
        update acc;

        // This should fail (third update exceeds limit)
        try {
            acc.Industry = 'Technology';
            update acc;
            System.assert(false, 'Should have thrown exception');
        } catch (Exception e) {
            System.assert(e.getMessage().contains('Maximum loop count'));
        }

        Test.stopTest();
    }

    @isTest
    static void testBypassMechanism() {
        Account acc = [SELECT Id, Name FROM Account LIMIT 1];

        Test.startTest();

        // Bypass the handler
        TriggerHandler.bypass('AccountTriggerHandler');

        acc.Industry = 'Technology';
        update acc;

        // No tasks should be created because handler is bypassed
        Integer taskCount = [SELECT COUNT() FROM Task 
                            WHERE WhatId = :acc.Id 
                            AND CreatedDate = TODAY];
        System.assertEquals(0, taskCount);

        // Clear bypass
        TriggerHandler.clearBypass('AccountTriggerHandler');

        Test.stopTest();
    }
}

Benefits of This Framework:

✅ Separation of Concerns: Logic organized by context and functionality

✅ Recursion Prevention: Built-in protection against infinite loops

✅ Bypass Mechanism: Ability to disable triggers during data loads

✅ Testability: Easy to test individual methods

✅ Maintainability: Clear structure for adding new logic

✅ Bulkification: Framework enforces bulk patterns

✅ Governor Limit Safety: Single point to monitor limits

Alternative: Lightweight Framework

For simpler needs, a lightweight version:

trigger AccountTrigger on Account (before insert, before update, after insert, after update) {
    if (Trigger.isBefore) {
        if (Trigger.isInsert) {
            AccountTriggerHelper.beforeInsert(Trigger.new);
        }
        if (Trigger.isUpdate) {
            AccountTriggerHelper.beforeUpdate(Trigger.new, Trigger.oldMap);
        }
    }
    if (Trigger.isAfter) {
        if (Trigger.isInsert) {
            AccountTriggerHelper.afterInsert(Trigger.new);
        }
        if (Trigger.isUpdate) {
            AccountTriggerHelper.afterUpdate(Trigger.new, Trigger.oldMap);
        }
    }
}

Best Practices:

✅ One trigger per object

✅ Use a framework for consistency

✅ Implement recursion prevention

✅ Test with 200+ records

✅ Monitor CPU time and DML limits

✅ Document complex logic

✅ Use helper classes for business logic

✅ Implement bypass for data migrations

docs.title: Q: What are Lightning Web Components (LWC) and how do they compare to Aura Components?
docs.text:
A: Lightning Web Components (LWC) is Salesforce's modern programming model for building user interfaces using standard web technologies. It represents the future of Salesforce UI development, superseding Aura Components.

What is LWC:

  • Standard-Based: Built on Web Components standards (Custom Elements, Shadow DOM, ES Modules)
  • Performance: Faster rendering and smaller bundle sizes
  • Modern JavaScript: Uses ES6+ features (classes, modules, promises, async/await)
  • Interoperable: Can coexist with Aura components on the same page
  • Salesforce Integration: Access to platform features via decorators

LWC vs Aura Components:

Feature LWC Aura Standard Web Standards Proprietary Performance Faster (50%+) Slower Learning Curve Easier (standard JS) Steeper Bundle Size Smaller Larger Browser Support Modern browsers Broader support Future Actively developed Maintenance mode Syntax Clean, minimal Verbose Security Shadow DOM isolation Locker Service

Basic LWC Component Structure:

helloWorld.html:

<template>
    <lightning-card title="Hello World" icon-name="custom:custom14">
        <div class="slds-m-around_medium">
            <p>Hello, {greeting}!</p>
            <lightning-input 
                label="Enter your name" 
                value={greeting} 
                onchange={handleChange}>
            </lightning-input>
        </div>
    </lightning-card>
</template>

helloWorld.js:

import { LightningElement, track } from 'lwc';

export default class HelloWorld extends LightningElement {
    @track greeting = 'World';

    handleChange(event) {
        this.greeting = event.target.value;
    }
}

helloWorld.js-meta.xml:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<LightningComponentBundle xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata">
    <apiVersion>59.0</apiVersion>
    <isExposed>true</isExposed>
    <targets>
        <target>lightning__AppPage</target>
        <target>lightning__RecordPage</target>
        <target>lightning__HomePage</target>
    </targets>
</LightningComponentBundle>

Advanced LWC Example: Account Search with Apex

accountSearch.html:

<template>
    <lightning-card title="Account Search" icon-name="standard:account">
        <div class="slds-m-around_medium">
            <!-- Search Input -->
            <lightning-input
                type="search"
                label="Search Accounts"
                value={searchTerm}
                onchange={handleSearchChange}>
            </lightning-input>

            <!-- Loading Spinner -->
            <template if:true={isLoading}>
                <lightning-spinner alternative-text="Loading" size="small"></lightning-spinner>
            </template>

            <!-- Error Message -->
            <template if:true={error}>
                <div class="slds-m-top_small">
                    <p class="slds-text-color_error">{error}</p>
                </div>
            </template>

            <!-- Results -->
            <template if:true={accounts}>
                <div class="slds-m-top_medium">
                    <template if:true={hasAccounts}>
                        <template for:each={accounts} for:item="account">
                            <div key={account.Id} class="slds-box slds-m-bottom_small">
                                <div class="slds-grid slds-gutters">
                                    <div class="slds-col slds-size_3-of-4">
                                        <p class="slds-text-heading_small">
                                            <a onclick={handleAccountClick} 
                                               data-id={account.Id}>
                                                {account.Name}
                                            </a>
                                        </p>
                                        <p class="slds-text-body_small slds-text-color_weak">
                                            {account.Industry} • {account.BillingCity}
                                        </p>
                                    </div>
                                    <div class="slds-col slds-size_1-of-4 slds-text-align_right">
                                        <lightning-formatted-number
                                            value={account.AnnualRevenue}
                                            format-style="currency"
                                            currency-code="USD">
                                        </lightning-formatted-number>
                                    </div>
                                </div>
                            </div>
                        </template>
                    </template>
                    <template if:false={hasAccounts}>
                        <p class="slds-text-align_center slds-m-top_medium">
                            No accounts found
                        </p>
                    </template>
                </div>
            </template>
        </div>
    </lightning-card>
</template>

accountSearch.js:

import { LightningElement, wire, track } from 'lwc';
import { NavigationMixin } from 'lightning/navigation';
import searchAccounts from '@salesforce/apex/AccountController.searchAccounts';
import { ShowToastEvent } from 'lightning/platformShowToastEvent';

export default class AccountSearch extends NavigationMixin(LightningElement) {
    @track searchTerm = '';
    @track accounts = [];
    @track error;
    @track isLoading = false;

    // Debounce timeout
    searchTimeout;

    // Getter for checking if accounts exist
    get hasAccounts() {
        return this.accounts && this.accounts.length > 0;
    }

    handleSearchChange(event) {
        // Clear previous timeout
        clearTimeout(this.searchTimeout);

        this.searchTerm = event.target.value;

        // Debounce search (wait 300ms after user stops typing)
        this.searchTimeout = setTimeout(() => {
            this.performSearch();
        }, 300);
    }

    async performSearch() {
        if (!this.searchTerm || this.searchTerm.length < 2) {
            this.accounts = [];
            return;
        }

        this.isLoading = true;
        this.error = undefined;

        try {
            const results = await searchAccounts({ 
                searchTerm: this.searchTerm 
            });
            this.accounts = results;
        } catch (error) {
            this.error = error.body?.message || 'An error occurred while searching';
            this.accounts = [];

            // Show toast notification
            this.dispatchEvent(
                new ShowToastEvent({
                    title: 'Error',
                    message: this.error,
                    variant: 'error'
                })
            );
        } finally {
            this.isLoading = false;
        }
    }

    handleAccountClick(event) {
        const accountId = event.currentTarget.dataset.id;

        // Navigate to account record page
        this[NavigationMixin.Navigate]({
            type: 'standard__recordPage',
            attributes: {
                recordId: accountId,
                objectApiName: 'Account',
                actionName: 'view'
            }
        });
    }
}

AccountController.cls (Apex):

public with sharing class AccountController {

    @AuraEnabled(cacheable=true)
    public static List<Account> searchAccounts(String searchTerm) {
        // Input validation
        if (String.isBlank(searchTerm) || searchTerm.length() < 2) {
            return new List<Account>();
        }

        // Sanitize input to prevent SOQL injection
        String sanitizedTerm = String.escapeSingleQuotes(searchTerm);
        String searchPattern = '%' + sanitizedTerm + '%';

        try {
            return [
                SELECT Id, Name, Industry, BillingCity, AnnualRevenue
                FROM Account
                WHERE Name LIKE :searchPattern
                OR Industry LIKE :searchPattern
                OR BillingCity LIKE :searchPattern
                WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED
                ORDER BY Name
                LIMIT 50
            ];
        } catch (Exception e) {
            throw new AuraHandledException('Error searching accounts: ' + e.getMessage());
        }
    }
}

Key LWC Concepts:

1. Decorators:

import { LightningElement, api, track, wire } from 'lwc';

export default class MyComponent extends LightningElement {
    // Public property (can be set from parent)
    @api recordId;

    // Tracked property (reactive)
    @track privateData = [];

    // Wire service to get data
    @wire(getRecord, { recordId: '$recordId', fields: FIELDS })
    account;
}

2. Lifecycle Hooks:

export default class LifecycleComponent extends LightningElement {
    constructor() {
        super();
        // Component instance created
    }

    connectedCallback() {
        // Component inserted into DOM
        // Good place for initialization
    }

    renderedCallback() {
        // Component finished rendering
        // Use sparingly (called multiple times)
    }

    disconnectedCallback() {
        // Component removed from DOM
        // Good place for cleanup
    }

    errorCallback(error, stack) {
        // Error occurred in component lifecycle
    }
}

3. Component Communication:

Parent to Child (Public Property):

// child.js
export default class Child extends LightningElement {
    @api message;
}

// parent.html
<template>
    <c-child message="Hello from parent"></c-child>
</template>

Child to Parent (Event):

// child.js
export default class Child extends LightningElement {
    handleClick() {
        const event = new CustomEvent('notify', {
            detail: { message: 'Button clicked' }
        });
        this.dispatchEvent(event);
    }
}

// parent.html
<template>
    <c-child onnotify={handleNotification}></c-child>
</template>

// parent.js
export default class Parent extends LightningElement {
    handleNotification(event) {
        console.log(event.detail.message);
    }
}

4. Lightning Data Service (LDS):

import { LightningElement, api, wire } from 'lwc';
import { getRecord, updateRecord } from 'lightning/uiRecordApi';
import ACCOUNT_NAME_FIELD from '@salesforce/schema/Account.Name';

export default class LdsExample extends LightningElement {
    @api recordId;

    @wire(getRecord, { 
        recordId: '$recordId', 
        fields: [ACCOUNT_NAME_FIELD] 
    })
    account;

    async handleUpdate() {
        const fields = {};
        fields.Id = this.recordId;
        fields.Name = 'Updated Name';

        const recordInput = { fields };

        try {
            await updateRecord(recordInput);
            // Show success toast
        } catch (error) {
            // Handle error
        }
    }
}

Migration Strategy (Aura to LWC):

Phase 1: Assessment

  • Identify Aura components for migration
  • Evaluate complexity and dependencies
  • Prioritize based on business value

Phase 2: New Development

  • Build all new components in LWC
  • Create LWC wrapper for Aura components if needed

Phase 3: Gradual Migration

  • Migrate simple components first
  • Test thoroughly in sandbox
  • Roll out incrementally to production

Best Practices:

✅ Use LWC for all new development

✅ Leverage Lightning Data Service when possible

✅ Implement proper error handling

✅ Use composition over inheritance

✅ Follow naming conventions (camelCase for properties, kebab-case for HTML)

✅ Write Jest tests for components

✅ Use lightning-base components (pre-built, accessible)

✅ Implement proper security (WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED)

Performance Tips:

✅ Use cacheable=true for @AuraEnabled methods

✅ Implement debouncing for search/filter operations

✅ Lazy load data when possible

✅ Use CSS for styling (not JavaScript)

✅ Minimize re-renders with proper reactive properties

Governor Limits:

⚠️ Component Size: 1 MB uncompressed

⚠️ Apex Methods: Subject to standard governor limits

⚠️ LDS Operations: Counted toward DML limits

Salesforce Edition Requirements:

  • ✅ All editions support LWC in Lightning Experience
  • ✅ Available in Experience Cloud (Community Cloud)
  • ✅ Mobile app support with proper configuration

📚 Learn More on Trailhead:

  • Lightning Web Components Basics
  • Quick Start: Lightning Web Components

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Q: What are the different Salesforce integration patterns and when should each be used?
docs.text:
A: Salesforce provides multiple integration patterns to connect with external systems. Choosing the right pattern depends on data volume, latency requirements, and system capabilities.

Integration Pattern Overview:

1. Request-Response (Synchronous):

  • Use Case: Real-time data needs, user-initiated actions
  • Technology: REST API, SOAP API
  • Direction: Bidirectional
  • Example: Credit check during order placement
  • Latency: Low (sub-second to seconds)
  • Volume: Low to medium (hundreds to thousands per hour)

2. Fire-and-Forget (Asynchronous):

  • Use Case: Non-critical updates, one-way data flow
  • Technology: Outbound Messages, Platform Events
  • Direction: Salesforce → External
  • Example: Send new lead to marketing automation
  • Latency: Medium (seconds to minutes)
  • Volume: Medium (thousands per hour)

3. Batch Data Synchronization:

  • Use Case: Large volumes, scheduled updates
  • Technology: Bulk API, Data Loader, ETL tools
  • Direction: Bidirectional
  • Example: Nightly product catalog sync
  • Latency: High (hours)
  • Volume: High (millions of records)

4. Remote Process Invocation:

  • Use Case: Complex processing offloaded to external system
  • Technology: REST/SOAP callouts, Named Credentials
  • Direction: Salesforce → External → Salesforce
  • Example: Tax calculation service
  • Latency: Low to medium
  • Volume: Low to medium

5. UI Update Based on Data Changes:

  • Use Case: Real-time UI updates, notifications
  • Technology: Platform Events, Streaming API, Change Data Capture
  • Direction: Salesforce → External
  • Example: Live dashboard updates
  • Latency: Near real-time (< 1 second)
  • Volume: Medium to high

Detailed Pattern Examples:

Pattern 1: REST API Integration

public class ExternalSystemIntegration {

    // Outbound REST callout
    public static String sendDataToExternalSystem(Account acc) {
        HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
        req.setEndpoint('callout:External_System/api/accounts');
        req.setMethod('POST');
        req.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json');

        // Build JSON payload
        Map<String, Object> payload = new Map<String, Object>{
            'accountName' => acc.Name,
            'industry' => acc.Industry,
            'revenue' => acc.AnnualRevenue
        };
        req.setBody(JSON.serialize(payload));

        Http http = new Http();
        HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

        if (res.getStatusCode() == 200) {
            return res.getBody();
        } else {
            throw new IntegrationException(
                'Error: ' + res.getStatusCode() + ' ' + res.getBody()
            );
        }
    }

    // Inbound REST service
    @RestResource(urlMapping='/accounts/*')
    global class AccountService {

        @HttpPost
        global static String createAccount(String name, String industry) {
            try {
                Account acc = new Account(
                    Name = name,
                    Industry = industry,
                    External_System__c = true
                );
                insert acc;

                return JSON.serialize(new Map<String, Object>{
                    'success' => true,
                    'accountId' => acc.Id
                });
            } catch (Exception e) {
                return JSON.serialize(new Map<String, Object>{
                    'success' => false,
                    'error' => e.getMessage()
                });
            }
        }

        @HttpGet
        global static Account getAccount() {
            RestRequest req = RestContext.request;
            String accountId = req.requestURI.substring(
                req.requestURI.lastIndexOf('/') + 1
            );

            return [
                SELECT Id, Name, Industry, AnnualRevenue
                FROM Account
                WHERE Id = :accountId
                LIMIT 1
            ];
        }

        @HttpPatch
        global static String updateAccount(String accountId, Map<String, Object> updates) {
            try {
                Account acc = new Account(Id = accountId);

                if (updates.containsKey('name')) {
                    acc.Name = (String)updates.get('name');
                }
                if (updates.containsKey('industry')) {
                    acc.Industry = (String)updates.get('industry');
                }

                update acc;

                return JSON.serialize(new Map<String, Object>{
                    'success' => true
                });
            } catch (Exception e) {
                return JSON.serialize(new Map<String, Object>{
                    'success' => false,
                    'error' => e.getMessage()
                });
            }
        }
    }

    public class IntegrationException extends Exception {}
}

Pattern 2: Platform Events (Event-Driven)

// Define Platform Event (via metadata)
// Order_Event__e with fields: Order_Id__c, Status__c, Total__c

// Publisher (Salesforce)
public class OrderEventPublisher {

    public static void publishOrderCreated(Order order) {
        Order_Event__e event = new Order_Event__e(
            Order_Id__c = order.Id,
            Status__c = 'Created',
            Total__c = order.TotalAmount
        );

        Database.SaveResult result = EventBus.publish(event);

        if (!result.isSuccess()) {
            for (Database.Error error : result.getErrors()) {
                System.debug('Error publishing event: ' + error.getMessage());
            }
        }
    }
}

// Subscriber (Apex Trigger on Platform Event)
trigger OrderEventTrigger on Order_Event__e (after insert) {
    List<Integration_Log__c> logs = new List<Integration_Log__c>();

    for (Order_Event__e event : Trigger.new) {
        logs.add(new Integration_Log__c(
            Order_Id__c = event.Order_Id__c,
            Event_Type__c = 'Order Created',
            Status__c = event.Status__c,
            Amount__c = event.Total__c,
            Received_Date__c = System.now()
        ));
    }

    if (!logs.isEmpty()) {
        insert logs;
    }
}

// External System Subscriber (using CometD)
// JavaScript/Node.js example
/*
const jsforce = require('jsforce');
const conn = new jsforce.Connection({
    oauth2: { /* oauth config */ }
});

conn.streaming.topic('/event/Order_Event__e').subscribe((message) => {
    console.log('Order Event received:', message);

    // Process the event
    processOrder({
        orderId: message.payload.Order_Id__c,
        status: message.payload.Status__c,
        total: message.payload.Total__c
    });
});
*/

Pattern 3: Bulk API Integration

public class BulkDataSync {

    @future(callout=true)
    public static void syncProductsFromExternalSystem() {
        HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
        req.setEndpoint('callout:Product_System/api/products/bulk');
        req.setMethod('GET');
        req.setHeader('Accept', 'application/json');
        req.setTimeout(120000); // 2 minutes

        Http http = new Http();
        HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

        if (res.getStatusCode() == 200) {
            List<Object> products = (List<Object>)JSON.deserializeUntyped(res.getBody());
            processBulkProducts(products);
        }
    }

    private static void processBulkProducts(List<Object> products) {
        List<Product2> productsToUpsert = new List<Product2>();
        Set<String> externalIds = new Set<String>();

        // Collect external IDs
        for (Object prodObj : products) {
            Map<String, Object> prod = (Map<String, Object>)prodObj;
            externalIds.add((String)prod.get('externalId'));
        }

        // Query existing products
        Map<String, Product2> existingProducts = new Map<String, Product2>();
        for (Product2 prod : [
            SELECT Id, External_ID__c, Name
            FROM Product2
            WHERE External_ID__c IN :externalIds
        ]) {
            existingProducts.put(prod.External_ID__c, prod);
        }

        // Prepare upsert
        for (Object prodObj : products) {
            Map<String, Object> prod = (Map<String, Object>)prodObj;
            String extId = (String)prod.get('externalId');

            Product2 p;
            if (existingProducts.containsKey(extId)) {
                p = existingProducts.get(extId);
            } else {
                p = new Product2();
            }

            p.Name = (String)prod.get('name');
            p.ProductCode = (String)prod.get('code');
            p.External_ID__c = extId;
            p.IsActive = true;

            productsToUpsert.add(p);
        }

        // Upsert in batches
        if (!productsToUpsert.isEmpty()) {
            Database.UpsertResult[] results = Database.upsert(
                productsToUpsert, 
                Product2.External_ID__c,
                false
            );

            // Log failures
            for (Integer i = 0; i < results.size(); i++) {
                if (!results[i].isSuccess()) {
                    System.debug('Failed to upsert product: ' + productsToUpsert[i].Name);
                    for (Database.Error error : results[i].getErrors()) {
                        System.debug('Error: ' + error.getMessage());
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

Pattern 4: Change Data Capture (CDC)

// Trigger on Change Event
trigger AccountChangeEventTrigger on AccountChangeEvent (after insert) {
    List<Integration_Queue__c> queueItems = new List<Integration_Queue__c>();

    for (AccountChangeEvent event : Trigger.new) {
        // Determine what changed
        EventBus.ChangeEventHeader header = event.ChangeEventHeader;

        Integration_Queue__c item = new Integration_Queue__c(
            Record_Id__c = header.recordIds[0],
            Object_Type__c = 'Account',
            Change_Type__c = header.changeType,
            Change_Origin__c = header.changeOrigin,
            Changed_Fields__c = String.join(header.changedFields, ','),
            Status__c = 'Pending',
            Retry_Count__c = 0
        );
        queueItems.add(item);
    }

    if (!queueItems.isEmpty()) {
        insert queueItems;

        // Process asynchronously
        IntegrationQueueProcessor.processQueue(queueItems);
    }
}

public class IntegrationQueueProcessor {

    @future(callout=true)
    public static void processQueue(List<Integration_Queue__c> items) {
        for (Integration_Queue__c item : items) {
            try {
                sendToExternalSystem(item);
                item.Status__c = 'Completed';
                item.Processed_Date__c = System.now();
            } catch (Exception e) {
                item.Status__c = 'Failed';
                item.Error_Message__c = e.getMessage();
                item.Retry_Count__c = item.Retry_Count__c + 1;
            }
        }
        update items;
    }

    private static void sendToExternalSystem(Integration_Queue__c item) {
        // Implementation of external system callout
        HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
        req.setEndpoint('callout:Change_Subscriber/api/changes');
        req.setMethod('POST');
        req.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json');

        Map<String, Object> payload = new Map<String, Object>{
            'recordId' => item.Record_Id__c,
            'objectType' => item.Object_Type__c,
            'changeType' => item.Change_Type__c,
            'changedFields' => item.Changed_Fields__c
        };
        req.setBody(JSON.serialize(payload));

        Http http = new Http();
        HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

        if (res.getStatusCode() != 200) {
            throw new IntegrationException('HTTP ' + res.getStatusCode() + ': ' + res.getBody());
        }
    }

    public class IntegrationException extends Exception {}
}

Integration Pattern Decision Matrix:

Requirement Recommended Pattern Real-time credit check Request-Response (REST/SOAP) Send new leads to marketing Platform Events or Outbound Messages Nightly product sync Bulk API or Batch Jobs Live dashboard updates Streaming API or Platform Events Complex tax calculation Remote Process Invocation (REST) Warehouse inventory check Request-Response with caching Order status notifications Platform Events (pub/sub) Mass data migration Bulk API 2.0

Best Practices by Role:

For Developers:

✅ Use Named Credentials for secure authentication

✅ Implement proper error handling and retry logic

✅ Use @future or Queueable for async callouts

✅ Monitor API usage and governor limits

✅ Implement circuit breaker patterns

✅ Log all integration transactions

For Architects:

✅ Design for idempotency

✅ Plan for failure scenarios

✅ Consider scalability and volume

✅ Document integration architecture

✅ Implement monitoring and alerting

✅ Use middleware when appropriate (MuleSoft, etc.)

✅ Consider security implications (data in transit/rest)

For Administrators:

✅ Configure Named Credentials properly

✅ Monitor integration logs regularly

✅ Set up remote site settings

✅ Manage API limits and usage

✅ Coordinate with external system admins

Governor Limits:

⚠️ API Calls per 24 Hours: 15,000 (Enterprise), 100,000 (Unlimited)

⚠️ Concurrent API Requests: 25

⚠️ Callout Timeout: 120 seconds max

⚠️ Callout Size: 6 MB request, 12 MB response

⚠️ Platform Events Published: 250,000 per 24 hours

⚠️ Streaming API Clients: 2,000 per org

Security Considerations:

✅ Always use HTTPS for API endpoints

✅ Implement OAuth 2.0 when possible

✅ Store credentials in Named Credentials

✅ Validate and sanitize all inputs

✅ Implement rate limiting

✅ Use field-level security on integrated fields

✅ Audit integration access regularly

  • API Basics
  • Platform Events Basics
