docs.title: Q: How does Salesforce's sharing model work?
docs.text:
A: Salesforce's sharing model is a comprehensive security framework that controls record-level access through multiple layers. Understanding this model is critical for proper data security implementation.

Sharing Model Layers (Most to Least Restrictive):

1. Organization-Wide Defaults (OWD):

  • Definition: Baseline access level for all users
  • Options: Private, Public Read Only, Public Read/Write, Controlled by Parent
  • Scope: Applies organization-wide
  • Use: Sets the most restrictive access level

2. Role Hierarchy:

  • Definition: Tree structure defining reporting relationships
  • Behavior: Users higher in hierarchy can access records owned by subordinates
  • Options: Can be disabled per object ("Grant Access Using Hierarchies")
  • Use: Reflects organizational structure

3. Sharing Rules:

  • Definition: Automatic sharing based on criteria or ownership
  • Types: Owner-based, Criteria-based
  • Direction: Can only open up access (never restrict)
  • Use: Extend access beyond OWD and hierarchy

4. Manual Sharing:

  • Definition: Record owner grants access to specific users/groups
  • Scope: Individual records
  • Use: Ad-hoc access needs

5. Apex Managed Sharing:

  • Definition: Programmatic sharing using Apex
  • Control: Full control over share records
  • Use: Complex sharing logic not achievable declaratively

Detailed Sharing Model Components:

Organization-Wide Defaults Configuration:

// Query to understand OWD settings (can't modify via Apex)
// This information would typically be viewed in Setup

// Example: Setting up for a custom object
Custom_Object__c obj;
// OWD options:
// - Private: Only owner and those above in hierarchy
// - Public Read Only: Everyone can read, only owner can edit
// - Public Read/Write: Everyone can read and edit

Sharing Rules Example:

Scenario: Sales Operations team needs access to all opportunities in their region

// Configured in Setup > Sharing Settings
// Criteria-Based Sharing Rule:
- Object: Opportunity
- Criteria: Region__c equals "West"
- Share with: Sales_Operations_West (Public Group)
- Access Level: Read/Write

Manual Sharing via Apex:

public class ManualSharingExample {

    public static void shareAccountWithUser(Id accountId, Id userId, String accessLevel) {
        AccountShare accountShare = new AccountShare();
        accountShare.AccountId = accountId;
        accountShare.UserOrGroupId = userId;
        accountShare.AccountAccessLevel = accessLevel; // 'Read' or 'Edit'
        accountShare.OpportunityAccessLevel = 'None'; // Related opportunities
        accountShare.CaseAccessLevel = 'None'; // Related cases
        accountShare.RowCause = Schema.AccountShare.RowCause.Manual;

        try {
            insert accountShare;
        } catch (DmlException e) {
            System.debug('Error sharing record: ' + e.getMessage());
        }
    }

    public static void removeManualSharing(Id accountId, Id userId) {
        List<AccountShare> sharesToDelete = [
            SELECT Id
            FROM AccountShare
            WHERE AccountId = :accountId
            AND UserOrGroupId = :userId
            AND RowCause = :Schema.AccountShare.RowCause.Manual
        ];

        if (!sharesToDelete.isEmpty()) {
            delete sharesToDelete;
        }
    }
}

Apex Managed Sharing:

public class ApexManagedSharingExample {

    // Custom sharing reason must be defined in Custom Object setup
    // e.g., Project_Team_Member__c

    public static void shareProjectWithTeam(Id projectId, Set<Id> teamMemberIds) {
        List<Custom_Project__Share> sharesToCreate = new List<Custom_Project__Share>();

        for (Id memberId : teamMemberIds) {
            Custom_Project__Share share = new Custom_Project__Share();
            share.ParentId = projectId;
            share.UserOrGroupId = memberId;
            share.AccessLevel = 'Edit';
            share.RowCause = Schema.Custom_Project__Share.RowCause.Project_Team_Member__c;

            sharesToCreate.add(share);
        }

        if (!sharesToCreate.isEmpty()) {
            Database.SaveResult[] results = Database.insert(sharesToCreate, false);

            for (Database.SaveResult result : results) {
                if (!result.isSuccess()) {
                    System.debug('Error creating share: ' + result.getErrors());
                }
            }
        }
    }

    public static void removeProjectTeamSharing(Id projectId) {
        List<Custom_Project__Share> sharesToDelete = [
            SELECT Id
            FROM Custom_Project__Share
            WHERE ParentId = :projectId
            AND RowCause = :Schema.Custom_Project__Share.RowCause.Project_Team_Member__c
        ];

        if (!sharesToDelete.isEmpty()) {
            delete sharesToDelete;
        }
    }
}

Checking User Access Programmatically:

public class RecordAccessChecker {

    public static Boolean canUserEditAccount(Id userId, Id accountId) {
        // Check if user has edit access
        UserRecordAccess access = [
            SELECT RecordId, HasReadAccess, HasEditAccess, HasDeleteAccess
            FROM UserRecordAccess
            WHERE UserId = :userId
            AND RecordId = :accountId
        ];

        return access.HasEditAccess;
    }

    public static Map<Id, Boolean> checkBulkAccess(Id userId, Set<Id> recordIds) {
        Map<Id, Boolean> accessMap = new Map<Id, Boolean>();

        for (UserRecordAccess access : [
            SELECT RecordId, HasEditAccess
            FROM UserRecordAccess
            WHERE UserId = :userId
            AND RecordId IN :recordIds
        ]) {
            accessMap.put(access.RecordId, access.HasEditAccess);
        }

        return accessMap;
    }

    public static Boolean canUserAccessField(String objectName, String fieldName) {
        Schema.SObjectType objType = Schema.getGlobalDescribe().get(objectName);
        Schema.DescribeSObjectResult objDescribe = objType.getDescribe();
        Map<String, Schema.SObjectField> fields = objDescribe.fields.getMap();
        Schema.DescribeFieldResult fieldDescribe = fields.get(fieldName).getDescribe();

        return fieldDescribe.isAccessible();
    }
}

Sharing in Apex: WITH SHARING vs WITHOUT SHARING:

// Respects user's sharing rules
public with sharing class WithSharingClass {
    public List<Account> getAccounts() {
        // Only returns accounts user has access to
        return [SELECT Id, Name FROM Account LIMIT 100];
    }
}

// Ignores sharing rules (runs in system context)
public without sharing class WithoutSharingClass {
    public List<Account> getAllAccounts() {
        // Returns all accounts regardless of user access
        return [SELECT Id, Name FROM Account LIMIT 100];
    }
}

// Inherits sharing context from caller
public class InheritedSharingClass {
    public List<Account> getAccounts() {
        // Sharing depends on calling class
        return [SELECT Id, Name FROM Account LIMIT 100];
    }
}

// Modern approach (API 40.0+)
public inherited sharing class ModernSharingClass {
    public List<Account> getAccounts() {
        // Explicitly inherits sharing from caller
        return [SELECT Id, Name FROM Account LIMIT 100];
    }
}

Complex Sharing Scenario:

public class TerritoryBasedSharing {

    // Share opportunities based on territory assignment
    public static void shareOpportunitiesByTerritory() {
        // Get territory assignments
        Map<Id, Set<Id>> territoryToUsers = new Map<Id, Set<Id>>();

        for (UserTerritory__c ut : [
            SELECT User__c, Territory__c
            FROM UserTerritory__c
            WHERE Active__c = true
        ]) {
            if (!territoryToUsers.containsKey(ut.Territory__c)) {
                territoryToUsers.put(ut.Territory__c, new Set<Id>());
            }
            territoryToUsers.get(ut.Territory__c).add(ut.User__c);
        }

        // Get opportunities in territories
        Map<Id, Set<Id>> oppToUsers = new Map<Id, Set<Id>>();

        for (Opportunity opp : [
            SELECT Id, Territory__c
            FROM Opportunity
            WHERE Territory__c IN :territoryToUsers.keySet()
            AND StageName != 'Closed Won'
            AND StageName != 'Closed Lost'
        ]) {
            oppToUsers.put(opp.Id, territoryToUsers.get(opp.Territory__c));
        }

        // Create sharing records
        List<OpportunityShare> sharesToCreate = new List<OpportunityShare>();

        for (Id oppId : oppToUsers.keySet()) {
            for (Id userId : oppToUsers.get(oppId)) {
                OpportunityShare share = new OpportunityShare();
                share.OpportunityId = oppId;
                share.UserOrGroupId = userId;
                share.OpportunityAccessLevel = 'Edit';
                share.RowCause = Schema.OpportunityShare.RowCause.Territory__c;

                sharesToCreate.add(share);
            }
        }

        if (!sharesToCreate.isEmpty()) {
            Database.insert(sharesToCreate, false);
        }
    }
}

Field-Level Security (FLS):

public class FieldLevelSecurityExample {

    public static void enforceFieldSecurity() {
        // Always check FLS before CRUD operations
        if (!Schema.sObjectType.Account.fields.Revenue__c.isAccessible()) {
            throw new SecurityException('No access to Revenue field');
        }

        if (!Schema.sObjectType.Account.fields.Revenue__c.isUpdateable()) {
            throw new SecurityException('Cannot update Revenue field');
        }

        // Perform operation
        Account acc = new Account(Id = 'xxx', Revenue__c = 1000000);
        update acc;
    }

    public static List<Account> getAccountsWithFieldSecurity() {
        // stripInaccessible removes fields user can't access
        List<Account> accounts = [
            SELECT Id, Name, Industry, Revenue__c, Confidential_Notes__c
            FROM Account
            LIMIT 100
        ];

        SObjectAccessDecision decision = Security.stripInaccessible(
            AccessType.READABLE,
            accounts
        );

        return decision.getRecords();
    }
}

Best Practices by Role:

For Administrators:

✅ Start with Private OWD and open up as needed

✅ Document sharing rules and their business justification

✅ Regular security audits of access

✅ Use Public Groups for easier maintenance

✅ Test sharing changes in sandbox first

✅ Leverage role hierarchy for reporting structure

For Developers:

✅ Always use WITH SHARING unless specific reason

✅ Check FLS before CRUD operations

✅ Use Security.stripInaccessible() for queries

✅ Test code with different user profiles

✅ Document security assumptions in code

✅ Use inherited sharing in modern code

For Architects:

✅ Design sharing model early in project

✅ Consider performance impact of complex sharing

✅ Plan for sharing recalculation overhead

✅ Document security architecture

✅ Balance security with usability

✅ Plan for scale (sharing rules impact)

Common Pitfalls:

❌ Using WITHOUT SHARING without justification

❌ Not testing with restricted users

❌ Ignoring field-level security

❌ Complex sharing rules causing performance issues

❌ Not documenting sharing decisions

❌ Mixing manual and Apex sharing without plan

Governor Limits:

⚠️ Sharing Rules per Object: 300 (50 ownership + 50 criteria-based per object)

⚠️ Manual Shares: Unlimited (within storage limits)

⚠️ Share Records: Count toward storage limits

⚠️ Sharing Recalculation: Can take hours for large orgs

Performance Considerations:

  • Minimize criteria-based sharing rules
  • Use owner-based rules when possible
  • Consider Apex managed sharing for complex logic
  • Monitor sharing recalculation times
  • Test with realistic data volumes

Security Checklist:

✅ OWD configured appropriately

✅ Role hierarchy matches org structure

✅ Sharing rules documented

✅ Field-level security enforced

✅ Object permissions set correctly

✅ Apex respects sharing rules

✅ Regular security reviews scheduled

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Q: How do I optimize SOQL queries for better performance?
docs.text:
A: SOQL query optimization is critical for maintaining good performance and avoiding governor limits. Poorly written queries can cause timeout issues and degrade user experience.

Key Optimization Principles:

1. Selective Queries (Use Indexes):

Salesforce automatically indexes certain fields. Queries using indexed fields are much faster.

Automatically Indexed Fields:

  • Id
  • Name
  • OwnerId
  • CreatedDate
  • SystemModstamp
  • RecordType
  • Master-Detail relationships
  • Lookup relationships
  • External ID fields (marked as such)
  • Unique fields

❌ Non-Selective Query (Slow):

// Bad: No indexed fields in WHERE clause
List<Account> accounts = [
    SELECT Id, Name
    FROM Account
    WHERE Description LIKE '%technology%'
    LIMIT 10000
];
// Problem: Full table scan required

✅ Selective Query (Fast):

// Good: Uses indexed field
List<Account> accounts = [
    SELECT Id, Name, Description
    FROM Account
    WHERE CreatedDate = LAST_N_DAYS:30
    AND OwnerId = :UserInfo.getUserId()
    LIMIT 10000
];
// Benefit: Index used, much faster execution

2. Query Only Needed Fields:

❌ Inefficient:

// Bad: Retrieving all fields (uses resources unnecessarily)
List<Account> accounts = [
    SELECT FIELDS(ALL)
    FROM Account
    WHERE Id = :accountId
];

✅ Efficient:

// Good: Only query fields you need
List<Account> accounts = [
    SELECT Id, Name, Industry, AnnualRevenue
    FROM Account
    WHERE Id = :accountId
];

3. Use Relationship Queries Efficiently:

❌ Multiple Queries:

// Bad: N+1 query problem
List<Account> accounts = [SELECT Id FROM Account LIMIT 100];
for (Account acc : accounts) {
    // Separate query for each account!
    List<Contact> contacts = [
        SELECT Id, Name
        FROM Contact
        WHERE AccountId = :acc.Id
    ];
}
// Problem: 101 SOQL queries (hits governor limit fast)

✅ Single Query with Relationship:

// Good: One query gets all data
List<Account> accounts = [
    SELECT Id, Name,
        (SELECT Id, FirstName, LastName, Email
         FROM Contacts
         WHERE Active__c = true)
    FROM Account
    WHERE Industry = 'Technology'
    LIMIT 100
];

for (Account acc : accounts) {
    for (Contact con : acc.Contacts) {
        // Process contacts
    }
}
// Benefit: Only 1 SOQL query

4. Aggregate Queries:

❌ Processing in Apex:

// Bad: Query all records and calculate in Apex
List<Opportunity> opps = [
    SELECT Amount
    FROM Opportunity
    WHERE AccountId = :accountId
];

Decimal total = 0;
for (Opportunity opp : opps) {
    total += opp.Amount;
}
// Problem: Wastes heap and CPU time

✅ Use SOQL Aggregation:

// Good: Let database do the work
AggregateResult[] results = [
    SELECT SUM(Amount) totalAmount, COUNT(Id) oppCount
    FROM Opportunity
    WHERE AccountId = :accountId
    AND StageName != 'Closed Lost'
];

Decimal total = (Decimal)results[0].get('totalAmount');
Integer count = (Integer)results[0].get('oppCount');
// Benefit: Faster, uses less resources

5. Query Filters and Limits:

❌ Filtering in Apex:

// Bad: Query too many records, filter in Apex
List<Account> allAccounts = [
    SELECT Id, Name, AnnualRevenue
    FROM Account
];

List<Account> highValueAccounts = new List<Account>();
for (Account acc : allAccounts) {
    if (acc.AnnualRevenue > 1000000) {
        highValueAccounts.add(acc);
    }
}
// Problem: Retrieves unnecessary data

✅ Filter in SOQL:

// Good: Filter in query
List<Account> highValueAccounts = [
    SELECT Id, Name, AnnualRevenue
    FROM Account
    WHERE AnnualRevenue > 1000000
    ORDER BY AnnualRevenue DESC
    LIMIT 1000
];
// Benefit: Only retrieves needed data

Complete SOQL Optimization Example:

public class OptimizedQueryExamples {

    // Example 1: Efficient Account with Related Data
    public static List<Account> getAccountsWithDetails(Set<Id> accountIds) {
        return [
            SELECT Id, Name, Industry, AnnualRevenue, BillingCity,
                   Owner.Name, Owner.Email,
                   (SELECT Id, FirstName, LastName, Email, Phone
                    FROM Contacts
                    WHERE Email != null
                    ORDER BY CreatedDate DESC
                    LIMIT 10),
                   (SELECT Id, Name, StageName, Amount, CloseDate
                    FROM Opportunities
                    WHERE StageName NOT IN ('Closed Won', 'Closed Lost')
                    ORDER BY CloseDate ASC
                    LIMIT 5)
            FROM Account
            WHERE Id IN :accountIds
            AND IsDeleted = false
            ORDER BY Name
        ];
    }

    // Example 2: Aggregate Query with Grouping
    public static Map<String, Decimal> getRevenueBySector() {
        Map<String, Decimal> revenueMap = new Map<String, Decimal>();

        for (AggregateResult ar : [
            SELECT Industry, SUM(AnnualRevenue) totalRevenue, COUNT(Id) accountCount
            FROM Account
            WHERE AnnualRevenue != null
            AND CreatedDate = THIS_YEAR
            GROUP BY Industry
            HAVING SUM(AnnualRevenue) > 1000000
            ORDER BY SUM(AnnualRevenue) DESC
        ]) {
            String industry = (String)ar.get('Industry');
            Decimal revenue = (Decimal)ar.get('totalRevenue');
            revenueMap.put(industry, revenue);
        }

        return revenueMap;
    }

    // Example 3: Parent-to-Child Query
    public static List<Account> getAccountsWithOpenOpportunities() {
        return [
            SELECT Id, Name,
                   (SELECT Id, Name, StageName, Amount, Probability
                    FROM Opportunities
                    WHERE IsClosed = false
                    AND Amount > 50000
                    ORDER BY Amount DESC)
            FROM Account
            WHERE Id IN (
                SELECT AccountId
                FROM Opportunity
                WHERE IsClosed = false
                AND Amount > 50000
            )
            LIMIT 200
        ];
    }

    // Example 4: Child-to-Parent Query
    public static List<Contact> getContactsWithAccountInfo() {
        return [
            SELECT Id, FirstName, LastName, Email,
                   Account.Name, Account.Industry, Account.BillingCity,
                   Account.Owner.Name, Account.Owner.Email
            FROM Contact
            WHERE Account.Industry = 'Technology'
            AND Email != null
            AND CreatedDate = LAST_N_DAYS:90
            ORDER BY CreatedDate DESC
            LIMIT 500
        ];
    }

    // Example 5: Using Date Literals (Indexed)
    public static List<Opportunity> getRecentOpportunities() {
        return [
            SELECT Id, Name, StageName, Amount, CloseDate, Account.Name
            FROM Opportunity
            WHERE CreatedDate = THIS_MONTH
            AND StageName IN ('Prospecting', 'Qualification', 'Needs Analysis')
            ORDER BY CreatedDate DESC
        ];
    }

    // Example 6: Query with FOR UPDATE (Locking)
    public static List<Account> getAccountsForUpdate(Set<Id> accountIds) {
        // Locks records to prevent concurrent modification
        return [
            SELECT Id, Name, AnnualRevenue
            FROM Account
            WHERE Id IN :accountIds
            FOR UPDATE
        ];
    }

    // Example 7: Semi-Join (Exists Pattern)
    public static List<Account> getAccountsWithContacts() {
        return [
            SELECT Id, Name, Industry
            FROM Account
            WHERE Id IN (
                SELECT AccountId
                FROM Contact
                WHERE Email != null
            )
            ORDER BY Name
        ];
    }

    // Example 8: Anti-Join (Not Exists Pattern)
    public static List<Account> getAccountsWithoutContacts() {
        return [
            SELECT Id, Name, Industry
            FROM Account
            WHERE Id NOT IN (
                SELECT AccountId
                FROM Contact
                WHERE AccountId != null
            )
            ORDER BY Name
        ];
    }
}

Advanced Optimization Techniques:

1. Query Plans and Explain Plans:

// Use Query Plan tool in Developer Console
// Helps identify if indexes are being used

// Example of checking selectivity
// A query is selective if it returns < 10% of total records

2. Custom Indexes:

// For non-standard fields that need indexing
// Must request from Salesforce Support
// Criteria:
// - Field queried frequently
// - Returns < 10% of records
// - Part of critical business process

3. Skinny Tables:

// For very wide objects with > 100 fields
// Salesforce creates narrow table with frequently accessed fields
// Must request from Salesforce Support
// Criteria:
// - Object has many fields
// - Specific subset queried frequently
// - Performance issues documented

Performance Monitoring:

public class QueryPerformanceMonitor {

    public static void logQueryPerformance(String queryName, Long startTime) {
        Long endTime = System.currentTimeMillis();
        Long duration = endTime - startTime;

        Performance_Log__c log = new Performance_Log__c(
            Query_Name__c = queryName,
            Duration_MS__c = duration,
            SOQL_Queries_Used__c = Limits.getQueries(),
            CPU_Time_Used__c = Limits.getCpuTime(),
            Heap_Size_Used__c = Limits.getHeapSize(),
            Timestamp__c = System.now()
        );

        insert log;

        // Alert if performance threshold exceeded
        if (duration > 5000) { // 5 seconds
            System.debug('PERFORMANCE WARNING: ' + queryName + 
                        ' took ' + duration + 'ms');
        }
    }

    public static void testQueryPerformance() {
        Long startTime = System.currentTimeMillis();

        // Execute query
        List<Account> accounts = [
            SELECT Id, Name, (SELECT Id FROM Contacts)
            FROM Account
            LIMIT 1000
        ];

        logQueryPerformance('AccountWithContacts', startTime);
    }
}

Query Best Practices Checklist:

✅ Use indexed fields in WHERE clauses

✅ Query only necessary fields

✅ Use relationship queries to avoid multiple queries

✅ Use aggregate queries instead of Apex calculations

✅ Apply filters in SOQL, not Apex

✅ Use LIMIT to restrict result size

✅ Test queries with production-size data

✅ Monitor query performance

✅ Use Query Plan tool for optimization

✅ Consider custom indexes for complex queries

Common Query Anti-Patterns:

❌ SOQL inside loops

❌ Querying all fields with FIELDS(ALL)

❌ Filtering large result sets in Apex

❌ Not using relationship queries

❌ Missing LIMIT clauses

❌ Querying deleted records unnecessarily

❌ Not using indexed fields

❌ Nested queries without proper filtering

Governor Limits:

⚠️ SOQL Queries: 100 per transaction (synchronous), 200 (asynchronous)

⚠️ Query Rows: 50,000 per transaction

⚠️ Query Timeout: 120 seconds

⚠️ Heap Size: 6 MB (synchronous), 12 MB (asynchronous)

⚠️ CPU Time: 10,000 ms (synchronous), 60,000 ms (asynchronous)

Performance Tips:

✅ Selective queries (< 10% of records) use indexes efficiently

✅ Queries on standard indexed fields are fastest

✅ Avoid text searches (LIKE) on non-indexed fields

✅ Use date literals (THIS_MONTH, LAST_N_DAYS:30) - they're indexed

✅ Aggregate queries are more efficient than Apex calculations

✅ Relationship queries save query limits

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Q: How do I debug Apex code and troubleshoot issues?
docs.text:
A: Effective debugging is essential for identifying and fixing issues in Salesforce. Understanding debug logs, exception handling, and troubleshooting techniques saves significant development time.

Debug Log Fundamentals:

Setting Debug Log Levels:

Setup → Debug Logs → New
- User: Select user to monitor
- Debug Level: Select or create debug level
- Expiration: Set when log expires (max 24 hours)

Debug Level Categories:
- Database: SOQL, DML operations
- Workflow: Process Builder, Workflows
- Validation: Validation rules
- Callout: External API calls
- Apex Code: Apex execution
- Apex Profiling: Method execution time
- Visualforce: Page rendering
- System: System processes

Debug Log Levels:

  • NONE: No logging
  • ERROR: Error messages only
  • WARN: Warnings and errors
  • INFO: Informational messages
  • DEBUG: Detailed debugging info
  • FINE, FINER, FINEST: Increasing detail levels

Using System.debug():

public class DebuggingExamples {

    public static void basicDebugging() {
        // Basic debug statement
        System.debug('Starting process...');

        // Debug with log level
        System.debug(LoggingLevel.ERROR, 'Critical error occurred');
        System.debug(LoggingLevel.WARN, 'Warning: approaching limit');
        System.debug(LoggingLevel.INFO, 'Information message');
        System.debug(LoggingLevel.DEBUG, 'Debug details');

        // Debug variables
        String accountName = 'Acme Corporation';
        System.debug('Account Name: ' + accountName);

        // Debug collections
        List<String> items = new List<String>{'A', 'B', 'C'};
        System.debug('Items: ' + items);

        // Debug objects
        Account acc = new Account(Name = 'Test', Industry = 'Technology');
        System.debug('Account: ' + acc);
        System.debug('Account JSON: ' + JSON.serializePretty(acc));
    }

    public static void debugQueryResults() {
        List<Account> accounts = [
            SELECT Id, Name, Industry
            FROM Account
            LIMIT 5
        ];

        System.debug('Query returned ' + accounts.size() + ' accounts');
        for (Account acc : accounts) {
            System.debug('Account: ' + acc.Name + ' (' + acc.Industry + ')');
        }
    }

    public static void debugGovernorLimits() {
        System.debug('=== GOVERNOR LIMITS ===');
        System.debug('SOQL Queries: ' + Limits.getQueries() + '/' + Limits.getLimitQueries());
        System.debug('DML Statements: ' + Limits.getDmlStatements() + '/' + Limits.getLimitDmlStatements());
        System.debug('DML Rows: ' + Limits.getDmlRows() + '/' + Limits.getLimitDmlRows());
        System.debug('CPU Time: ' + Limits.getCpuTime() + '/' + Limits.getLimitCpuTime());
        System.debug('Heap Size: ' + Limits.getHeapSize() + '/' + Limits.getLimitHeapSize());
        System.debug('=======================');
    }
}

Exception Handling:

public class ExceptionHandlingExamples {

    // Comprehensive exception handling
    public static void robustExceptionHandling() {
        try {
            // Risky operation
            Account acc = [SELECT Id FROM Account WHERE Name = 'NonExistent'];
            update acc;

        } catch (QueryException e) {
            // Specific exception for query issues
            System.debug('Query error: ' + e.getMessage());
            System.debug('Line number: ' + e.getLineNumber());
            System.debug('Stack trace: ' + e.getStackTraceString());

        } catch (DmlException e) {
            // Specific exception for DML issues
            System.debug('DML error: ' + e.getMessage());
            System.debug('Number of errors: ' + e.getNumDml());

            for (Integer i = 0; i < e.getNumDml(); i++) {
                System.debug('Error ' + i + ': ' + e.getDmlMessage(i));
                System.debug('Failed record ID: ' + e.getDmlId(i));
                System.debug('Field causing error: ' + e.getDmlFieldNames(i));
            }

        } catch (Exception e) {
            // Generic exception catch-all
            System.debug('Unexpected error: ' + e.getMessage());
            System.debug('Type: ' + e.getTypeName());
            System.debug('Line: ' + e.getLineNumber());
            System.debug('Stack: ' + e.getStackTraceString());

        } finally {
            // Always executes
            System.debug('Cleanup code here');
        }
    }

    // Custom exception
    public class CustomBusinessException extends Exception {
        private String errorCode;

        public CustomBusinessException(String message, String code) {
            this(message);
            this.errorCode = code;
        }

        public String getErrorCode() {
            return this.errorCode;
        }
    }

    public static void throwCustomException() {
        throw new CustomBusinessException('Business rule violated', 'BUS001');
    }

    // Partial success with Database methods
    public static void partialSuccessPattern() {
        List<Account> accounts = new List<Account>{
            new Account(Name = 'Valid Account'),
            new Account(), // Missing required Name
            new Account(Name = 'Another Valid Account')
        };

        // allOrNone = false allows partial success
        Database.SaveResult[] results = Database.insert(accounts, false);

        for (Integer i = 0; i < results.size(); i++) {
            if (results[i].isSuccess()) {
                System.debug('Successfully inserted account: ' + accounts[i].Name);
            } else {
                System.debug('Failed to insert account');
                for (Database.Error error : results[i].getErrors()) {
                    System.debug('Error: ' + error.getMessage());
                    System.debug('Fields: ' + error.getFields());
                    System.debug('Status Code: ' + error.getStatusCode());
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

Advanced Debugging Techniques:

public class AdvancedDebugging {

    // Checkpoint debugging (Developer Console)
    public static void checkpointExample() {
        // Set checkpoints in Developer Console
        // Execute method
        // Inspect heap and variables at each checkpoint

        List<Account> accounts = [SELECT Id, Name FROM Account LIMIT 10];

        for (Account acc : accounts) {
            // Checkpoint 1: Inspect acc variable
            String modifiedName = acc.Name.toUpperCase();
            // Checkpoint 2: Inspect modifiedName
            acc.Name = modifiedName;
        }

        update accounts;
        // Checkpoint 3: Verify updates
    }

    // Performance profiling
    public static void profilePerformance() {
        Long startCPU = Limits.getCpuTime();
        Long startHeap = Limits.getHeapSize();

        // Code to profile
        performExpensiveOperation();

        Long endCPU = Limits.getCpuTime();
        Long endHeap = Limits.getHeapSize();

        System.debug('CPU Time Used: ' + (endCPU - startCPU) + 'ms');
        System.debug('Heap Used: ' + (endHeap - startHeap) + ' bytes');
    }

    private static void performExpensiveOperation() {
        // Simulate work
        List<Account> accounts = [
            SELECT Id, Name, (SELECT Id FROM Contacts)
            FROM Account
            LIMIT 1000
        ];
    }

    // Debugging with trace flags
    public static void traceExample() {
        // Enable trace flag for specific user
        // All operations logged automatically

        System.debug('=== Starting complex operation ===');

        // Step 1
        System.debug('Step 1: Querying accounts');
        List<Account> accounts = getAccounts();

        // Step 2
        System.debug('Step 2: Processing ' + accounts.size() + ' accounts');
        processAccounts(accounts);

        // Step 3
        System.debug('Step 3: Updating records');
        updateAccounts(accounts);

        System.debug('=== Operation complete ===');
    }

    private static List<Account> getAccounts() {
        return [SELECT Id, Name FROM Account LIMIT 100];
    }

    private static void processAccounts(List<Account> accounts) {
        for (Account acc : accounts) {
            acc.Name = acc.Name + ' (Processed)';
        }
    }

    private static void updateAccounts(List<Account> accounts) {
        update accounts;
    }
}

Common Issues and Solutions:

Issue 1: SOQL 101 Error

// ❌ Problem: SOQL inside loop
trigger BadTrigger on Contact (after insert) {
    for (Contact con : Trigger.new) {
        Account acc = [SELECT Id FROM Account WHERE Id = :con.AccountId];
    }
}

// ✅ Solution: Bulkify the query
trigger GoodTrigger on Contact (after insert) {
    Set<Id> accountIds = new Set<Id>();
    for (Contact con : Trigger.new) {
        accountIds.add(con.AccountId);
    }

    Map<Id, Account> accounts = new Map<Id, Account>(
        [SELECT Id FROM Account WHERE Id IN :accountIds]
    );
}

Issue 2: CPU Timeout

// ❌ Problem: Inefficient loops
public static void inefficientCode() {
    List<Account> accounts = [SELECT Id, Name FROM Account LIMIT 10000];
    for (Account acc1 : accounts) {
        for (Account acc2 : accounts) {
            // O(n²) complexity
            if (acc1.Name == acc2.Name) {
                // Process
            }
        }
    }
}

// ✅ Solution: Use sets and maps
public static void efficientCode() {
    List<Account> accounts = [SELECT Id, Name FROM Account LIMIT 10000];
    Map<String, List<Account>> accountsByName = new Map<String, List<Account>>();

    for (Account acc : accounts) {
        if (!accountsByName.containsKey(acc.Name)) {
            accountsByName.put(acc.Name, new List<Account>());
        }
        accountsByName.get(acc.Name).add(acc);
    }
    // O(n) complexity
}

Issue 3: Heap Size Exceeded

// ❌ Problem: Loading too much data
public static void heapIssue() {
    List<Account> accounts = [
        SELECT Id, Name, Description, 
               (SELECT Id, FirstName, LastName, Description FROM Contacts)
        FROM Account
    ];
}

// ✅ Solution: Batch processing
public static void heapSolution() {
    // Process in smaller batches
    Integer batchSize = 200;
    Integer offset = 0;

    List<Account> accounts;
    do {
        accounts = [
            SELECT Id, Name
            FROM Account
            LIMIT :batchSize
            OFFSET :offset
        ];

        processBatch(accounts);
        offset += batchSize;

    } while (accounts.size() == batchSize);
}

Debugging Checklist:

✅ Enable debug logs for affected user

✅ Set appropriate debug levels

✅ Use System.debug() strategically

✅ Check governor limits throughout execution

✅ Use try-catch for specific exceptions

✅ Log critical information before errors

✅ Test with realistic data volumes

✅ Use Developer Console checkpoints

✅ Review full stack traces

✅ Check for governor limit warnings

Tools for Debugging:

  • Developer Console: Real-time log viewing, checkpoints, query editor
  • VS Code + Salesforce Extensions: Modern development environment
  • Apex Replay Debugger: Step-through debugging
  • Query Plan Tool: Optimize SOQL queries
  • Event Monitoring: Track user activity and performance

Best Practices:

✅ Remove or comment out debug statements in production code

✅ Use meaningful debug messages

✅ Include context in error messages

✅ Log governor limits before hitting them

✅ Implement proper exception handling

✅ Don't catch Exception unless necessary (be specific)

✅ Clean up resources in finally blocks

✅ Use custom exceptions for business logic errors

docs.title: Q: What are the key topics for Salesforce certifications?
docs.text:
A: Salesforce offers multiple certification paths for different roles. Understanding what each certification covers helps you prepare effectively.

Administrator Certifications:

1. Salesforce Administrator (ADM-201):

Coverage Areas:

  • Organization Setup (3%): Company information, fiscal year, currency management
  • User Management (7%): Users, profiles, roles, permission sets
  • Security & Access (13%): OWD, sharing rules, field-level security
  • Standard & Custom Objects (14%): Object relationships, field types, validation
  • Sales & Marketing Applications (12%): Leads, accounts, opportunities, campaigns
  • Service & Support Applications (11%): Cases, knowledge, service console
  • Activity Management (3%): Tasks, events, calendars
  • Data Management (10%): Import, export, data quality
  • Analytics (10%): Reports, dashboards, folders
  • Workflow/Process Automation (13%): Flows, approval processes, validation rules
  • Mobile (2%): Salesforce mobile app
  • AppExchange (2%): Installing and managing packages

Key Study Areas:

  • Object relationships and schema design
  • Automation tools (Flow, Process Builder, Workflow Rules)
  • Security model (profiles, permission sets, sharing)
  • Report types and dashboard components
  • Data management tools and best practices

Developer Certifications:

2. Platform Developer I (PD1):

Coverage Areas:

  • Salesforce Fundamentals (7%): Platform basics, org limits
  • Data Modeling & Management (13%): Objects, fields, relationships, schema
  • Logic & Process Automation (30%): Apex triggers, classes, testing
  • User Interface (23%): Visualforce, Lightning Components, page layouts
  • Testing, Debugging & Deployment (17%): Test classes, debug logs, deployment
  • Developer Console & Tools (10%): Developer tools, debugging

Key Study Areas:

  • Apex programming (classes, triggers, batch, queueable)
  • SOQL and SOSL queries
  • DML operations and governor limits
  • Trigger frameworks and best practices
  • Test class development (75%+ coverage)
  • Lightning Web Components basics
  • Visualforce fundamentals

3. Platform Developer II (PD2):

Advanced Topics:

  • Advanced Apex (37%): Design patterns, asynchronous Apex, integration
  • Integration (23%): REST/SOAP APIs, callouts, platform events
  • Data Modeling (13%): Complex schemas, performance optimization
  • User Interface (13%): Advanced Lightning Components, dynamic UI
  • Testing (14%): Advanced testing, mocking, test data

Architect Certifications:

4. Application Architect:

  • Data modeling at scale
  • Business logic and process automation
  • Security and sharing architecture
  • Integration architecture
  • Mobile solutions

5. System Architect:

  • Data lifecycle management
  • Change management and deployments
  • Development lifecycle
  • Environment management
  • Release management

Certification Preparation Tips:

For Administrator:

✅ Practice in Developer Edition org

✅ Complete Trailhead modules (Admin Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced)

✅ Focus on hands-on configuration

✅ Understand when to use each automation tool

✅ Practice creating reports and dashboards

✅ Review Salesforce Help documentation

For Platform Developer I:

✅ Write Apex code daily

✅ Build sample applications

✅ Practice SOQL queries

✅ Understand governor limits thoroughly

✅ Write test classes for everything

✅ Study trigger frameworks

✅ Learn Lightning Web Components basics

For Platform Developer II:

✅ Master design patterns

✅ Build complex integrations

✅ Practice asynchronous Apex

✅ Implement enterprise patterns

✅ Focus on scalability and performance

✅ Study security best practices

Sample Certification Questions:

Administrator Question:

Q: A sales manager wants to see all opportunities owned by their team members,
but team members should not see each other's opportunities. How should this be configured?

A) Set Opportunity OWD to Private and create a role hierarchy

Answer: A
Explanation: Private OWD restricts access to owner only. Role hierarchy allows
managers to see subordinate records automatically.

Developer Question:

Q: What is the maximum number of SOQL queries allowed in a single Apex transaction?

A) 100 for synchronous, 200 for asynchronous

Explanation: This is a critical governor limit that must be designed around.

✅ Don't spend too long on one question

✅ Mark questions for review

docs.title: Q: What are the main types of APIs available in Salesforce?
docs.text:
A: Salesforce provides multiple API types to support different integration scenarios and use cases.

Available API Types:

  • REST API: Modern, lightweight API using JSON for web and mobile applications
  • SOAP API: Enterprise-grade API using XML for complex integrations
  • Bulk API 2.0: High-performance API for processing large data volumes
  • Streaming API: Push-based API for real-time event notifications
  • Metadata API: Manages org configuration and customization metadata
  • Tooling API: Supports development tools and custom development features
  • GraphQL API: Query multiple objects in a single request (beta)

When to Use Each API:

  • REST API: Modern integrations, mobile apps, single record operations
  • SOAP API: Enterprise systems requiring strict contracts and WSDL
  • Bulk API: Data migrations, batch processing, ETL operations
  • Streaming API: Real-time dashboards, event-driven architectures
  • Metadata API: DevOps, deployment automation, org management
  • Tooling API: IDE development, custom development tools

Example REST API Call:

// Making a REST API callout from Apex
Http http = new Http();
HttpRequest request = new HttpRequest();
request.setEndpoint('https://yourinstance.salesforce.com/services/data/v60.0/sobjects/Account');
request.setMethod('GET');
request.setHeader('Authorization', 'Bearer ' + UserInfo.getSessionId());
request.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json');

HttpResponse response = http.send(request);
if (response.getStatusCode() == 200) {
    System.debug('Success: ' + response.getBody());
}

Governor Limits:

⚠️ Callout Limits: 100 callouts per transaction (synchronous)

⚠️ Timeout: 120 seconds maximum per callout

⚠️ Total Callout Time: 120 seconds per transaction

Salesforce Edition Requirements:

  • ✅ All editions support API access
  • ❌ Essentials Edition has limited API call limits
  • ✅ Professional Edition: 1,000 API calls per 24 hours
  • ✅ Enterprise Edition: Unlimited API calls (subject to throttling)

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Q: What is the difference between synchronous and asynchronous API calls?
docs.text:
A: Synchronous and asynchronous API calls differ in their execution timing and use cases.

Key Differences:

  • Synchronous: Request waits for response before continuing execution
  • Asynchronous: Request returns immediately, processing continues in background
  • Response Time: Synchronous has immediate response, asynchronous notifies upon completion
  • Use Case: Synchronous for real-time data, asynchronous for large data volumes

Synchronous Example:

// Synchronous REST callout
@future(callout=true)
public static void syncCallout() {
    HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
    req.setEndpoint('https://api.example.com/data');
    req.setMethod('GET');

    Http http = new Http();
    HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

    // Process response immediately
    if (res.getStatusCode() == 200) {
        processData(res.getBody());
    }
}

Asynchronous Example:

// Using Queueable for asynchronous processing
public class AsyncCallout implements Queueable, Database.AllowsCallouts {
    public void execute(QueueableContext context) {
        HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
        req.setEndpoint('https://api.example.com/largedata');
        req.setMethod('GET');

        Http http = new Http();
        HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

        // Process in background
        processBulkData(res.getBody());
    }
}

// Enqueue the job
System.enqueueJob(new AsyncCallout());

When to Use Each:

  • Synchronous: User-initiated actions requiring immediate feedback
  • Asynchronous: Background processing, batch operations, non-critical updates
  • Synchronous: Validation checks, real-time data retrieval
  • Asynchronous: Data synchronization, scheduled integrations, bulk operations

Governor Limits:

⚠️ Synchronous: 10,000 ms CPU time, 6 MB heap size

⚠️ Asynchronous: 60,000 ms CPU time, 12 MB heap size

⚠️ Queueable Jobs: 50 enqueued in a single transaction

Best Practices:

✅ Use asynchronous for long-running operations

✅ Implement proper error handling for both types

✅ Consider user experience when choosing synchronous

✅ Use Platform Events for fire-and-forget scenarios

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Q: What are API rate limits and how do they work?
docs.text:
A: API rate limits control the number of API requests an organization can make within a specific timeframe to ensure platform stability.

Rate Limit Types:

  • Daily Limits: Total API calls allowed per 24-hour period
  • Concurrent Limits: Maximum simultaneous API requests
  • Per-User Limits: Limits applied to individual user sessions
  • Burst Limits: Short-term request spikes allowed

Daily API Limits by Edition:

  • Professional Edition: 1,000 calls per 24 hours
  • Enterprise Edition: Unlimited (subject to org-wide concurrent limits)
  • Unlimited Edition: Unlimited (subject to org-wide concurrent limits)
  • Developer Edition: 15,000 calls per 24 hours

Concurrent Request Limits:

  • Long-running requests (>20 seconds): 25 concurrent requests
  • Short-running requests (<20 seconds): Higher allowance, dynamically managed
  • Per-org basis: Applies across all users and integrations

Monitoring API Usage:

// Query API usage from System Overview
// Navigate to: Setup > System Overview > API Usage
// Or use REST API endpoint
GET /services/data/v60.0/limits

Example Response:

{
  "DailyApiRequests": {
    "Max": 15000,
    "Remaining": 14850,
    "Used": 150
  },
  "ConcurrentAsyncGetReportInstances": {
    "Max": 200,
    "Remaining": 200
  }
}

Handling Rate Limits:

// Implement exponential backoff
public class RateLimitHandler {
    private static final Integer MAX_RETRIES = 3;
    private static final Integer BASE_DELAY = 1000;

    public static HttpResponse makeCalloutWithRetry(HttpRequest req) {
        Http http = new Http();
        Integer retries = 0;

        while (retries < MAX_RETRIES) {
            HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

            if (res.getStatusCode() == 429) { // Too Many Requests
                Integer delay = BASE_DELAY * (Integer)Math.pow(2, retries);
                // In production, use scheduled job for delays
                retries++;
            } else {
                return res;
            }
        }
        throw new CalloutException('Max retries exceeded');
    }
}

Best Practices:

✅ Monitor API usage regularly via System Overview

✅ Implement exponential backoff for 429 errors

✅ Use Bulk API 2.0 for large data volumes

✅ Cache frequently accessed data to reduce calls

✅ Consolidate multiple operations into composite requests

Governor Limits:

⚠️ API Request Timeout: 120 seconds maximum

⚠️ Bulk API Batch Size: 10,000 records maximum per batch

⚠️ Composite API: 25 sub-requests per composite request

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Q: How do I authenticate with the Salesforce REST API?
docs.text:
A: Salesforce REST API supports multiple authentication methods depending on your integration type and security requirements.

Authentication Methods:

  • OAuth 2.0: Industry-standard protocol for secure authorization
  • Session ID: Direct authentication using Salesforce session
  • JWT Bearer Flow: Server-to-server integration without user interaction
  • SAML Bearer Flow: Enterprise SSO-based authentication

OAuth 2.0 Web Server Flow:

// Step 1: Redirect user to authorization URL
String authUrl = 'https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/authorize?' +
    'response_type=code' +
    '&client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID' +
    '&redirect_uri=YOUR_REDIRECT_URI' +
    '&scope=api refresh_token';

// Step 2: Exchange authorization code for access token
HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
req.setEndpoint('https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token');
req.setMethod('POST');
req.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded');
req.setBody(
    'grant_type=authorization_code' +
    '&code=AUTHORIZATION_CODE' +
    '&client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID' +
    '&client_secret=YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET' +
    '&redirect_uri=YOUR_REDIRECT_URI'
);

Http http = new Http();
HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

JWT Bearer Token Flow:

// Create JWT token for server-to-server auth
public class JWTBearerFlow {
    private static final String ISSUER = 'YOUR_CLIENT_ID';
    private static final String AUDIENCE = 'https://login.salesforce.com';
    private static final String SUBJECT = 'user@example.com';

    public static String getAccessToken() {
        // Create JWT header
        Map<String, String> header = new Map<String, String>{
            'alg' => 'RS256',
            'typ' => 'JWT'
        };

        // Create JWT payload
        Long now = System.now().getTime() / 1000;
        Map<String, Object> claims = new Map<String, Object>{
            'iss' => ISSUER,
            'sub' => SUBJECT,
            'aud' => AUDIENCE,
            'exp' => now + 3600
        };

        // Sign JWT with private key and exchange for access token
        String assertion = createSignedJWT(header, claims);
        return exchangeJWTForToken(assertion);
    }

    private static String exchangeJWTForToken(String assertion) {
        HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
        req.setEndpoint(AUDIENCE + '/services/oauth2/token');
        req.setMethod('POST');
        req.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded');
        req.setBody(
            'grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer' +
            '&assertion=' + assertion
        );

        Http http = new Http();
        HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

        Map<String, Object> result = (Map<String, Object>)JSON.deserializeUntyped(res.getBody());
        return (String)result.get('access_token');
    }

    private static String createSignedJWT(Map<String, String> header, Map<String, Object> claims) {
        // Implementation requires crypto library
        // Use Auth.JWT class in production
        return '';
    }
}

Using Session ID Authentication:

// Simple session-based authentication
Http http = new Http();
HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
req.setEndpoint('https://yourinstance.salesforce.com/services/data/v60.0/query?q=SELECT+Id+FROM+Account+LIMIT+10');
req.setMethod('GET');
req.setHeader('Authorization', 'Bearer ' + UserInfo.getSessionId());
req.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json');

HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

Security Best Practices:

✅ Store credentials securely in Named Credentials or Custom Settings

✅ Use OAuth 2.0 for user-facing integrations

✅ Implement token refresh logic for long-running integrations

✅ Use JWT Bearer Flow for server-to-server integrations

✅ Never hardcode credentials in code

✅ Implement proper session timeout handling

Named Credential Example:

// Using Named Credentials (recommended approach)
HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
req.setEndpoint('callout:MyNamedCredential/services/data/v60.0/sobjects/Account');
req.setMethod('GET');
// Authentication handled automatically by Named Credential

Http http = new Http();
HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

Governor Limits:

⚠️ OAuth Tokens: No limit on token generation

⚠️ Session Timeout: Configurable per org (2-24 hours)

⚠️ Refresh Token: Valid until explicitly revoked

Connected App Configuration:

  • Enable OAuth Settings in Connected App
  • Configure OAuth Scopes (api, refresh_token, etc.)
  • Add callback URLs for web server flow
  • Enable JWT Bearer Flow if needed

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Q: How do I perform CRUD operations using REST API?
docs.text:
A: Salesforce REST API provides standard HTTP methods to perform Create, Read, Update, and Delete operations on Salesforce objects.

CRUD Operations Overview:

  • Create (POST): Insert new records
  • Read (GET): Query and retrieve records
  • Update (PATCH): Modify existing records
  • Delete (DELETE): Remove records

Create Operation (POST):

// Create a new Account record
HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
req.setEndpoint('callout:MyNamedCredential/services/data/v60.0/sobjects/Account');
req.setMethod('POST');
req.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json');

Map<String, Object> accountData = new Map<String, Object>{
    'Name' => 'Acme Corporation',
    'Industry' => 'Technology',
    'Phone' => '555-1234',
    'BillingCity' => 'San Francisco'
};

req.setBody(JSON.serialize(accountData));

Http http = new Http();
HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

if (res.getStatusCode() == 201) {
    Map<String, Object> result = (Map<String, Object>)JSON.deserializeUntyped(res.getBody());
    String newAccountId = (String)result.get('id');
    System.debug('Created Account: ' + newAccountId);
}

Read Operation (GET):

// Retrieve a single record by ID
HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
req.setEndpoint('callout:MyNamedCredential/services/data/v60.0/sobjects/Account/0011234567890ABC');
req.setMethod('GET');
req.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json');

Http http = new Http();
HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

if (res.getStatusCode() == 200) {
    Map<String, Object> account = (Map<String, Object>)JSON.deserializeUntyped(res.getBody());
    String accountName = (String)account.get('Name');
    System.debug('Account Name: ' + accountName);
}

Query Multiple Records:

// Query using SOQL
String query = 'SELECT Id, Name, Industry FROM Account WHERE Industry = \'Technology\' LIMIT 10';
String encodedQuery = EncodingUtil.urlEncode(query, 'UTF-8');

HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
req.setEndpoint('callout:MyNamedCredential/services/data/v60.0/query?q=' + encodedQuery);
req.setMethod('GET');
req.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json');

Http http = new Http();
HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

if (res.getStatusCode() == 200) {
    Map<String, Object> results = (Map<String, Object>)JSON.deserializeUntyped(res.getBody());
    List<Object> records = (List<Object>)results.get('records');
    System.debug('Found ' + records.size() + ' accounts');
}

Update Operation (PATCH):

// Update existing Account record
HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
req.setEndpoint('callout:MyNamedCredential/services/data/v60.0/sobjects/Account/0011234567890ABC');
req.setMethod('PATCH');
req.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json');

Map<String, Object> updateData = new Map<String, Object>{
    'Phone' => '555-9999',
    'AnnualRevenue' => 5000000
};

req.setBody(JSON.serialize(updateData));

Http http = new Http();
HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

if (res.getStatusCode() == 204) {
    System.debug('Account updated successfully');
}

Delete Operation (DELETE):

// Delete an Account record
HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
req.setEndpoint('callout:MyNamedCredential/services/data/v60.0/sobjects/Account/0011234567890ABC');
req.setMethod('DELETE');

Http http = new Http();
HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

if (res.getStatusCode() == 204) {
    System.debug('Account deleted successfully');
}

Bulk CRUD with Composite API:

// Create multiple records in a single request
HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
req.setEndpoint('callout:MyNamedCredential/services/data/v60.0/composite/tree/Account');
req.setMethod('POST');
req.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json');

Map<String, Object> compositeRequest = new Map<String, Object>{
    'records' => new List<Object>{
        new Map<String, Object>{
            'attributes' => new Map<String, String>{'type' => 'Account', 'referenceId' => 'ref1'},
            'Name' => 'Account 1',
            'Industry' => 'Technology'
        },
        new Map<String, Object>{
            'attributes' => new Map<String, String>{'type' => 'Account', 'referenceId' => 'ref2'},
            'Name' => 'Account 2',
            'Industry' => 'Finance'
        }
    }
};

req.setBody(JSON.serialize(compositeRequest));

Http http = new Http();
HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

Error Handling:

// Robust error handling for REST API calls
public class RESTAPIHandler {
    public static void handleResponse(HttpResponse res) {
        Integer statusCode = res.getStatusCode();

        if (statusCode >= 200 && statusCode < 300) {
            System.debug('Success: ' + res.getBody());
        } else if (statusCode == 400) {
            System.debug('Bad Request: ' + res.getBody());
        } else if (statusCode == 401) {
            System.debug('Unauthorized: Check authentication');
        } else if (statusCode == 404) {
            System.debug('Not Found: Resource does not exist');
        } else if (statusCode == 429) {
            System.debug('Rate Limit Exceeded: Implement backoff');
        } else {
            System.debug('Error ' + statusCode + ': ' + res.getBody());
        }
    }
}

Best Practices:

✅ Use Named Credentials for endpoint management

✅ Implement proper error handling for all status codes

✅ Use PATCH for updates (more efficient than PUT)

✅ Validate data before making API calls

✅ Use Composite API for multiple operations

✅ Implement retry logic for transient errors

Governor Limits:

⚠️ Callout Timeout: 120 seconds maximum

⚠️ Composite API: 25 sub-requests per composite request

⚠️ Query Results: 2,000 records maximum per query

⚠️ Response Size: 6 MB maximum

HTTP Status Codes:

  • 200 OK: Successful GET request
  • 201 Created: Successful POST request
  • 204 No Content: Successful PATCH/DELETE request
  • 400 Bad Request: Invalid request data
  • 401 Unauthorized: Authentication failure
  • 404 Not Found: Resource not found
  • 429 Too Many Requests: Rate limit exceeded

docs.title: Q: What is the Composite API and when should I use it?
docs.text:
A: The Composite API allows you to execute multiple REST API requests in a single call, improving performance and reducing API call limits.

Key Features:

  • Batch Operations: Execute up to 25 sub-requests in a single call
  • Request Dependencies: Reference results from previous sub-requests
  • All-or-None: Option to rollback all operations if one fails
  • Improved Performance: Reduces network latency and API call count

Composite API Types:

  • Composite: Execute independent requests in a single call
  • Composite Batch: Similar to Composite, with all-or-none option
  • Composite Graph: Execute dependent requests with automatic ordering
  • SObject Tree: Create multiple related records in a hierarchy

Composite API Example:

// Execute multiple independent operations
HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
req.setEndpoint('callout:MyNamedCredential/services/data/v60.0/composite');
req.setMethod('POST');
req.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json');

Map<String, Object> compositeBody = new Map<String, Object>{
    'allOrNone' => false,
    'compositeRequest' => new List<Object>{
        // Create Account
        new Map<String, Object>{
            'method' => 'POST',
            'url' => '/services/data/v60.0/sobjects/Account',
            'referenceId' => 'NewAccount',
            'body' => new Map<String, Object>{
                'Name' => 'Composite Account',
                'Industry' => 'Technology'
            }
        },
        // Create Contact related to Account
        new Map<String, Object>{
            'method' => 'POST',
            'url' => '/services/data/v60.0/sobjects/Contact',
            'referenceId' => 'NewContact',
            'body' => new Map<String, Object>{
                'FirstName' => 'John',
                'LastName' => 'Doe',
                'AccountId' => '@{NewAccount.id}'  // Reference previous result
            }
        },
        // Query related records
        new Map<String, Object>{
            'method' => 'GET',
            'url' => '/services/data/v60.0/query?q=SELECT+Id,Name+FROM+Contact+WHERE+AccountId=\'@{NewAccount.id}\'',
            'referenceId' => 'QueryContacts'
        }
    }
};

req.setBody(JSON.serialize(compositeBody));

Http http = new Http();
HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

if (res.getStatusCode() == 200) {
    Map<String, Object> results = (Map<String, Object>)JSON.deserializeUntyped(res.getBody());
    List<Object> compositeResponse = (List<Object>)results.get('compositeResponse');

    for (Object response : compositeResponse) {
        Map<String, Object> subResponse = (Map<String, Object>)response;
        System.debug('Reference ID: ' + subResponse.get('referenceId'));
        System.debug('HTTP Status: ' + subResponse.get('httpStatusCode'));
    }
}

SObject Tree Example:

// Create Account with related Contacts and Opportunities
HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
req.setEndpoint('callout:MyNamedCredential/services/data/v60.0/composite/tree/Account');
req.setMethod('POST');
req.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json');

Map<String, Object> treeRequest = new Map<String, Object>{
    'records' => new List<Object>{
        new Map<String, Object>{
            'attributes' => new Map<String, String>{
                'type' => 'Account',
                'referenceId' => 'Account1'
            },
            'Name' => 'Parent Account',
            'Industry' => 'Technology',
            'Contacts' => new Map<String, Object>{
                'records' => new List<Object>{
                    new Map<String, Object>{
                        'attributes' => new Map<String, String>{
                            'type' => 'Contact',
                            'referenceId' => 'Contact1'
                        },
                        'FirstName' => 'Jane',
                        'LastName' => 'Smith'
                    }
                }
            },
            'Opportunities' => new Map<String, Object>{
                'records' => new List<Object>{
                    new Map<String, Object>{
                        'attributes' => new Map<String, String>{
                            'type' => 'Opportunity',
                            'referenceId' => 'Opp1'
                        },
                        'Name' => 'Big Deal',
                        'StageName' => 'Prospecting',
                        'CloseDate' => '2025-12-31'
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
};

req.setBody(JSON.serialize(treeRequest));

Http http = new Http();
HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

Composite Batch with All-or-None:

// All-or-none transaction behavior
HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
req.setEndpoint('callout:MyNamedCredential/services/data/v60.0/composite/batch');
req.setMethod('POST');
req.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json');

Map<String, Object> batchRequest = new Map<String, Object>{
    'haltOnError' => true,  // Rollback all on error
    'batchRequests' => new List<Object>{
        new Map<String, Object>{
            'method' => 'POST',
            'url' => '/services/data/v60.0/sobjects/Account',
            'richInput' => new Map<String, Object>{
                'Name' => 'Account 1',
                'Industry' => 'Technology'
            }
        },
        new Map<String, Object>{
            'method' => 'POST',
            'url' => '/services/data/v60.0/sobjects/Account',
            'richInput' => new Map<String, Object>{
                'Name' => 'Account 2',
                'Industry' => 'Finance'
            }
        }
    }
};

req.setBody(JSON.serialize(batchRequest));

Http http = new Http();
HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

When to Use Composite API:

  • Multiple Related Operations: Creating parent and child records together
  • Reduce API Calls: Batch multiple operations to stay within API limits
  • Transactional Requirements: Need all-or-none behavior across operations
  • Performance Optimization: Reduce network latency with fewer HTTP requests
  • Complex Workflows: Implement multi-step processes in a single call

When NOT to Use Composite API:

  • Single Operations: Individual CRUD operations are more straightforward
  • Large Data Volumes: Use Bulk API 2.0 for processing thousands of records
  • Independent Operations: When operations don't need to be grouped
  • Simple Queries: Direct query API is more efficient

Best Practices:

✅ Limit to 25 sub-requests per composite call

✅ Use reference IDs to link related operations

✅ Implement proper error handling for each sub-request

✅ Use allOrNone for transactional requirements

✅ Consider Bulk API for large data volumes

✅ Monitor API call usage saved by using Composite

Governor Limits:

⚠️ Maximum Sub-Requests: 25 per composite request

⚠️ Request Size: 5 MB maximum per composite request

⚠️ Response Size: 6 MB maximum per composite response

⚠️ SObject Tree Depth: 5 levels maximum

Performance Benefits:

  • Reduced Network Latency: Single HTTP connection vs multiple connections
  • Lower API Call Count: 1 API call instead of multiple
  • Improved Throughput: Process more operations within governor limits
  • Simplified Error Handling: Handle all responses in one place

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Q: When should I use SOAP API instead of REST API?
docs.text:
A: SOAP API is best suited for enterprise integrations requiring strict contracts, complex operations, and legacy system compatibility.

SOAP API Advantages:

  • Strict Contracts: WSDL provides formal service definition
  • Complex Operations: Supports compound operations and transactions
  • Enterprise Standards: Built-in WS-Security and reliable messaging
  • Legacy Compatibility: Works with older enterprise systems
  • Type Safety: Strong typing reduces integration errors

SOAP vs REST Comparison:

  • SOAP: XML-based, WSDL contract, enterprise-grade security
  • REST: JSON-based, lightweight, modern web/mobile applications
  • SOAP: Complex operations, describe/metadata operations
  • REST: Simple CRUD operations, stateless architecture

SOAP API Use Cases:

  • Enterprise Service Bus (ESB) integrations
  • Legacy systems requiring WSDL contracts
  • Complex business process orchestration
  • Systems requiring WS-Security standards
  • Compound operations (describe, metadata retrieval)

SOAP API Example:

<!-- SOAP Request to create Account -->
POST /services/Soap/u/60.0
Host: yourinstance.salesforce.com
Content-Type: text/xml; charset=UTF-8
SOAPAction: create

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<soapenv:Envelope xmlns:soapenv="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/"
                  xmlns:urn="urn:enterprise.soap.sforce.com">
  <soapenv:Header>
    <urn:SessionHeader>
      <urn:sessionId>YOUR_SESSION_ID</urn:sessionId>
    </urn:SessionHeader>
  </soapenv:Header>
  <soapenv:Body>
    <urn:create>
      <urn:sObjects>
        <urn:type>Account</urn:type>
        <urn:Name>Acme Corporation</urn:Name>
        <urn:Industry>Technology</urn:Industry>
      </urn:sObjects>
    </urn:create>
  </soapenv:Body>
</soapenv:Envelope>

Apex SOAP Callout Example:

// Making SOAP API call from Apex
public class SoapAPIExample {

    public static void createAccountViaSOAP() {
        String soapBody = 
            '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>' +
            '<soapenv:Envelope xmlns:soapenv="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" ' +
            'xmlns:urn="urn:enterprise.soap.sforce.com">' +
            '  <soapenv:Header>' +
            '    <urn:SessionHeader>' +
            '      <urn:sessionId>' + UserInfo.getSessionId() + '</urn:sessionId>' +
            '    </urn:SessionHeader>' +
            '  </soapenv:Header>' +
            '  <soapenv:Body>' +
            '    <urn:create>' +
            '      <urn:sObjects>' +
            '        <urn:type>Account</urn:type>' +
            '        <urn:Name>SOAP Created Account</urn:Name>' +
            '      </urn:sObjects>' +
            '    </urn:create>' +
            '  </soapenv:Body>' +
            '</soapenv:Envelope>';

        HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
        req.setEndpoint(URL.getOrgDomainUrl().toExternalForm() + '/services/Soap/u/60.0');
        req.setMethod('POST');
        req.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/xml; charset=UTF-8');
        req.setHeader('SOAPAction', 'create');
        req.setBody(soapBody);

        Http http = new Http();
        HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

        if (res.getStatusCode() == 200) {
            System.debug('SOAP Response: ' + res.getBody());
        }
    }
}

WSDL Generation:

// Generate WSDL for custom Apex web service
global class AccountWebService {

    webservice static String createAccount(String name, String industry) {
        Account acc = new Account(
            Name = name,
            Industry = industry
        );
        insert acc;
        return acc.Id;
    }

    webservice static Account getAccount(String accountId) {
        return [SELECT Id, Name, Industry FROM Account WHERE Id = :accountId];
    }
}

// Access WSDL at:
// https://yourinstance.salesforce.com/services/wsdl/class/AccountWebService

SOAP API Operations:

  • create/update/delete: Standard CRUD operations
  • query/queryMore: SOQL query execution with pagination
  • retrieve: Get records by ID
  • search: SOSL text search
  • describeSObjects: Retrieve object metadata
  • getUpdated/getDeleted: Track changes since last sync

Complex SOAP Operation Example:

<!-- Query with queryMore for pagination -->
<soapenv:Envelope xmlns:soapenv="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/"
                  xmlns:urn="urn:enterprise.soap.sforce.com">
  <soapenv:Body>
    <urn:query>
      <urn:queryString>SELECT Id, Name FROM Account WHERE Industry = 'Technology'</urn:queryString>
    </urn:query>
  </soapenv:Body>
</soapenv:Envelope>

When to Choose SOAP:

✅ Enterprise application integrations

✅ Complex operations requiring metadata

✅ Formal service contracts (WSDL) required

✅ WS-Security standards needed

✅ Legacy system compatibility

When to Choose REST:

✅ Modern web and mobile applications

✅ Simple CRUD operations

✅ JSON data format preference

✅ Lightweight, stateless architecture

✅ Higher performance requirements

Governor Limits:

⚠️ Batch Size: 200 records maximum per operation

⚠️ Query Results: queryMore required for >2,000 records

⚠️ API Calls: Count against daily API limit

⚠️ Timeout: 120 seconds maximum

Salesforce Edition Requirements:

  • ✅ All editions support SOAP API
  • ✅ API call limits vary by edition
  • ✅ Enterprise WSDL for custom objects

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Q: How do I handle large data volumes with SOAP API?
docs.text:
A: For large data volumes with SOAP API, use batch operations, queryMore for pagination, and consider Bulk API 2.0 for massive datasets.

Batch Processing with SOAP:

// Process 200 records per batch (SOAP limit)
public class SOAPBatchProcessor {

    public static void batchCreateAccounts(List<Account> accounts) {
        Integer batchSize = 200;

        for (Integer i = 0; i < accounts.size(); i += batchSize) {
            Integer endIndex = Math.min(i + batchSize, accounts.size());
            List<Account> batch = accounts.subList(i, endIndex);

            createAccountsBatch(batch);
        }
    }

    private static void createAccountsBatch(List<Account> accounts) {
        String soapBody = buildCreateBatchSOAP(accounts);

        HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
        req.setEndpoint(URL.getOrgDomainUrl().toExternalForm() + '/services/Soap/u/60.0');
        req.setMethod('POST');
        req.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/xml');
        req.setHeader('SOAPAction', 'create');
        req.setBody(soapBody);

        Http http = new Http();
        HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

        handleBatchResponse(res);
    }

    private static String buildCreateBatchSOAP(List<Account> accounts) {
        String soapBody = 
            '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>' +
            '<soapenv:Envelope xmlns:soapenv="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" ' +
            'xmlns:urn="urn:enterprise.soap.sforce.com">' +
            '  <soapenv:Header>' +
            '    <urn:SessionHeader>' +
            '      <urn:sessionId>' + UserInfo.getSessionId() + '</urn:sessionId>' +
            '    </urn:SessionHeader>' +
            '  </soapenv:Header>' +
            '  <soapenv:Body>' +
            '    <urn:create>';

        for (Account acc : accounts) {
            soapBody += 
                '      <urn:sObjects>' +
                '        <urn:type>Account</urn:type>' +
                '        <urn:Name>' + String.escapeSingleQuotes(acc.Name) + '</urn:Name>' +
                '        <urn:Industry>' + String.escapeSingleQuotes(acc.Industry) + '</urn:Industry>' +
                '      </urn:sObjects>';
        }

        soapBody += 
            '    </urn:create>' +
            '  </soapenv:Body>' +
            '</soapenv:Envelope>';

        return soapBody;
    }

    private static void handleBatchResponse(HttpResponse res) {
        // Parse response and handle errors
        if (res.getStatusCode() == 200) {
            System.debug('Batch processed successfully');
        } else {
            System.debug('Error: ' + res.getBody());
        }
    }
}

QueryMore for Large Result Sets:

// Handle large query results with queryMore
public class SOAPQueryProcessor {

    private static final Integer BATCH_SIZE = 2000;

    public static List<Account> queryAllAccounts() {
        List<Account> allAccounts = new List<Account>();
        String queryLocator = null;
        Boolean hasMore = true;

        while (hasMore) {
            Map<String, Object> result = executeQuery(queryLocator);

            List<Object> records = (List<Object>)result.get('records');
            for (Object record : records) {
                // Process each account
                allAccounts.add(parseAccount((Map<String, Object>)record));
            }

            hasMore = (Boolean)result.get('done') == false;
            queryLocator = (String)result.get('queryLocator');
        }

        return allAccounts;
    }

    private static Map<String, Object> executeQuery(String queryLocator) {
        String soapBody;

        if (queryLocator == null) {
            // Initial query
            soapBody = buildQuerySOAP('SELECT Id, Name FROM Account');
        } else {
            // QueryMore for next batch
            soapBody = buildQueryMoreSOAP(queryLocator);
        }

        HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
        req.setEndpoint(URL.getOrgDomainUrl().toExternalForm() + '/services/Soap/u/60.0');
        req.setMethod('POST');
        req.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/xml');
        req.setHeader('SOAPAction', queryLocator == null ? 'query' : 'queryMore');
        req.setBody(soapBody);

        Http http = new Http();
        HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

        return parseQueryResponse(res.getBody());
    }

    private static String buildQuerySOAP(String queryString) {
        return 
            '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>' +
            '<soapenv:Envelope xmlns:soapenv="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" ' +
            'xmlns:urn="urn:enterprise.soap.sforce.com">' +
            '  <soapenv:Header>' +
            '    <urn:SessionHeader>' +
            '      <urn:sessionId>' + UserInfo.getSessionId() + '</urn:sessionId>' +
            '    </urn:SessionHeader>' +
            '  </soapenv:Header>' +
            '  <soapenv:Body>' +
            '    <urn:query>' +
            '      <urn:queryString>' + queryString + '</urn:queryString>' +
            '    </urn:query>' +
            '  </soapenv:Body>' +
            '</soapenv:Envelope>';
    }

    private static String buildQueryMoreSOAP(String queryLocator) {
        return 
            '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>' +
            '<soapenv:Envelope xmlns:soapenv="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" ' +
            'xmlns:urn="urn:enterprise.soap.sforce.com">' +
            '  <soapenv:Header>' +
            '    <urn:SessionHeader>' +
            '      <urn:sessionId>' + UserInfo.getSessionId() + '</urn:sessionId>' +
            '    </urn:SessionHeader>' +
            '  </soapenv:Header>' +
            '  <soapenv:Body>' +
            '    <urn:queryMore>' +
            '      <urn:queryLocator>' + queryLocator + '</urn:queryLocator>' +
            '    </urn:queryMore>' +
            '  </soapenv:Body>' +
            '</soapenv:Envelope>';
    }

    private static Map<String, Object> parseQueryResponse(String xmlResponse) {
        // Parse XML response (simplified)
        // In production, use DOM or XMLStreamReader
        return new Map<String, Object>{
            'records' => new List<Object>(),
            'done' => true,
            'queryLocator' => null
        };
    }

    private static Account parseAccount(Map<String, Object> record) {
        Account acc = new Account();
        acc.Id = (String)record.get('Id');
        acc.Name = (String)record.get('Name');
        return acc;
    }
}

When to Use Bulk API Instead:

  • Volume: More than 10,000 records
  • Performance: Need parallel processing
  • Asynchronous: Can process in background
  • Complex Operations: Multiple object types

Bulk API 2.0 Example:

// For large volumes, use Bulk API 2.0
public class BulkAPIExample {

    public static void bulkCreateAccounts(List<Account> accounts) {
        // Create job
        HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
        req.setEndpoint('callout:MyNamedCredential/services/data/v60.0/jobs/ingest');
        req.setMethod('POST');
        req.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json');

        Map<String, String> jobRequest = new Map<String, String>{
            'operation' => 'insert',
            'object' => 'Account',
            'contentType' => 'CSV',
            'lineEnding' => 'LF'
        };

        req.setBody(JSON.serialize(jobRequest));

        Http http = new Http();
        HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

        if (res.getStatusCode() == 200) {
            Map<String, Object> job = (Map<String, Object>)JSON.deserializeUntyped(res.getBody());
            String jobId = (String)job.get('id');

            // Upload CSV data
            uploadBulkData(jobId, accounts);

            // Close job to start processing
            closeBulkJob(jobId);
        }
    }

    private static void uploadBulkData(String jobId, List<Account> accounts) {
        // Convert accounts to CSV
        String csvData = convertToCSV(accounts);

        HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
        req.setEndpoint('callout:MyNamedCredential/services/data/v60.0/jobs/ingest/' + jobId + '/batches');
        req.setMethod('PUT');
        req.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/csv');
        req.setBody(csvData);

        Http http = new Http();
        http.send(req);
    }

    private static void closeBulkJob(String jobId) {
        HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
        req.setEndpoint('callout:MyNamedCredential/services/data/v60.0/jobs/ingest/' + jobId);
        req.setMethod('PATCH');
        req.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json');
        req.setBody('{"state":"UploadComplete"}');

        Http http = new Http();
        http.send(req);
    }

    private static String convertToCSV(List<Account> accounts) {
        String csv = 'Name,Industry\n';
        for (Account acc : accounts) {
            csv += acc.Name + ',' + acc.Industry + '\n';
        }
        return csv;
    }
}

Best Practices:

✅ Use SOAP API batch size of 200 records maximum

✅ Implement queryMore for results over 2,000 records

✅ Switch to Bulk API 2.0 for volumes over 10,000 records

✅ Process batches asynchronously when possible

✅ Implement proper error handling per batch

✅ Monitor API call consumption

Governor Limits:

⚠️ SOAP Batch Size: 200 records maximum per operation

⚠️ Query Results: 2,000 records per query call

⚠️ QueryMore: Required for additional records

⚠️ Bulk API 2.0: 150 million records per 24 hours

Performance Comparison:

  • SOAP API: 200 records/batch, synchronous processing
  • Bulk API 2.0: 10,000 records/batch, parallel processing
  • SOAP: Best for <10,000 records
  • Bulk: Best for >10,000 records
