docs.title: Q: What is the relationship between CPQ and Opportunity in Salesforce?
docs.text:
A: CPQ Quotes are created from Opportunities and maintain a parent-child relationship where the Opportunity represents the overall sales deal and CPQ Quotes contain the detailed product configuration and pricing.

Quote-Opportunity Relationship:

  • One-to-Many: One Opportunity can have multiple Quotes
  • Primary Quote: One Quote can be designated as the Primary Quote
  • Synced Quote: The Primary Quote syncs its products and amounts to the Opportunity
  • Quote Lines: Automatically create or update Opportunity Products when synced

Workflow:

  • Create Opportunity in Sales Cloud
  • Click "New Quote" from Opportunity
  • Configure products in CPQ
  • Set Quote as Primary
  • Quote Line Items sync to Opportunity Products
  • Opportunity Amount updates from Quote

Key Fields Synced:

  • Total Amount: Quote total syncs to Opportunity Amount
  • Products: Quote Lines sync to Opportunity Products
  • Close Date: Can sync from Quote to Opportunity
  • Status: Quote status affects Opportunity stage

Example Configuration:

// Query Opportunity with Primary Quote
List<Opportunity> opps = [
    SELECT Id, Name, Amount, 
           (SELECT Id, SBQQ__Primary__c, SBQQ__NetAmount__c 
            FROM SBQQ__Quotes__r 
            WHERE SBQQ__Primary__c = true)
    FROM Opportunity
    WHERE Id = :oppId
];

if (!opps.isEmpty() && !opps[0].SBQQ__Quotes__r.isEmpty()) {
    SBQQ__Quote__c primaryQuote = opps[0].SBQQ__Quotes__r[0];
    System.debug('Primary Quote Amount: ' + primaryQuote.SBQQ__NetAmount__c);
}

Best Practices:

  • ✅ Always designate one Quote as Primary
  • ✅ Keep Quote and Opportunity stages aligned
  • ✅ Use Quote Line Editor for product changes
  • ✅ Enable quote sync to maintain data consistency
  • ❌ Avoid editing Opportunity Products directly when using CPQ

Governor Limits:

  • ⚠️ Maximum 2,000 Quote Lines per Quote
  • ⚠️ Quote calculations subject to standard CPU time limits
  • ⚠️ Large Quotes may require asynchronous processing

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Q: What are the key objects in the CPQ data model?
docs.text:
A: The CPQ data model consists of several custom objects that work together to enable product configuration, pricing, and quote generation.

Core CPQ Objects:

Quote Objects:

  • SBQQ__Quote__c: Master quote record containing customer, dates, and terms
  • SBQQ__QuoteLine__c: Individual products added to the quote
  • SBQQ__QuoteLineGroup__c: Grouping mechanism for quote lines

Product Objects:

  • Product2: Standard Salesforce product (shared with Sales Cloud)
  • SBQQ__Product__c: CPQ-enhanced product with configuration options
  • SBQQ__ProductOption__c: Defines optional or required features
  • SBQQ__ProductFeature__c: Feature sets for product configuration

Pricing Objects:

  • SBQQ__PriceRule__c: Automated pricing calculations
  • SBQQ__PriceCondition__c: Conditions that trigger price rules
  • SBQQ__PriceAction__c: Actions executed by price rules
  • SBQQ__DiscountSchedule__c: Volume-based discount tiers
  • SBQQ__PriceBook__c: Custom price books (extends standard PriceBook2)

Configuration Objects:

  • SBQQ__ProductRule__c: Configuration rules and validations
  • SBQQ__ConfigurationAttribute__c: Dynamic product attributes
  • SBQQ__OptionConstraint__c: Dependencies between product options

Contract & Subscription Objects:

  • Contract: Standard Salesforce contract
  • SBQQ__Subscription__c: Subscription records for recurring revenue
  • Asset: Standard asset records for installed products
  • SBQQ__ContractedPrice__c: Customer-specific contracted pricing

Object Relationships:

Key Relationships:

  • Quote → Quote Lines (Master-Detail)
  • Quote Line → Product (Lookup)
  • Quote → Opportunity (Lookup)
  • Product Option → Product (Lookup)
  • Price Rule → Price Conditions and Price Actions
  • Subscription → Quote Line (Lookup)

Example Query with Relationships:

// Query Quote with all related data
List<SBQQ__Quote__c> quotes = [
    SELECT Id, Name, SBQQ__Account__c, SBQQ__Opportunity2__c,
           SBQQ__NetAmount__c, SBQQ__Primary__c,
           (SELECT Id, SBQQ__Product__c, SBQQ__ProductName__c,
                   SBQQ__Quantity__c, SBQQ__NetPrice__c,
                   SBQQ__Discount__c, SBQQ__NetTotal__c
            FROM SBQQ__LineItems__r
            ORDER BY SBQQ__Number__c)
    FROM SBQQ__Quote__c
    WHERE SBQQ__Opportunity2__c = :oppId
    AND SBQQ__Primary__c = true
    LIMIT 1
];

Data Storage Considerations:

  • ⚠️ Quote Lines can grow large (watch heap size in triggers)
  • ⚠️ Price Rules execute on every quote calculation
  • ⚠️ Custom pricing logic should be optimized for bulk operations

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Q: How do you set up a product bundle in Salesforce CPQ?
docs.text:
A: Product bundles allow you to sell groups of products together with parent-child relationships and configuration options.

Bundle Components:

  • Parent Product: The main product that customers select
  • Product Options: Child products that can be added to the bundle
  • Product Features: Logical groupings of options
  • Configuration Attributes: Dynamic fields for customization

Setup Steps:

Step 1: Create the Parent Product

  • Create Product2 record
  • Mark as "Component" = false
  • Set "Has Configuration Attributes" if needed
  • Define pricing model (one-time or subscription)

Step 2: Create Child Products

  • Create Product2 records for each component
  • Mark as "Component" = true (optional)
  • Set individual pricing

Step 3: Create Product Features (Optional)

  • Create SBQQ__ProductFeature__c records
  • Group related options together
  • Set feature type (Required, Optional)
  • Define min/max selections

Step 4: Create Product Options

  • Create SBQQ__ProductOption__c records
  • Link to parent product (Configured SKU)
  • Link to child product (Optional SKU)
  • Set quantity behavior
  • Define if option is required

Example Bundle Structure:

Parent: Cloud Storage Bundle
├── Feature: Storage Capacity (Required, select 1)
│   ├── Option: 100 GB Storage
│   ├── Option: 500 GB Storage
│   └── Option: 1 TB Storage
├── Feature: Additional Services (Optional, select multiple)
│   ├── Option: Data Backup Service
│   ├── Option: Enhanced Security
│   └── Option: 24/7 Support
└── Feature: User Licenses (Required)
    └── Option: User License (Quantity editable)

Product Option Configuration:

// Example: Create Product Option programmatically
SBQQ__ProductOption__c option = new SBQQ__ProductOption__c(
    SBQQ__ConfiguredSKU__c = parentProductId,  // Parent Product
    SBQQ__OptionalSKU__c = childProductId,     // Child Product
    SBQQ__Number__c = 10,                      // Display order
    SBQQ__Quantity__c = 1,                     // Default quantity
    SBQQ__Type__c = 'Component',               // Option type
    SBQQ__Required__c = true,                  // Is required
    SBQQ__Selected__c = true,                  // Pre-selected
    SBQQ__Feature__c = featureId               // Feature grouping
);
insert option;

Bundle Types:

  • Static Bundle: Fixed components, no configuration needed
  • Configurable Bundle: Customer selects from options
  • Dynamic Bundle: Options based on attributes or rules

Configuration Rules:

// Product Rule to enforce bundle logic
// Type: Validation
// Error Message: "Must select at least one storage option"
// Evaluation Event: Save
// Active: true

// Configuration Rule example (Setup in CPQ UI):
// Condition: Storage Feature has no selections
// Action: Show error message

Best Practices:

  • ✅ Use Product Features to organize complex bundles
  • ✅ Set appropriate min/max selection limits
  • ✅ Use Option Constraints for dependencies
  • ✅ Test bundle configuration in Quote Line Editor
  • ✅ Document bundle structure for sales team
  • ❌ Avoid overly complex nested bundles (performance)

Common Bundle Patterns:

  • Good-Better-Best: Tiered service packages
  • Base + Add-ons: Core product with optional features
  • Hardware + Software: Physical products with licenses
  • Subscription Tiers: Different service levels

Governor Limits:

  • ⚠️ No hard limit on Product Options per Product
  • ⚠️ Complex bundles can increase quote calculation time
  • ⚠️ Watch for CPU timeout on large quote calculations

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Q: How do Product Rules work in Salesforce CPQ?
docs.text:
A: Product Rules are automation tools that guide product configuration, validate selections, display alerts, and dynamically adjust products based on conditions.

Product Rule Types:

Validation Rules:

  • Enforce business logic during configuration
  • Prevent invalid product combinations
  • Display error messages to users
  • Block quote save until resolved

Selection Rules:

  • Automatically add/remove products
  • Configure based on criteria
  • Streamline configuration process
  • Pre-select recommended options

Alert Rules:

  • Display warning messages
  • Provide guidance without blocking
  • Inform users of considerations
  • Don't prevent quote save

Filter Rules:

  • Control which products are visible
  • Simplify product selection
  • Reduce configuration complexity
  • Hide irrelevant options

Product Rule Components:

Configuration Rule (SBQQ__ProductRule__c):

  • Type: Validation, Selection, Alert, or Filter
  • Scope: Product or Quote
  • Evaluation Event: Edit, Save, Always, Load
  • Error Message: Displayed for Validation/Alert rules
  • Active: Enable/disable rule

Error Conditions (SBQQ__ErrorCondition__c):

  • Define when rule triggers
  • Can be positive or negative logic
  • Support multiple conditions with AND/OR
  • Reference product fields or quote fields

Configuration (SBQQ__Configuration__c):

  • Links condition to product rule
  • Defines which products rule applies to
  • Multiple configurations per rule

Product Actions (SBQQ__ProductAction__c):

  • Add, remove, show, or hide products
  • Set quantities or field values
  • Execute when conditions are met

Example Validation Rule:

Rule Name: Require Support for Enterprise Plan
Type: Validation
Scope: Product
Evaluation Event: Save
Active: true
Error Message: "Enterprise Plan requires Premium Support. Please add Premium Support to continue."

Error Condition:
- Product: Enterprise Plan (Code: ENT-001)
- Tested Object: Product Option
- Tested Field: Selected
- Operator: Equals
- Filter Value: true

Configuration:
- Configuration Type: Required
- Tested Product: Enterprise Plan

Product Action:
- Type: Show Message (implicit via validation type)

Example Selection Rule:

Rule Name: Auto-Add Installation for Hardware
Type: Selection
Scope: Product
Evaluation Event: Edit
Active: true

Error Condition:
- Product Family: Hardware
- Tested Object: Quote Line
- Tested Field: Product Family
- Operator: Equals
- Filter Value: Hardware

Product Action:
- Type: Add
- Product: Installation Service (SKU: INST-001)
- Quantity: 1
- Required: false

Complex Rule Example with Code Context:

// Product Rule Evaluation (CPQ does this automatically)
// This shows the conceptual logic, not actual implementation

// Validation Rule: Prevent incompatible products
if (hasProduct('Product A') && hasProduct('Product B')) {
    throw new ValidationException(
        'Product A and Product B cannot be sold together.'
    );
}

// Selection Rule: Auto-bundle related products
if (hasProduct('Security Software')) {
    if (!hasProduct('Antivirus Module')) {
        autoAddProduct('Antivirus Module', quantity: 1);
    }
}

// Filter Rule: Show only compatible options
if (selectedHardware == 'Windows') {
    hideProducts(productFamily: 'Mac Software');
}

Rule Evaluation Order:

  • Load Rules → Edit Rules → Save Rules → Always Rules
  • Multiple rules evaluated in sequence
  • Earlier rules can affect later rule evaluation

Testing Product Rules:

// Test Product Rule behavior
@isTest
private class ProductRuleTest {
    @isTest
    static void testValidationRule() {
        // Setup: Create test products and quote
        Product2 entPlan = new Product2(
            Name = 'Enterprise Plan',
            ProductCode = 'ENT-001'
        );
        insert entPlan;

        // Create quote and add product
        SBQQ__Quote__c quote = TestDataFactory.createQuote();
        SBQQ__QuoteLine__c quoteLine = new SBQQ__QuoteLine__c(
            SBQQ__Quote__c = quote.Id,
            SBQQ__Product__c = entPlan.Id,
            SBQQ__Quantity__c = 1
        );

        // Test: Try to save without required support
        Test.startTest();
        try {
            insert quoteLine;
            // If rule works, this should fail
            System.assert(false, 'Expected validation error');
        } catch (Exception e) {
            System.assert(
                e.getMessage().contains('requires Premium Support'),
                'Expected rule error message'
            );
        }
        Test.stopTest();
    }
}

Best Practices:

  • ✅ Test rules thoroughly before deploying to production
  • ✅ Use clear, user-friendly error messages
  • ✅ Document complex rule logic
  • ✅ Consider rule evaluation order
  • ✅ Use Alert rules for warnings, Validation for errors
  • ✅ Keep rules simple when possible
  • ❌ Avoid circular dependencies between rules
  • ❌ Don't create too many rules (performance impact)

Common Use Cases:

  • Enforce product dependencies
  • Prevent incompatible combinations
  • Auto-bundle complementary products
  • Ensure regulatory compliance
  • Guide users through configuration
  • Implement business policies

Troubleshooting:

  • Use CPQ Debug Logs to trace rule execution
  • Check Evaluation Event setting
  • Verify Error Conditions are configured correctly
  • Test with different product combinations
  • Review Scope (Product vs Quote)

Governor Limits:

  • ⚠️ No specific limit on Product Rules
  • ⚠️ Complex rules increase CPU time
  • ⚠️ Too many rules can cause timeout issues
  • ⚠️ Test performance with realistic quote sizes

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Q: What are Configuration Attributes and how are they used?
docs.text:
A: Configuration Attributes are custom fields that appear during product configuration, allowing dynamic customization of products and quote lines based on user input.

Configuration Attribute Basics:

  • Custom fields that appear in the configurator
  • Capture additional information during configuration
  • Drive pricing, product selection, or quote behavior
  • Can be required or optional
  • Support various data types

Configuration Attribute Types:

Set Automatically:

  • Values calculated by formulas or rules
  • Not directly editable by users
  • Used for backend calculations

Enter Manually:

  • User provides value during configuration
  • Most common type
  • Can be used in formulas and rules

Hidden:

  • Not displayed to users
  • Used for calculations or rule logic
  • Set by automation

Configuration Attribute Setup:

Field Setup:
- Object: SBQQ__ProductOption__c or SBQQ__QuoteLine__c
- Type: Custom field (Text, Number, Picklist, Date, etc.)
- Configuration Attribute record created
- Display Order: Controls sequence in configurator
- Column Order: Controls position (Feature or Configuration)

Example Use Cases:

Custom Text Input:

Product: Custom Sign
Configuration Attribute: Company Name
Type: Text (80)
Apply To: Product Option
Target Field: SBQQ__QuoteLine__c.Company_Name__c
Feature: Customization Options
Display Order: 10
Required: true

Dynamic Calculation:

Product: Cloud Hosting
Configuration Attribute: Expected Users
Type: Number
Apply To: Product Option
Target Field: SBQQ__QuoteLine__c.Expected_Users__c
Feature: Sizing
Display Order: 10

// Price Rule uses this to calculate price
// If Expected_Users__c > 100, add $500
// If Expected_Users__c > 500, add $2000

Conditional Display:

Product: Software License
Configuration Attribute: Deployment Type
Type: Picklist (Cloud, On-Premise, Hybrid)
Apply To: Product Option
Target Field: SBQQ__QuoteLine__c.Deployment_Type__c

// Product Rule shows different options based on selection
// Cloud: Shows "Cloud Support" options
// On-Premise: Shows "Installation Service" options

Implementation Example:

// Custom field on Quote Line
SBQQ__QuoteLine__c.Number_of_Locations__c (Number, 0 decimal places)

// Configuration Attribute record
SBQQ__ConfigurationAttribute__c attr = new SBQQ__ConfigurationAttribute__c(
    SBQQ__Product__c = productId,
    SBQQ__TargetField__c = 'SBQQ__QuoteLine__c.Number_of_Locations__c',
    SBQQ__DisplayOrder__c = 10,
    SBQQ__ColumnOrder__c = 10,
    SBQQ__Feature__c = featureId,
    SBQQ__Required__c = true,
    SBQQ__AppliedImmediately__c = true,
    SBQQ__ApplyToProductOptions__c = false,
    Name = 'Number of Locations'
);

// Price Rule based on attribute
SBQQ__PriceRule__c priceRule = new SBQQ__PriceRule__c(
    Name = 'Multi-Location Pricing',
    SBQQ__Active__c = true,
    SBQQ__EvaluationOrder__c = 10
);

// Price Condition
SBQQ__PriceCondition__c condition = new SBQQ__PriceCondition__c(
    SBQQ__Rule__c = priceRule.Id,
    SBQQ__Field__c = 'Number_of_Locations__c',
    SBQQ__Operator__c = 'greater than',
    SBQQ__Value__c = '1'
);

// Price Action: Add $100 per additional location
SBQQ__PriceAction__c action = new SBQQ__PriceAction__c(
    SBQQ__Rule__c = priceRule.Id,
    SBQQ__Field__c = 'SBQQ__ListPrice__c',
    SBQQ__Formula__c = 'SBQQ__ListPrice__c + ((Number_of_Locations__c - 1) * 100)'
);

Using Attributes in Formulas:

// Formula field on Quote Line
// Calculate total based on configuration attribute

// Custom Formula: Extended_Price__c
SBQQ__Quantity__c * SBQQ__NetPrice__c * 
IF(Deployment_Type__c = "On-Premise", 1.15, 1.0)

// 15% markup for on-premise deployments

Integration with Product Rules:

// Product Rule: Show Installation Option for On-Premise
Error Condition:
- Tested Field: Deployment_Type__c
- Operator: equals
- Value: On-Premise

Product Action:
- Type: Show
- Product: Installation Service
- Required: true

Configuration Attribute Settings:

Apply Immediately:

  • Recalculate quote when value changes
  • Updates pricing in real-time
  • Use for values that affect price

Apply to Product Options:

  • Attribute flows down to selected options
  • Useful for bundle-wide settings
  • Avoids re-entering same data

Position:

  • Feature Column: Shows with product features
  • Configuration Column: Separate configuration section
  • Affects user experience

Best Practices:

  • ✅ Use descriptive attribute names
  • ✅ Provide help text for user guidance
  • ✅ Set appropriate validation rules
  • ✅ Test in Quote Line Editor before deployment
  • ✅ Document attribute business logic
  • ✅ Use picklists instead of text when possible
  • ❌ Don't create too many required attributes
  • ❌ Avoid complex nested dependencies

Common Patterns:

Sizing Calculator:

Attributes: Number of Users, Data Volume GB, API Calls/Day
Formula: Calculate recommended SKU tier
Outcome: Auto-select appropriate product tier

Customization Options:

Attributes: Logo Upload, Color Scheme, Custom Text
Target: Quote Line custom fields
Outcome: Pass customization to fulfillment

Service Level Selection:

Attribute: SLA Level (Picklist: Standard, Premium, Enterprise)
Impact: Shows appropriate support products
Impact: Adjusts pricing via Price Rules

Troubleshooting:

  • Verify Target Field exists on Quote Line
  • Check Apply Immediately setting for real-time updates
  • Ensure field API names match exactly
  • Test with different attribute combinations
  • Review debug logs for formula errors

Performance Considerations:

  • ⚠️ Each attribute adds to quote calculation time
  • ⚠️ Complex formulas can slow configurator
  • ⚠️ Minimize number of attributes when possible
  • ⚠️ Test with large quotes to check performance

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Q: How does pricing hierarchy work in Salesforce CPQ?
docs.text:
A: CPQ uses a multi-tier pricing hierarchy that determines the final price for quote line items, starting from list price and applying various pricing methods in sequence.

Pricing Hierarchy (in order):

List Price:

  • Base price from Price Book
  • Starting point for all calculations
  • Can vary by price book and currency

Cost:

  • Product cost (if tracked)
  • Used for margin calculations
  • Optional field

Customer Price:

  • Special pricing for specific customers
  • Stored in Contracted Price object
  • Overrides list price

Partner Price:

  • Pricing for partner/channel deals
  • Partner-specific discounts
  • Distribution channel pricing

Price Rules:

  • Automated pricing calculations
  • Volume discounts, promotions, bundles
  • Most flexible pricing method

Discount Schedule:

  • Tiered discount based on quantity
  • Automatic application
  • Volume-based pricing

Manual Discount:

  • Sales rep applies discount
  • Can be percentage or amount
  • Subject to approval workflows

Final Net Price:

  • Calculated after all adjustments
  • What customer actually pays
  • Shown on quote and proposal

Price Calculation Flow:

Price Calculation Example:

Product: Cloud Storage - Premium Tier
List Price: $100/month
Quantity: 50 licenses

Step 1 - List Price: $100
Step 2 - Customer Price: Not applicable
Step 3 - Price Rule (Volume Discount): 
        IF Quantity >= 50 THEN ListPrice * 0.85
        New Price: $85
Step 4 - Discount Schedule: 
        50-99 units = 5% off
        Applied to: $85 * 0.95 = $80.75
Step 5 - Manual Discount: 5% additional discount
        Applied to: $80.75 * 0.95 = $76.71

Final Net Price: $76.71/month
Total Quote Line: $76.71 * 50 = $3,835.50/month

Key Price Fields on Quote Line:

// Important pricing fields
SBQQ__QuoteLine__c quoteLine = [
    SELECT 
        SBQQ__ListPrice__c,           // Base list price
        SBQQ__CustomerPrice__c,       // Special customer price
        SBQQ__PartnerPrice__c,        // Partner/channel price
        SBQQ__RegularPrice__c,        // After price rules, before discounts
        SBQQ__SpecialPrice__c,        // After discount schedule
        SBQQ__Discount__c,            // Discount percentage
        SBQQ__AdditionalDiscountAmount__c, // Additional discount $
        SBQQ__NetPrice__c,            // Final unit price
        SBQQ__NetTotal__c,            // Final line total
        SBQQ__CustomerTotal__c,       // Total customer pays
        SBQQ__PriceEditable__c        // Can user edit price?
    FROM SBQQ__QuoteLine__c
    WHERE SBQQ__Quote__c = :quoteId
];

Price Book Hierarchy:

Standard Price Book (Salesforce standard)
    └── Custom Price Book 1 (US Dollars)
        └── Custom Price Book 2 (US - Government)
            └── Custom Price Book 3 (US - Gov - Agency A)

Contracted Pricing:

// Create contracted price for customer
SBQQ__ContractedPrice__c contractPrice = new SBQQ__ContractedPrice__c(
    SBQQ__Account__c = accountId,
    SBQQ__Product__c = productId,
    SBQQ__Price__c = 85.00,            // Special price
    SBQQ__EffectiveDate__c = Date.today(),
    SBQQ__ExpirationDate__c = Date.today().addYears(1),
    SBQQ__Discount__c = 15.0            // 15% off list
);
insert contractPrice;

// This price will automatically apply when:
// - Account matches
// - Product matches
// - Current date within effective dates

Price Waterfall Report:

// Generate price waterfall for analysis
Map<String, Decimal> priceWaterfall = new Map<String, Decimal>{
    'List Price' => quoteLine.SBQQ__ListPrice__c,
    'Customer Price' => quoteLine.SBQQ__CustomerPrice__c,
    'Regular Price' => quoteLine.SBQQ__RegularPrice__c,
    'Special Price' => quoteLine.SBQQ__SpecialPrice__c,
    'Net Price' => quoteLine.SBQQ__NetPrice__c
};

Decimal totalDiscount = quoteLine.SBQQ__ListPrice__c - 
                       quoteLine.SBQQ__NetPrice__c;
Decimal discountPercent = (totalDiscount / quoteLine.SBQQ__ListPrice__c) * 100;

System.debug('Total Discount: ' + totalDiscount);
System.debug('Discount %: ' + discountPercent);

Best Practices:

  • ✅ Document pricing strategy clearly
  • ✅ Use Price Rules for automatic discounts
  • ✅ Reserve manual discounts for special cases
  • ✅ Set up approval processes for large discounts
  • ✅ Test pricing with various scenarios
  • ✅ Maintain price books regularly
  • ✅ Use contracted prices for key accounts
  • ❌ Don't allow unlimited manual discounts
  • ❌ Avoid overly complex price rule chains

Pricing Strategies:

Cost-Plus Pricing:

Cost: $50
Markup: 40%
List Price: $70
Net Price after discounts: $63
Margin: $13 (20.6%)

Value-Based Pricing:

Customer Value: $500
List Price: $200 (40% of value)
Volume Discount: -15%
Net Price: $170

Competitive Pricing:

Competitor Price: $120
List Price: $115 (undercut by 5%)
Quality Premium: +$10
Net Price: $125

Governor Limits:

  • ⚠️ Price Rule execution counts toward CPU time
  • ⚠️ Complex pricing can cause timeouts
  • ⚠️ Large discount schedules impact performance
  • ⚠️ Optimize price rules for efficiency

docs.title: Q: How do you create and configure Price Rules in Salesforce CPQ?
docs.text:
A: Price Rules automate pricing calculations by evaluating conditions and executing actions to adjust prices, add products, or update fields on quote lines.

Price Rule Components:

SBQQ__PriceRule__c (Main Rule):

  • Name: Descriptive rule name
  • Active: Enable/disable rule
  • Evaluation Order: Sequence of execution (lower runs first)
  • Evaluation Scope: Calculator or Configurator
  • Conditions Met: All or Any conditions must be true
  • Calculator Evaluation Event: Before Calculate, On Calculate
  • Configurator Evaluation Event: Before Load, On Load, Edit, Save

SBQQ__PriceCondition__c (When):

  • Defines when rule should fire
  • Tests field values on Quote, Quote Line, or related objects
  • Multiple conditions linked by AND/OR logic
  • Supports standard operators (equals, greater than, etc.)

SBQQ__PriceAction__c (Then):

  • Defines what happens when conditions are met
  • Can update prices, set fields, or perform calculations
  • Uses formulas for complex calculations
  • Multiple actions can execute per rule

Price Rule Example - Volume Discount:

Rule Name: Volume Discount - 50+ Units
Active: true
Evaluation Order: 10
Evaluation Scope: Calculator
Conditions Met: All

Price Condition:
- Object: Quote Line
- Field: Quantity
- Operator: greater or equal
- Value: 50

Price Action:
- Target Object: Quote Line
- Target Field: Discount (%)
- Type: Custom
- Value: 15

Result: Apply 15% discount when quantity >= 50

Complex Price Rule with Formula:

Rule Name: Tiered Volume Pricing
Active: true
Evaluation Order: 20

Price Condition 1:
- Field: Quantity
- Operator: greater or equal
- Value: 10

Price Action:
- Target Field: List Price
- Type: Custom
- Formula: 
  IF(Quantity >= 100, ListPrice * 0.70,
     IF(Quantity >= 50, ListPrice * 0.80,
        IF(Quantity >= 10, ListPrice * 0.90, ListPrice)))

Result: 
- 10-49 units: 10% discount
- 50-99 units: 20% discount  
- 100+ units: 30% discount

Price Rule for Bundle Adjustment:

Rule Name: Bundle Discount
Active: true
Evaluation Scope: Calculator

Price Condition 1:
- Field: Product Code
- Operator: equals
- Value: BUNDLE-001

Price Condition 2:
- Field: Quote.Line Count
- Operator: greater or equal
- Value: 5

Price Action:
- Target Field: Additional Discount (%)
- Value: 10

Result: 10% additional discount when bundle has 5+ products

Summary Variable Price Rule:

Rule Name: Apply Account Discount Level
Active: true
Evaluation Order: 5

Price Condition:
- Field: Quote.Account.Discount_Level__c
- Operator: not equals
- Value: null

Price Action:
- Target Field: Discount (%)
- Type: Custom  
- Formula: Quote.Account.Discount_Level__c

Result: Apply account-level discount to all quote lines

Price Rule Code Representation:

// This is conceptual - CPQ handles automatically
public class PriceRuleEngine {

    public void evaluatePriceRules(SBQQ__Quote__c quote) {
        // Get active price rules in evaluation order
        List<SBQQ__PriceRule__c> rules = [
            SELECT Id, Name, SBQQ__EvaluationOrder__c,
                   (SELECT Id, SBQQ__Field__c, SBQQ__Operator__c, 
                           SBQQ__Value__c 
                    FROM SBQQ__PriceConditions__r),
                   (SELECT Id, SBQQ__Field__c, SBQQ__Formula__c,
                           SBQQ__ValueField__c
                    FROM SBQQ__PriceActions__r)
            FROM SBQQ__PriceRule__c
            WHERE SBQQ__Active__c = true
            ORDER BY SBQQ__EvaluationOrder__c
        ];

        for (SBQQ__PriceRule__c rule : rules) {
            if (evaluateConditions(rule, quote)) {
                executeActions(rule, quote);
            }
        }
    }

    private Boolean evaluateConditions(
        SBQQ__PriceRule__c rule, 
        SBQQ__Quote__c quote
    ) {
        // Evaluate each condition
        for (SBQQ__PriceCondition__c condition : 
             rule.SBQQ__PriceConditions__r) {
            // Check condition logic
            Boolean conditionMet = checkCondition(condition, quote);
            if (!conditionMet && rule.SBQQ__ConditionsMet__c == 'All') {
                return false; // All conditions required
            }
        }
        return true;
    }

    private void executeActions(
        SBQQ__PriceRule__c rule,
        SBQQ__Quote__c quote
    ) {
        // Execute each action
        for (SBQQ__PriceAction__c action : 
             rule.SBQQ__PriceActions__r) {
            applyPriceAction(action, quote);
        }
    }
}

Testing Price Rules:

@isTest
private class PriceRuleTest {

    @isTest
    static void testVolumeDiscount() {
        // Setup
        Product2 product = TestDataFactory.createProduct();
        SBQQ__Quote__c quote = TestDataFactory.createQuote();

        // Create quote line with quantity >= 50
        SBQQ__QuoteLine__c quoteLine = new SBQQ__QuoteLine__c(
            SBQQ__Quote__c = quote.Id,
            SBQQ__Product__c = product.Id,
            SBQQ__Quantity__c = 60,
            SBQQ__ListPrice__c = 100
        );
        insert quoteLine;

        // Calculate quote
        Test.startTest();
        SBQQ.TriggerControl.disable();
        QuoteCalculator.calculate(quote.Id);
        Test.stopTest();

        // Verify: 15% discount applied
        quoteLine = [
            SELECT SBQQ__Discount__c, SBQQ__NetPrice__c
            FROM SBQQ__QuoteLine__c
            WHERE Id = :quoteLine.Id
        ];

        System.assertEquals(15, quoteLine.SBQQ__Discount__c,
            'Volume discount should be 15%');
        System.assertEquals(85, quoteLine.SBQQ__NetPrice__c,
            'Net price should reflect discount');
    }

    @isTest
    static void testBundleDiscount() {
        // Test bundle pricing logic
        // Similar structure to above
    }
}

Price Rule Best Practices:

  • ✅ Use clear, descriptive rule names
  • ✅ Set evaluation order strategically (lower = earlier)
  • ✅ Test rules with various scenarios
  • ✅ Document complex formulas
  • ✅ Use conditions to limit rule execution
  • ✅ Monitor rule performance (CPU time)
  • ✅ Keep formulas simple when possible
  • ❌ Don't create circular rule dependencies
  • ❌ Avoid too many overlapping rules
  • ❌ Don't modify system fields unless necessary

Common Price Rule Patterns:

Early Payment Discount:

Condition: Payment Terms = "Net 15"
Action: Additional Discount = 2%

Multi-Year Discount:

Condition: Subscription Term >= 24 months
Action: Discount = 10%

Product Combination Pricing:

Condition 1: Has Product A
Condition 2: Has Product B
Action: Apply 15% to Product B

Minimum Price Enforcement:

Condition: Net Price < Cost * 1.2
Action: Net Price = Cost * 1.2
Result: Enforce 20% minimum margin

Troubleshooting Price Rules:

  • Enable CPQ Debug Mode in setup
  • Check rule evaluation order
  • Verify conditions are configured correctly
  • Test with CPQ Calculator APIs
  • Review error logs for timeouts
  • Simplify complex formulas if needed

Governor Limits:

  • ⚠️ Price rules count toward CPU time limits
  • ⚠️ Complex formulas can cause timeouts
  • ⚠️ Limit: 10,000 ms CPU time (synchronous)
  • ⚠️ Optimize rules for large quotes

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Q: How do Discount Schedules work in Salesforce CPQ?
docs.text:
A: Discount Schedules automate tiered discounting based on quantity or usage thresholds, providing volume-based pricing without manual configuration.

Discount Schedule Types:

Range Discount Schedule:

  • Applies discount based on quantity ranges
  • Different discount for each tier
  • Most common type

Slab Discount Schedule:

  • Different price per unit for entire quantity
  • "All units" priced at tier rate
  • Simpler calculation

Discount Schedule vs. Price Rule:

Discount Schedule:

  • ✅ Automatic tier-based discounting
  • ✅ No conditions needed
  • ✅ Visual tier setup
  • ✅ Simple to maintain
  • ❌ Limited to quantity-based logic
  • ❌ One schedule per product

Price Rule:

  • ✅ Complex conditional logic
  • ✅ Multiple conditions
  • ✅ Custom formulas
  • ✅ Can combine with other factors
  • ❌ More complex to setup
  • ❌ Requires testing

Creating a Discount Schedule:

Object: SBQQ__DiscountSchedule__c

Fields:
- Name: "Volume Discount - Cloud Storage"
- Type: Range (or Slab)
- Discount Unit: Percent (or Amount)
- Quote Line Quantity Field: Quantity
- Constraint Field: (optional filter field)
- Cross Orders: false (apply to single order)
- Cross Products: false (apply to single product)

Tiers (SBQQ__DiscountTier__c):
Tier 1: 
  - Lower Bound: 1
  - Upper Bound: 9
  - Discount: 0%

Tier 2:
  - Lower Bound: 10
  - Upper Bound: 49
  - Discount: 10%

Tier 3:
  - Lower Bound: 50
  - Upper Bound: 99
  - Discount: 20%

Tier 4:
  - Lower Bound: 100
  - Upper Bound: (blank for no upper limit)
  - Discount: 30%

Linking Schedule to Product:

// Add discount schedule to product
Product2 product = [SELECT Id FROM Product2 WHERE Id = :productId];
product.SBQQ__DiscountSchedule__c = discountScheduleId;
update product;

// Now all quote lines for this product will use the schedule

Range Discount Example:

Product: Software License
List Price: $100 per license
Discount Schedule Type: Range

Quantity 25 licenses:
- Tier 2 (10-49): 10% discount
- Price per license: $100 * 0.90 = $90
- Total: 25 * $90 = $2,250

Quantity 75 licenses:
- Tier 3 (50-99): 20% discount  
- Price per license: $100 * 0.80 = $80
- Total: 75 * $80 = $6,000

Slab Discount Example:

Product: Data Storage
List Price: $10 per GB
Discount Schedule Type: Slab

Tier Structure:
- 0-999 GB: $10/GB
- 1000-4999 GB: $8/GB
- 5000+ GB: $6/GB

Quantity 500 GB:
- Falls in Tier 1
- All 500 GB at $10/GB
- Total: 500 * $10 = $5,000

Quantity 2000 GB:
- Falls in Tier 2
- All 2000 GB at $8/GB
- Total: 2000 * $8 = $16,000

Creating Discount Schedule Programmatically:

// Create discount schedule
SBQQ__DiscountSchedule__c schedule = new SBQQ__DiscountSchedule__c(
    Name = 'Volume Discount - Software',
    SBQQ__Type__c = 'Range',
    SBQQ__DiscountUnit__c = 'Percent',
    SBQQ__QuoteLineQuantityField__c = 'Quantity'
);
insert schedule;

// Create tiers
List<SBQQ__DiscountTier__c> tiers = new List<SBQQ__DiscountTier__c>();

tiers.add(new SBQQ__DiscountTier__c(
    SBQQ__Schedule__c = schedule.Id,
    SBQQ__LowerBound__c = 1,
    SBQQ__UpperBound__c = 9,
    SBQQ__Discount__c = 0,
    SBQQ__Number__c = 1
));

tiers.add(new SBQQ__DiscountTier__c(
    SBQQ__Schedule__c = schedule.Id,
    SBQQ__LowerBound__c = 10,
    SBQQ__UpperBound__c = 49,
    SBQQ__Discount__c = 10,
    SBQQ__Number__c = 2
));

tiers.add(new SBQQ__DiscountTier__c(
    SBQQ__Schedule__c = schedule.Id,
    SBQQ__LowerBound__c = 50,
    SBQQ__UpperBound__c = 99,
    SBQQ__Discount__c = 20,
    SBQQ__Number__c = 3
));

tiers.add(new SBQQ__DiscountTier__c(
    SBQQ__Schedule__c = schedule.Id,
    SBQQ__LowerBound__c = 100,
    SBQQ__Discount__c = 30,
    SBQQ__Number__c = 4
));

insert tiers;

// Link to product
Product2 product = [SELECT Id FROM Product2 WHERE ProductCode = 'SW-001'];
product.SBQQ__DiscountSchedule__c = schedule.Id;
update product;

Advanced Discount Schedule Features:

Cross Orders:

  • Combine quantities across multiple orders
  • Used for contract-level volume commitments
  • Applies discount based on total volume

Cross Products:

  • Combine quantities across product family
  • Example: Total Microsoft licenses
  • Family-level volume pricing

Constraint Field:

  • Filter which quote lines qualify
  • Example: Only apply to "Enterprise Edition"
  • Adds conditional logic

Example with Constraints:

// Schedule applies only to annual subscriptions
SBQQ__DiscountSchedule__c schedule = new SBQQ__DiscountSchedule__c(
    Name = 'Annual Subscription Volume Discount',
    SBQQ__Type__c = 'Range',
    SBQQ__ConstraintField__c = 'SBQQ__QuoteLine__c.Subscription_Term__c',
    SBQQ__DiscountUnit__c = 'Percent'
);

// Only applies when Subscription_Term__c = 12

Testing Discount Schedules:

@isTest
private class DiscountScheduleTest {

    @isTest
    static void testRangeDiscount() {
        // Setup discount schedule
        SBQQ__DiscountSchedule__c schedule = 
            TestDataFactory.createDiscountSchedule('Range');

        Product2 product = TestDataFactory.createProduct();
        product.SBQQ__DiscountSchedule__c = schedule.Id;
        update product;

        SBQQ__Quote__c quote = TestDataFactory.createQuote();

        // Test Tier 2 (10-49 units, 10% discount)
        Test.startTest();
        SBQQ__QuoteLine__c quoteLine = new SBQQ__QuoteLine__c(
            SBQQ__Quote__c = quote.Id,
            SBQQ__Product__c = product.Id,
            SBQQ__Quantity__c = 25,
            SBQQ__ListPrice__c = 100
        );
        insert quoteLine;

        // Calculate
        QuoteCalculator.calculate(quote.Id);
        Test.stopTest();

        // Verify
        quoteLine = [
            SELECT SBQQ__Discount__c, SBQQ__NetPrice__c
            FROM SBQQ__QuoteLine__c
            WHERE Id = :quoteLine.Id
        ];

        System.assertEquals(10, quoteLine.SBQQ__Discount__c);
        System.assertEquals(90, quoteLine.SBQQ__NetPrice__c);
    }
}

Best Practices:

  • ✅ Use Range for most scenarios (simpler)
  • ✅ Use Slab for per-unit tier pricing
  • ✅ Set clear tier boundaries
  • ✅ Test with edge cases (tier boundaries)
  • ✅ Document schedule business logic
  • ✅ Use Amount discount for fixed reductions
  • ✅ Review and update schedules annually
  • ❌ Don't create overlapping tiers
  • ❌ Avoid too many tiers (keep simple)
  • ❌ Don't forget upper bounds on middle tiers

Common Use Cases:

Standard Volume Pricing:

1-9 units: List price
10-49 units: 10% off
50-99 units: 20% off
100+ units: 30% off

Wholesale Pricing:

1-499 units: $10 each
500-999 units: $8 each  
1000+ units: $6 each

Service Tier Pricing:

Based on # of users:
1-10 users: $50/user
11-50 users: $40/user
51-100 users: $30/user
101+ users: $25/user

Troubleshooting:

  • Verify schedule is linked to product
  • Check tier boundaries don't overlap
  • Ensure quote line has quantity
  • Verify discount unit (Percent vs Amount)
  • Test schedule type (Range vs Slab)
  • Check for conflicting price rules

Performance Considerations:

  • ⚠️ Discount schedules are efficient
  • ⚠️ Cross-product schedules more complex
  • ⚠️ Test with large quotes (1000+ lines)
  • ⚠️ Minimal CPU impact compared to price rules

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Q: How do you create and customize CPQ quote templates?
docs.text:
A: CPQ quote templates use a combination of Quote Templates, Quote Line Groups, and Template Content to generate professional PDF documents with dynamic content.

Quote Template Components:

SBQQ__QuoteTemplate__c:

  • Master template definition
  • Controls overall document structure
  • Links to Template Sections

SBQQ__TemplateSection__c:

  • Individual sections of the document
  • Header, footer, body sections
  • Conditional display logic

SBQQ__TemplateContent__c:

  • HTML/CSS content for sections
  • Merge fields for dynamic data
  • Rich formatting capabilities

Creating a Quote Template:

Step 1: Create Quote Template
- Name: "Standard Quote Template"
- Default: true (use by default)
- Page Size: Letter
- Page Orientation: Portrait
- Font: Arial
- Font Size: 10

Step 2: Create Template Sections
Section 1: Header
- Type: Header
- Display Order: 1
- Conditional: (blank - always show)

Section 2: Quote Information  
- Type: Body
- Display Order: 2

Section 3: Line Items
- Type: Line Items
- Display Order: 3
- Top Margin: 10
- Bottom Margin: 10

Section 4: Terms and Conditions
- Type: Body
- Display Order: 4
- Page Break: true (start new page)

Section 5: Footer
- Type: Footer
- Display Order: 5

Template Content HTML Example:

<!-- Header Section -->
<table style="width: 100%; border-bottom: 2px solid #003366;">
    <tr>
        <td style="width: 50%;">
            <img src="{!Company_Logo}" alt="Company Logo" style="max-width: 200px;"/>
        </td>
        <td style="width: 50%; text-align: right; vertical-align: bottom;">
            <h1 style="color: #003366; margin: 0;">QUOTE</h1>
            <p style="margin: 5px 0;">
                <strong>Quote #:</strong> {!SBQQ__Quote__c.Name}<br/>
                <strong>Date:</strong> {!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__CreatedDate__c}<br/>
                <strong>Valid Until:</strong> {!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__ExpirationDate__c}
            </p>
        </td>
    </tr>
</table>

<!-- Customer Information Section -->
<table style="width: 100%; margin-top: 20px;">
    <tr>
        <td style="width: 50%; vertical-align: top;">
            <h3 style="color: #003366; border-bottom: 1px solid #ccc;">Bill To:</h3>
            <p>
                <strong>{!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__Account__c.Name}</strong><br/>
                {!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__BillingStreet__c}<br/>
                {!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__BillingCity__c}, 
                {!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__BillingState__c} 
                {!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__BillingPostalCode__c}<br/>
                {!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__BillingCountry__c}
            </p>
        </td>
        <td style="width: 50%; vertical-align: top;">
            <h3 style="color: #003366; border-bottom: 1px solid #ccc;">Ship To:</h3>
            <p>
                <strong>{!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__Account__c.Name}</strong><br/>
                {!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__ShippingStreet__c}<br/>
                {!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__ShippingCity__c},
                {!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__ShippingState__c}
                {!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__ShippingPostalCode__c}<br/>
                {!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__ShippingCountry__c}
            </p>
        </td>
    </tr>
</table>

<!-- Quote Details -->
<table style="width: 100%; margin-top: 20px; background-color: #f5f5f5; padding: 10px;">
    <tr>
        <td style="width: 33%;">
            <strong>Sales Rep:</strong><br/>
            {!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__SalesRep__c.Name}
        </td>
        <td style="width: 33%;">
            <strong>Payment Terms:</strong><br/>
            {!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__PaymentTerms__c}
        </td>
        <td style="width: 34%;">
            <strong>Subscription Term:</strong><br/>
            {!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__SubscriptionTerm__c} months
        </td>
    </tr>
</table>

<!-- Line Items Table -->
<table style="width: 100%; margin-top: 30px; border-collapse: collapse;">
    <thead>
        <tr style="background-color: #003366; color: white;">
            <th style="padding: 10px; text-align: left; border: 1px solid #ddd;">Item</th>
            <th style="padding: 10px; text-align: left; border: 1px solid #ddd;">Description</th>
            <th style="padding: 10px; text-align: center; border: 1px solid #ddd;">Quantity</th>
            <th style="padding: 10px; text-align: right; border: 1px solid #ddd;">Unit Price</th>
            <th style="padding: 10px; text-align: right; border: 1px solid #ddd;">Discount</th>
            <th style="padding: 10px; text-align: right; border: 1px solid #ddd;">Total</th>
        </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
        {!QuoteLineItems}
        <!-- CPQ Auto-populates line items here -->
    </tbody>
</table>

<!-- Totals Section -->
<table style="width: 100%; margin-top: 20px;">
    <tr>
        <td style="width: 70%;"></td>
        <td style="width: 30%; border-top: 2px solid #003366;">
            <table style="width: 100%;">
                <tr>
                    <td><strong>Subtotal:</strong></td>
                    <td style="text-align: right;">
                        {!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__ListAmount__c}
                    </td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td><strong>Discount:</strong></td>
                    <td style="text-align: right; color: red;">
                        -{!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__TotalDiscountAmount__c}
                    </td>
                </tr>
                <tr style="font-size: 14px;">
                    <td><strong>Total:</strong></td>
                    <td style="text-align: right;">
                        <strong>{!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__NetAmount__c}</strong>
                    </td>
                </tr>
            </table>
        </td>
    </tr>
</table>

<!-- Terms and Conditions -->
<div style="margin-top: 40px; page-break-before: always;">
    <h2 style="color: #003366; border-bottom: 2px solid #003366;">
        Terms and Conditions
    </h2>
    <div style="font-size: 9px; line-height: 1.4;">
        {!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__Notes__c}

        <p><strong>1. Payment Terms:</strong> Payment is due within {!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__PaymentTerms__c} of invoice date.</p>

        <p><strong>2. Subscription Terms:</strong> This quote is for a {!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__SubscriptionTerm__c} month subscription term.</p>

        <p><strong>3. Acceptance:</strong> This quote is valid until {!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__ExpirationDate__c}.</p>

        <!-- Add more terms as needed -->
    </div>
</div>

<!-- Footer -->
<div style="text-align: center; font-size: 8px; color: #666;">
    <p>
        {!Company_Name} | {!Company_Address} | {!Company_Phone} | {!Company_Website}
    </p>
    <p>Page {!PageNumber} of {!PageCount}</p>
</div>

Custom Merge Fields:

Standard Merge Fields:
{!SBQQ__Quote__c.Field_API_Name}
{!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__Account__c.Name}
{!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__Opportunity2__c.Name}

Line Item Fields (in Line Items section):
{!SBQQ__QuoteLine__c.SBQQ__ProductName__c}
{!SBQQ__QuoteLine__c.SBQQ__Quantity__c}
{!SBQQ__QuoteLine__c.SBQQ__NetPrice__c}

Conditional Display:
{!IF(SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__Type__c == "Renewal", "RENEWAL QUOTE", "NEW QUOTE")}

Formatting:
{!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__NetAmount__c, Number, Currency}
{!SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__StartDate__c, Date, MM/DD/YYYY}

Programmatic Quote Document Generation:

// Generate quote document
public class QuoteDocumentGenerator {

    public static Id generateQuoteDocument(Id quoteId) {
        // Get quote with template
        SBQQ__Quote__c quote = [
            SELECT Id, SBQQ__QuoteTemplate__c
            FROM SBQQ__Quote__c
            WHERE Id = :quoteId
        ];

        // Generate PDF using CPQ API
        PageReference quotePdf = Page.SBQQ__Quote;
        quotePdf.getParameters().put('id', quoteId);

        Blob pdfContent;
        if (Test.isRunningTest()) {
            pdfContent = Blob.valueOf('Test PDF Content');
        } else {
            pdfContent = quotePdf.getContent();
        }

        // Create attachment
        Attachment att = new Attachment(
            Name = 'Quote_' + quote.Id + '.pdf',
            ParentId = quoteId,
            Body = pdfContent,
            ContentType = 'application/pdf'
        );
        insert att;

        return att.Id;
    }

    // Email quote document
    public static void emailQuoteDocument(Id quoteId, String toEmail) {
        Id attachmentId = generateQuoteDocument(quoteId);

        Messaging.EmailFileAttachment attachment = 
            new Messaging.EmailFileAttachment();
        attachment.setFileName('Quote.pdf');
        attachment.setBody([
            SELECT Body FROM Attachment WHERE Id = :attachmentId
        ].Body);

        Messaging.SingleEmailMessage email = 
            new Messaging.SingleEmailMessage();
        email.setToAddresses(new String[] { toEmail });
        email.setSubject('Your Quote from Acme Corp');
        email.setPlainTextBody('Please find your quote attached.');
        email.setFileAttachments(
            new Messaging.EmailFileAttachment[] { attachment }
        );

        Messaging.sendEmail(new Messaging.SingleEmailMessage[] { email });
    }
}

Quote Line Groups:

// Organize quote lines into groups for better document structure
SBQQ__QuoteLineGroup__c group1 = new SBQQ__QuoteLineGroup__c(
    SBQQ__Quote__c = quoteId,
    Name = 'Cloud Services',
    SBQQ__Number__c = 1,
    SBQQ__SectionIntro__c = 'Cloud-based products and services'
);
insert group1;

// Assign quote lines to group
List<SBQQ__QuoteLine__c> lines = [
    SELECT Id
    FROM SBQQ__QuoteLine__c
    WHERE SBQQ__Quote__c = :quoteId
    AND SBQQ__Product__c.Family = 'Cloud Services'
];

for (SBQQ__QuoteLine__c line : lines) {
    line.SBQQ__Group__c = group1.Id;
}
update lines;

Best Practices:

  • ✅ Use professional, branded templates
  • ✅ Include all necessary legal terms
  • ✅ Test templates with various quote scenarios
  • ✅ Use conditional logic for dynamic content
  • ✅ Include clear pricing breakdown
  • ✅ Add company branding (logo, colors)
  • ✅ Use Quote Line Groups for organization
  • ✅ Provide multiple template options (detailed, summary)
  • ❌ Don't overcomplicate template design
  • ❌ Avoid inline CSS (use styles)
  • ❌ Don't forget to test PDF rendering

Common Template Scenarios:

Detailed Quote:

  • Complete line item details
  • Product descriptions
  • Individual discounts
  • Multiple sections

Summary Quote:

  • Grouped line items
  • High-level pricing
  • Simplified view
  • Executive presentation

Renewal Quote:

  • Previous subscription details
  • Changes from prior term
  • Renewal-specific terms
  • Comparison pricing

Governor Limits:

  • ⚠️ PDF generation counts toward heap size
  • ⚠️ Large quotes may require optimization
  • ⚠️ Email attachment size limits: 25 MB total
  • ⚠️ Consider Content Documents for large PDFs

docs.title: Q: What are Marketing Cloud Studios and how do they work together?
docs.text:
A: Marketing Cloud Studios are specialized applications within Marketing Cloud, each designed for specific marketing channels and capabilities.

Email Studio:

Purpose: Create, send, and track email campaigns

Key Features:

  • Drag-and-drop email builder
  • Template creation and management
  • Dynamic content and personalization
  • A/B testing capabilities
  • Email automation and scheduling
  • Subscriber management
  • Deliverability tracking

Use Cases:

  • Promotional campaigns
  • Newsletter distribution
  • Transactional emails
  • Drip campaigns
  • Welcome series

Key Objects:

Email: Message content and design
Subscriber: Email recipient
List: Collection of subscribers
Data Extension: Custom data tables
Send: Email delivery event

Mobile Studio:

Purpose: SMS, push notifications, and mobile messaging

Key Features:

  • SMS campaigns
  • MMS messaging
  • Push notifications (iOS/Android)
  • In-app messages
  • Location-based messaging
  • Mobile keywords and short codes

Use Cases:

  • Appointment reminders
  • Order confirmations
  • Flash sales alerts
  • App engagement
  • Customer service notifications

Journey Builder:

Purpose: Orchestrate multi-channel customer journeys

Key Features:

  • Visual journey design
  • Multi-touch campaigns
  • Decision splits based on behavior
  • Wait periods and timing control
  • Cross-channel orchestration
  • Real-time personalization

Journey Components:

  • Entry Sources: How contacts enter (API, Data Extension, Event)
  • Activities: Actions taken (Send Email, SMS, Wait, Update Data)
  • Decisions: Split paths based on criteria
  • Goals: Track journey success metrics

Example Journey Flow:

Entry: New Customer (API Event)
    ↓
Send: Welcome Email
    ↓
Wait: 2 days
    ↓
Decision: Opened Welcome Email?
    ├─ Yes → Send: Product Tutorial Email
    │         ↓
    │         Wait: 3 days
    │         ↓
    │         Send: Special Offer SMS
    │
    └─ No → Send: Reminder Email
              ↓
              Wait: 1 day
              ↓
              Decision: Opened Reminder?
                  ├─ Yes → Rejoin main flow
                  └─ No → Exit Journey

Social Studio:

Purpose: Social media management and listening

Key Features:

  • Social listening and monitoring
  • Post scheduling across platforms
  • Engagement management
  • Social analytics
  • Influencer tracking
  • Crisis management

Supported Platforms:

  • Facebook
  • Twitter
  • LinkedIn
  • Instagram
  • YouTube

Advertising Studio:

Purpose: Digital advertising integration

Key Features:

  • Audience synchronization from Marketing Cloud
  • Cross-channel advertising
  • Facebook, Google, LinkedIn ads
  • Lookalike audience creation
  • Journey Builder integration
  • ROI tracking

Workflow:

1. Build audience in Marketing Cloud
2. Sync to advertising platforms
3. Create targeted ad campaigns
4. Track conversions back to Marketing Cloud
5. Retarget based on email engagement

Interaction Studio (formerly Evergage):

Purpose: Real-time personalization and interaction management

Key Features:

  • Web personalization
  • Real-time behavioral tracking
  • Machine learning recommendations
  • A/B testing
  • Next-best-action engine

Use Cases:

  • Website personalization
  • Product recommendations
  • Content optimization
  • Real-time offers

Data Studio (Audience Studio/DMP):

Purpose: Data management and audience segmentation

Key Features:

  • Data integration from multiple sources
  • Audience segmentation
  • Data governance
  • Identity resolution
  • Data activation

Integration Example:

// Marketing Cloud API Integration from Salesforce
public class MarketingCloudIntegration {

    // Send triggered email via Marketing Cloud
    public static void sendTriggeredEmail(
        String subscriberKey,
        String emailTemplate,
        Map<String, String> attributes
    ) {
        // Marketing Cloud REST API endpoint
        String endpoint = 'https://[subdomain].rest.marketingcloudapis.com/messaging/v1/email/messages';

        // Build request
        HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
        req.setEndpoint(endpoint);
        req.setMethod('POST');
        req.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json');
        req.setHeader('Authorization', 'Bearer ' + getAccessToken());

        // Email payload
        Map<String, Object> payload = new Map<String, Object>{
            'definitionKey' => emailTemplate,
            'recipients' => new List<Map<String, Object>>{
                new Map<String, Object>{
                    'contactKey' => subscriberKey,
                    'to' => attributes.get('email'),
                    'attributes' => attributes
                }
            }
        };

        req.setBody(JSON.serialize(payload));

        // Send request
        Http http = new Http();
        HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

        if (res.getStatusCode() != 202) {
            throw new CalloutException(
                'Marketing Cloud API error: ' + res.getBody()
            );
        }
    }

    // Journey Builder API - Inject contact into journey
    public static void injectIntoJourney(
        String journeyKey,
        String contactKey,
        Map<String, Object> eventData
    ) {
        String endpoint = 'https://[subdomain].rest.marketingcloudapis.com/interaction/v1/events';

        HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
        req.setEndpoint(endpoint);
        req.setMethod('POST');
        req.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json');
        req.setHeader('Authorization', 'Bearer ' + getAccessToken());

        Map<String, Object> payload = new Map<String, Object>{
            'ContactKey' => contactKey,
            'EventDefinitionKey' => journeyKey,
            'Data' => eventData
        };

        req.setBody(JSON.serialize(payload));

        Http http = new Http();
        HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

        System.debug('Journey Injection: ' + res.getBody());
    }

    private static String getAccessToken() {
        // Implement OAuth 2.0 authentication
        // Return access token
        return 'access_token_here';
    }
}

Studios Working Together:

Scenario: E-commerce Customer Lifecycle

1. Email Studio: Welcome email after registration
2. Mobile Studio: SMS confirmation of first purchase
3. Journey Builder: 30-day onboarding journey
4. Social Studio: Encourage social sharing with discount
5. Advertising Studio: Retarget on Facebook if inactive
6. Interaction Studio: Personalized web experience

Best Practices:

  • ✅ Use Journey Builder as orchestration layer
  • ✅ Leverage Data Extensions for segmentation
  • ✅ Implement consistent branding across Studios
  • ✅ Track attribution across channels
  • ✅ Use AMPscript for dynamic content
  • ✅ Monitor deliverability in Email Studio
  • ❌ Don't duplicate audiences across Studios
  • ❌ Avoid siloed campaigns (use Journey Builder)

Marketing Cloud Connect:

  • Links Marketing Cloud to Sales Cloud
  • Syncs Contacts, Leads, and Campaign data
  • Enables triggered sends from Sales Cloud
  • Provides journey data in CRM

Edition Requirements:

  • Basic: Email Studio only
  • Pro: Email + Mobile Studios
  • Corporate: All Studios available
  • Enterprise: Advanced features and scalability

docs.title: Q: How does lead scoring work in Pardot/Account Engagement?
docs.text:
A: Lead scoring automatically assigns point values to prospects based on their demographics and activities, helping sales teams prioritize high-value leads.

Lead Scoring Components:

Score:

  • Numerical value (typically 0-100+)
  • Increases with positive engagement
  • Decreases with negative signals
  • Identifies hot leads

Grade:

  • Letter grade (A+ to F)
  • Based on fit (demographics)
  • Measures ideal customer match
  • Profile scoring

Scoring Categories:

Prospect Activities (Behavior):

  • Email opens: +1 point
  • Email clicks: +5 points
  • Form submissions: +10 points
  • Landing page views: +3 points
  • File downloads: +15 points
  • Webinar attendance: +25 points
  • Website visits: +1 point

Engagement Scoring:

  • Multiple email opens: Diminishing returns
  • Click-through: Higher value
  • Form completions: Highest value
  • Time on site: Moderate value

Demographic/Firmographic (Grading):

  • Job title matches: Grade boost
  • Company size in range: Grade boost
  • Industry match: Grade boost
  • Location match: Grade boost
  • Budget authority: Grade boost

Score Adjustments:

Positive Scoring:
+ 50 points: Demo request
+ 25 points: Pricing page view
+ 20 points: Case study download
+ 15 points: Webinar registration
+ 10 points: Blog subscription
+ 5 points: Email click-through
+ 3 points: Repeat site visit
+ 1 point: Email open

Negative Scoring:
- 10 points: Unsubscribe from emails
- 5 points: No activity for 60 days
- 3 points: Spam complaint
- 0 points: Hard bounce (removed)

Score Decay:
- Subtract points for inactivity
- Monthly or quarterly reduction
- Keeps scores current
- Identifies disengaged prospects

Grading Profile Setup:

Grading Category: Job Title
A: C-Level, VP, Director
B: Manager
C: Individual Contributor
D: Student, Other
F: Competitor, Vendor

Grading Category: Company Size
A: 1000+ employees
B: 100-999 employees
C: 10-99 employees
D: 1-9 employees
F: 0 employees

Grading Category: Industry
A: Technology, Finance (target industries)
B: Healthcare, Manufacturing
C: Retail
D: Other
F: Not-for-profit, Government (if not target)

Combined Grade Calculation:
Overall Grade = Average of all category grades

Automation Rules for Scoring:

Rule: High Score Lead Assignment
Criteria:
- Prospect Score greater than 100
- Prospect Grade A or B
- Owner: Default Prospect Account
Actions:
- Assign to Sales Queue
- Send alert to Sales Manager
- Add to "Hot Leads" list
- Trigger Salesforce assignment rule

Rule: Score Decay for Inactivity
Criteria:
- Last Activity more than 60 days ago
Actions:
- Subtract 10 points from score
- Change grade to C (if below threshold)
- Add to re-engagement campaign

Rule: Demo Request Boost
Criteria:
- Form "Demo Request" submitted
Actions:
- Add 50 points
- Change owner to Sales Rep
- Send immediate alert
- Create High Priority Task

Pardot API - Score Update Example:

// Update prospect score via API
public class PardotScoringIntegration {

    public static void updateProspectScore(
        String prospectEmail,
        Integer scoreAdjustment,
        String reason
    ) {
        // Pardot API endpoint
        String endpoint = 'https://pi.pardot.com/api/prospect/version/4/do/update/email/' + 
                          EncodingUtil.urlEncode(prospectEmail, 'UTF-8');

        HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
        req.setEndpoint(endpoint);
        req.setMethod('POST');
        req.setHeader('Authorization', 'Pardot api_key=' + getPardotApiKey());
        req.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded');

        // Add score adjustment
        String body = 'score=' + scoreAdjustment + 
                     '&score_adjustment_note=' + 
                     EncodingUtil.urlEncode(reason, 'UTF-8');
        req.setBody(body);

        Http http = new Http();
        HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

        if (res.getStatusCode() == 200) {
            System.debug('Score updated successfully');
        }
    }

    // Sync high-scoring prospects to Salesforce
    public static void syncHighScoringProspects() {
        // Query Pardot for prospects with score > 100
        String endpoint = 'https://pi.pardot.com/api/prospect/version/4/do/query';

        HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
        req.setEndpoint(endpoint + '?score_greater_than=100&grade_equal_to=A,B');
        req.setMethod('GET');
        req.setHeader('Authorization', 'Pardot api_key=' + getPardotApiKey());

        Http http = new Http();
        HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

        // Parse response and create/update Leads
        if (res.getStatusCode() == 200) {
            // Process prospects and create Leads
            Map<String, Object> result = 
                (Map<String, Object>) JSON.deserializeUntyped(res.getBody());

            // Create or update Lead records
            List<Lead> leadsToUpsert = new List<Lead>();
            // ... process and upsert
        }
    }

    private static String getPardotApiKey() {
        // Retrieve from custom setting or credential
        return 'api_key_here';
    }
}

Score-Based Lead Routing:

Scoring Tier | Score Range | Grade | Action
Hot Lead     | 100+        | A-B   | Immediate assignment to Sales
Warm Lead    | 50-99       | B-C   | Add to nurture campaign
Cold Lead    | 0-49        | C-D   | Marketing automation only
Unqualified  | Any         | F     | Suppress or remove

Salesforce Lead Status Integration:

// Sync Pardot Score to Salesforce Lead
trigger PardotScoreSync on Lead (after update) {
    for (Lead lead : Trigger.new) {
        // Check if Pardot score changed
        if (lead.pi__score__c != Trigger.oldMap.get(lead.Id).pi__score__c) {

            // Update Lead Status based on score
            if (lead.pi__score__c >= 100 && lead.pi__grade__c == 'A') {
                lead.Status = 'Hot Lead';
                lead.Rating = 'Hot';
            } else if (lead.pi__score__c >= 50) {
                lead.Status = 'Warm Lead';
                lead.Rating = 'Warm';
            } else {
                lead.Status = 'Cold Lead';
                lead.Rating = 'Cold';
            }

            // Create task for high scores
            if (lead.pi__score__c >= 100 && lead.OwnerId != null) {
                Task followUp = new Task(
                    WhoId = lead.Id,
                    Subject = 'Follow up on Hot Lead',
                    Description = 'Lead scored ' + lead.pi__score__c + 
                                  ' points. Grade: ' + lead.pi__grade__c,
                    Priority = 'High',
                    Status = 'Not Started',
                    ActivityDate = Date.today()
                );
                insert followUp;
            }
        }
    }
}

Best Practices:

  • ✅ Align scoring with sales team input
  • ✅ Review and adjust scores quarterly
  • ✅ Use score decay to reflect engagement recency
  • ✅ Combine score and grade for qualification
  • ✅ Test scoring model with historical data
  • ✅ Document scoring rationale
  • ✅ Train sales team on score interpretation
  • ❌ Don't over-complicate scoring model
  • ❌ Avoid scoring every minor interaction
  • ❌ Don't ignore negative scoring triggers

Common Scoring Models:

Simple Model:

Engagement: 0-50 points
Fit: Grade A-F
Threshold: 50+ points + Grade B or better = MQL

Advanced Model:

Behavior Score: 0-100 (activities)
Fit Score: 0-100 (demographics)
Intent Score: 0-100 (engagement recency)
Combined Score: (Behavior + Fit + Intent) / 3
MQL Threshold: 80+

Industry-Specific Model:

B2B SaaS:
- Product tour completion: +40
- Technical documentation view: +20
- API documentation view: +30
- Pricing calculator use: +35
- Integration research: +25

Reporting on Lead Scoring:

  • Score distribution report
  • Conversion rate by score range
  • Time to MQL by channel
  • Score velocity (rate of increase)
  • Grade distribution
  • Sales acceptance rate by score

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Q: How do you integrate CPQ with external systems using APIs?
docs.text:
A: CPQ provides REST and SOAP APIs for integration, along with platform events and Apex classes for custom integration scenarios.

CPQ API Capabilities:

Product Catalog API:

  • Query products and configurations
  • Retrieve pricing information
  • Access product rules
  • Get bundle structures

Quote Calculation API:

  • Trigger quote recalculation
  • Apply pricing rules
  • Calculate discounts
  • Generate line items

Document Generation API:

  • Create quote PDFs
  • Generate proposals
  • Email documents
  • Store in files

Order and Contract API:

  • Create orders from quotes
  • Manage subscriptions
  • Handle amendments
  • Process renewals

REST API Integration Example:

// External system calls CPQ to create quote
public class CPQRestAPIExample {

    // Create quote via REST API
    @HttpPost
    global static String createQuote(QuoteRequest request) {
        try {
            // Create Quote
            SBQQ__Quote__c quote = new SBQQ__Quote__c(
                SBQQ__Account__c = request.accountId,
                SBQQ__Opportunity2__c = request.opportunityId,
                SBQQ__PriceBook__c = request.priceBookId,
                SBQQ__StartDate__c = request.startDate,
                SBQQ__SubscriptionTerm__c = request.subscriptionTerm
            );
            insert quote;

            // Create Quote Lines
            List<SBQQ__QuoteLine__c> lines = new List<SBQQ__QuoteLine__c>();
            for (QuoteLineRequest lineReq : request.lineItems) {
                lines.add(new SBQQ__QuoteLine__c(
                    SBQQ__Quote__c = quote.Id,
                    SBQQ__Product__c = lineReq.productId,
                    SBQQ__Quantity__c = lineReq.quantity
                ));
            }
            insert lines;

            // Calculate Quote
            SBQQ.TriggerControl.disable();
            quote = calculateQuote(quote.Id);

            // Return response
            QuoteResponse response = new QuoteResponse();
            response.quoteId = quote.Id;
            response.totalAmount = quote.SBQQ__NetAmount__c;
            response.status = 'Success';

            return JSON.serialize(response);

        } catch (Exception e) {
            return JSON.serialize(new QuoteResponse(
                'Error', 
                e.getMessage()
            ));
        }
    }

    // Calculate quote using CPQ API
    private static SBQQ__Quote__c calculateQuote(Id quoteId) {
        // Use CPQ Calculator API
        QuoteModel quoteModel = SBQQ.ServiceRouter.load(
            'SBQQ.QuoteAPI.QuoteCalculator',
            null,
            JSON.serialize(new Map<String, Object>{
                'quoteId' => quoteId
            })
        );

        String calculatedJson = SBQQ.ServiceRouter.save(
            'SBQQ.QuoteAPI.QuoteCalculator',
            JSON.serialize(quoteModel)
        );

        return [
            SELECT Id, SBQQ__NetAmount__c, SBQQ__TotalPrice__c
            FROM SBQQ__Quote__c
            WHERE Id = :quoteId
        ];
    }

    // Helper classes
    global class QuoteRequest {
        public Id accountId;
        public Id opportunityId;
        public Id priceBookId;
        public Date startDate;
        public Integer subscriptionTerm;
        public List<QuoteLineRequest> lineItems;
    }

    global class QuoteLineRequest {
        public Id productId;
        public Decimal quantity;
    }

    global class QuoteResponse {
        public String status;
        public String message;
        public Id quoteId;
        public Decimal totalAmount;

        public QuoteResponse() {}

        public QuoteResponse(String status, String message) {
            this.status = status;
            this.message = message;
        }
    }
}

CPQ Calculator API (Apex):

// Programmatic quote calculation
public class CPQCalculatorExample {

    public static void calculateQuoteWithAPI(Id quoteId) {
        // Load quote model
        String quoteJSON = SBQQ.ServiceRouter.load(
            'SBQQ.QuoteAPI.QuoteReader',
            null,
            JSON.serialize(new Map<String, Object>{
                'quoteId' => quoteId
            })
        );

        // Parse quote model
        Map<String, Object> quoteModel = 
            (Map<String, Object>) JSON.deserializeUntyped(quoteJSON);

        // Modify quote programmatically
        // ... make changes to quoteModel

        // Calculate and save
        String calculatedJSON = SBQQ.ServiceRouter.save(
            'SBQQ.QuoteAPI.QuoteCalculator',
            JSON.serialize(quoteModel)
        );

        System.debug('Quote calculated: ' + calculatedJSON);
    }

    // Add products to quote programmatically
    public static void addProductsToQuote(
        Id quoteId,
        List<ProductRequest> products
    ) {
        // Read existing quote
        SBQQ__Quote__c quote = [
            SELECT Id, SBQQ__PriceBook__c
            FROM SBQQ__Quote__c
            WHERE Id = :quoteId
        ];

        // Get pricebook entries
        Map<Id, PricebookEntry> priceMap = new Map<Id, PricebookEntry>();
        for (PricebookEntry pbe : [
            SELECT Id, Product2Id, UnitPrice
            FROM PricebookEntry
            WHERE Pricebook2Id = :quote.SBQQ__PriceBook__c
            AND Product2Id IN :getProductIds(products)
        ]) {
            priceMap.put(pbe.Product2Id, pbe);
        }

        // Create quote lines
        List<SBQQ__QuoteLine__c> lines = new List<SBQQ__QuoteLine__c>();
        for (ProductRequest prod : products) {
            PricebookEntry pbe = priceMap.get(prod.productId);
            if (pbe != null) {
                lines.add(new SBQQ__QuoteLine__c(
                    SBQQ__Quote__c = quoteId,
                    SBQQ__Product__c = prod.productId,
                    SBQQ__Quantity__c = prod.quantity,
                    SBQQ__PricebookEntryId__c = pbe.Id,
                    SBQQ__ListPrice__c = pbe.UnitPrice
                ));
            }
        }

        if (!lines.isEmpty()) {
            insert lines;
            calculateQuoteWithAPI(quoteId);
        }
    }

    private static Set<Id> getProductIds(List<ProductRequest> products) {
        Set<Id> ids = new Set<Id>();
        for (ProductRequest prod : products) {
            ids.add(prod.productId);
        }
        return ids;
    }

    public class ProductRequest {
        public Id productId;
        public Decimal quantity;
    }
}

Platform Events for Real-Time Integration:

// Define custom platform event
// CPQ_Quote_Event__e

trigger CPQQuoteEventTrigger on SBQQ__Quote__c (after insert, after update) {
    List<CPQ_Quote_Event__e> events = new List<CPQ_Quote_Event__e>();

    for (SBQQ__Quote__c quote : Trigger.new) {
        // Check if quote reached approval threshold
        if (quote.SBQQ__Status__c == 'Approved' && 
            (Trigger.isInsert || 
             quote.SBQQ__Status__c != Trigger.oldMap.get(quote.Id).SBQQ__Status__c)) {

            events.add(new CPQ_Quote_Event__e(
                Quote_Id__c = quote.Id,
                Account_Id__c = quote.SBQQ__Account__c,
                Total_Amount__c = quote.SBQQ__NetAmount__c,
                Event_Type__c = 'Quote Approved',
                Timestamp__c = Datetime.now()
            ));
        }
    }

    if (!events.isEmpty()) {
        EventBus.publish(events);
    }
}

// Subscribe to events in external system
// External system listens via CometD or REST API

Middleware Integration Pattern:

// MuleSoft/Integration Layer Example
public class CPQMiddlewareIntegration {

    // Outbound: Send quote to ERP
    public static void sendQuoteToERP(Id quoteId) {
        SBQQ__Quote__c quote = [
            SELECT Id, Name, SBQQ__Account__r.Name,
                   SBQQ__NetAmount__c, SBQQ__Status__c,
                   (SELECT SBQQ__ProductName__c, SBQQ__Quantity__c,
                           SBQQ__NetPrice__c, SBQQ__NetTotal__c
                    FROM SBQQ__LineItems__r)
            FROM SBQQ__Quote__c
            WHERE Id = :quoteId
        ];

        // Build payload
        Map<String, Object> payload = new Map<String, Object>{
            'quoteNumber' => quote.Name,
            'customerName' => quote.SBQQ__Account__r.Name,
            'totalAmount' => quote.SBQQ__NetAmount__c,
            'status' => quote.SBQQ__Status__c,
            'lineItems' => buildLineItems(quote.SBQQ__LineItems__r)
        };

        // Call middleware
        HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
        req.setEndpoint('callout:ERP_Integration/api/quotes');
        req.setMethod('POST');
        req.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json');
        req.setBody(JSON.serialize(payload));

        Http http = new Http();
        HttpResponse res = http.send(req);

        if (res.getStatusCode() == 200) {
            // Update quote with ERP reference
            quote.ERP_Quote_Number__c = 
                getERPQuoteNumber(res.getBody());
            update quote;
        }
    }

    // Inbound: Receive pricing from ERP
    @HttpPost
    global static String updatePricingFromERP(ERPPricingRequest request) {
        try {
            // Find quote
            SBQQ__Quote__c quote = [
                SELECT Id
                FROM SBQQ__Quote__c
                WHERE ERP_Quote_Number__c = :request.erpQuoteNumber
                LIMIT 1
            ];

            // Update prices
            List<SBQQ__QuoteLine__c> linesToUpdate = 
                new List<SBQQ__QuoteLine__c>();

            for (ERPPricingLine erpLine : request.lineItems) {
                SBQQ__QuoteLine__c quoteLine = [
                    SELECT Id, SBQQ__CustomerPrice__c
                    FROM SBQQ__QuoteLine__c
                    WHERE SBQQ__Quote__c = :quote.Id
                    AND SBQQ__ProductCode__c = :erpLine.productCode
                    LIMIT 1
                ];

                quoteLine.SBQQ__CustomerPrice__c = erpLine.specialPrice;
                quoteLine.ERP_Cost__c = erpLine.cost;
                linesToUpdate.add(quoteLine);
            }

            if (!linesToUpdate.isEmpty()) {
                update linesToUpdate;
                CPQCalculatorExample.calculateQuoteWithAPI(quote.Id);
            }

            return JSON.serialize(new Map<String, String>{
                'status' => 'Success',
                'quoteId' => quote.Id
            });

        } catch (Exception e) {
            return JSON.serialize(new Map<String, String>{
                'status' => 'Error',
                'message' => e.getMessage()
            });
        }
    }

    private static List<Map<String, Object>> buildLineItems(
        List<SBQQ__QuoteLine__c> lines
    ) {
        List<Map<String, Object>> items = new List<Map<String, Object>>();
        for (SBQQ__QuoteLine__c line : lines) {
            items.add(new Map<String, Object>{
                'productName' => line.SBQQ__ProductName__c,
                'quantity' => line.SBQQ__Quantity__c,
                'unitPrice' => line.SBQQ__NetPrice__c,
                'totalPrice' => line.SBQQ__NetTotal__c
            });
        }
        return items;
    }

    private static String getERPQuoteNumber(String responseBody) {
        Map<String, Object> response = 
            (Map<String, Object>) JSON.deserializeUntyped(responseBody);
        return (String) response.get('erpQuoteNumber');
    }

    global class ERPPricingRequest {
        public String erpQuoteNumber;
        public List<ERPPricingLine> lineItems;
    }

    global class ERPPricingLine {
        public String productCode;
        public Decimal specialPrice;
        public Decimal cost;
    }
}

Best Practices:

  • ✅ Use CPQ APIs for quote manipulation
  • ✅ Implement error handling and retry logic
  • ✅ Use Platform Events for real-time updates
  • ✅ Leverage Named Credentials for authentication
  • ✅ Test integrations in sandbox first
  • ✅ Monitor API usage and limits
  • ✅ Document integration architecture
  • ❌ Don't bypass CPQ calculation engine
  • ❌ Avoid direct DML on quote lines during calculation
  • ❌ Don't hardcode credentials

Governor Limits:

  • ⚠️ API Callouts: 100 per transaction
  • ⚠️ HTTP Request timeout: 120 seconds
  • ⚠️ Platform Events: 150 publish calls per hour
  • ⚠️ Apex CPU time: 10,000 ms
