docs.title: Q: What are the best practices for CPQ performance optimization?
docs.text:
A: CPQ performance optimization focuses on efficient data handling, streamlined calculations, and proper use of platform capabilities to ensure fast quote processing.

Quote Calculation Optimization:

Minimize Quote Line Count:

  • Consolidate similar products when possible
  • Use product quantities instead of multiple lines
  • Group related items efficiently
  • Target: < 500 lines per quote for optimal performance

Optimize Price Rules:

// ❌ BAD: Inefficient price rule with multiple queries
// This creates N+1 query issues
for each quote line:
    query related data
    calculate price
    update line

// ✅ GOOD: Bulkified price calculation
// Query all related data once
Map<Id, RelatedData> dataMap = query all related data at once
for each quote line:
    use dataMap for calculation
    calculate price
bulk update all lines

Price Rule Best Practices:

  • ✅ Use Summary Variables instead of SOQL in formulas
  • ✅ Limit conditions to essential criteria only
  • ✅ Use appropriate evaluation scope (Calculator vs Configurator)
  • ✅ Set proper evaluation order (lower runs first)
  • ✅ Combine related rules when possible
  • ❌ Avoid complex nested IF statements in formulas
  • ❌ Don't create redundant or overlapping rules
  • ❌ Avoid SOQL queries in price rule formulas

Product Rule Optimization:

  • Minimize number of active product rules
  • Use specific conditions to limit execution
  • Test rules with large product catalogs
  • Consider rule evaluation order impact

Custom Code Optimization:

// ❌ BAD: Non-bulkified trigger
trigger QuoteLineTrigger on SBQQ__QuoteLine__c (before insert) {
    for (SBQQ__QuoteLine__c line : Trigger.new) {
        // Query inside loop - inefficient
        Product2 product = [
            SELECT Cost__c 
            FROM Product2 
            WHERE Id = :line.SBQQ__Product__c
        ];
        line.Cost__c = product.Cost__c;
    }
}

// ✅ GOOD: Bulkified trigger
trigger QuoteLineTrigger on SBQQ__QuoteLine__c (before insert) {
    Set<Id> productIds = new Set<Id>();
    for (SBQQ__QuoteLine__c line : Trigger.new) {
        productIds.add(line.SBQQ__Product__c);
    }

    // Single query for all products
    Map<Id, Product2> productMap = new Map<Id, Product2>([
        SELECT Id, Cost__c
        FROM Product2
        WHERE Id IN :productIds
    ]);

    // Update lines using map
    for (SBQQ__QuoteLine__c line : Trigger.new) {
        Product2 product = productMap.get(line.SBQQ__Product__c);
        if (product != null) {
            line.Cost__c = product.Cost__c;
        }
    }
}

Database Query Optimization:

// ❌ BAD: Querying all fields
List<SBQQ__Quote__c> quotes = [
    SELECT FIELDS(ALL)
    FROM SBQQ__Quote__c
    WHERE SBQQ__Account__c = :accountId
];

// ✅ GOOD: Query only needed fields
List<SBQQ__Quote__c> quotes = [
    SELECT Id, Name, SBQQ__NetAmount__c, SBQQ__Status__c
    FROM SBQQ__Quote__c
    WHERE SBQQ__Account__c = :accountId
    AND SBQQ__Status__c IN ('Draft', 'Approved')
    LIMIT 100
];

// ✅ BETTER: Use selective filters with indexes
List<SBQQ__Quote__c> quotes = [
    SELECT Id, Name, SBQQ__NetAmount__c, SBQQ__Status__c
    FROM SBQQ__Quote__c
    WHERE SBQQ__Primary__c = true
    AND SBQQ__Opportunity2__c = :oppId
    LIMIT 1
];

CPQ Package Settings Optimization:

Navigate to: CPQ > Settings > Plugins

Optimization Settings:
✅ Enable Advanced Calculator
✅ Enable Large Quote Experience (for 500+ lines)
✅ Disable Constraint Rules (if not used)
✅ Enable Quote Line Sorting
✅ Use Segmented Quoting for complex quotes

Calculate Settings:
- Calculate Immediately: false (for large quotes)
- Enable Quantities on Groups: only if needed
- Preserve Bundle Structure: only if needed

Bundle Configuration Optimization:

  • Limit bundle depth (max 2-3 levels)
  • Reduce number of product options per feature
  • Use option constraints sparingly
  • Test bundle performance with max selections

Template Generation Optimization:

// Optimize quote document generation
public class OptimizedQuoteDocument {

    public static void generateQuoteDocumentAsync(Id quoteId) {
        // Use async method for large quotes
        System.enqueueJob(new QuoteDocumentQueueable(quoteId));
    }

    public class QuoteDocumentQueueable implements Queueable {
        private Id quoteId;

        public QuoteDocumentQueueable(Id quoteId) {
            this.quoteId = quoteId;
        }

        public void execute(QueueableContext context) {
            // Query only required fields
            SBQQ__Quote__c quote = [
                SELECT Id, Name, SBQQ__Account__c, SBQQ__NetAmount__c,
                       (SELECT SBQQ__ProductName__c, SBQQ__Quantity__c,
                               SBQQ__NetPrice__c, SBQQ__NetTotal__c
                        FROM SBQQ__LineItems__r
                        WHERE SBQQ__Hidden__c = false
                        ORDER BY SBQQ__Number__c
                        LIMIT 1000)
                FROM SBQQ__Quote__c
                WHERE Id = :quoteId
            ];

            // Generate PDF efficiently
            PageReference pdf = Page.SBQQ__Quote;
            pdf.getParameters().put('id', quoteId);

            Blob pdfBlob = Test.isRunningTest() ? 
                          Blob.valueOf('Test') : 
                          pdf.getContentAsPDF();

            // Use ContentVersion for large files
            ContentVersion cv = new ContentVersion(
                Title = 'Quote_' + quote.Name + '.pdf',
                PathOnClient = 'Quote_' + quote.Name + '.pdf',
                VersionData = pdfBlob,
                FirstPublishLocationId = quoteId
            );
            insert cv;
        }
    }
}

Large Quote Handling:

// Handle quotes with 500+ lines
public class LargeQuoteHandler {

    // Process in batches
    public static void processlargequote(Id quoteId) {
        // Break into manageable chunks
        List<SBQQ__QuoteLine__c> allLines = [
            SELECT Id, SBQQ__Product__c, SBQQ__Quantity__c
            FROM SBQQ__QuoteLine__c
            WHERE SBQQ__Quote__c = :quoteId
        ];

        Integer batchSize = 200;
        List<List<SBQQ__QuoteLine__c>> batches = 
            splitIntoBatches(allLines, batchSize);

        for (List<SBQQ__QuoteLine__c> batch : batches) {
            // Process each batch
            processBatch(batch);
        }
    }

    private static List<List<SBQQ__QuoteLine__c>> splitIntoBatches(
        List<SBQQ__QuoteLine__c> lines,
        Integer batchSize
    ) {
        List<List<SBQQ__QuoteLine__c>> batches = 
            new List<List<SBQQ__QuoteLine__c>>();

        for (Integer i = 0; i < lines.size(); i += batchSize) {
            Integer endIndex = Math.min(i + batchSize, lines.size());
            batches.add(lines.subList(i, endIndex));
        }

        return batches;
    }

    private static void processBatch(List<SBQQ__QuoteLine__c> batch) {
        // Process batch logic
        // Update fields, calculate pricing, etc.
    }
}

Monitoring and Debugging:

// Enable debug logs for performance analysis
System.debug(LoggingLevel.INFO, 
    'Quote Calculation Start: ' + Datetime.now());

Savepoint sp = Database.setSavepoint();

try {
    // Perform operation
    Long startTime = System.currentTimeMillis();

    calculateQuote(quoteId);

    Long endTime = System.currentTimeMillis();
    System.debug('Calculation Time: ' + (endTime - startTime) + 'ms');

} catch (Exception e) {
    Database.rollback(sp);
    System.debug(LoggingLevel.ERROR, 'Error: ' + e.getMessage());
    throw e;
}

// Check limits
System.debug('CPU Time Used: ' + Limits.getCpuTime());
System.debug('Heap Size Used: ' + Limits.getHeapSize());
System.debug('SOQL Queries: ' + Limits.getQueries());
System.debug('DML Statements: ' + Limits.getDmlStatements());

Performance Benchmarks:

Quote Size          | Target Calculation Time
1-50 lines         | < 5 seconds
51-200 lines       | < 15 seconds
201-500 lines      | < 30 seconds
501-1000 lines     | < 60 seconds (async recommended)
1000+ lines        | Async processing required

Best Practices Summary:

  • ✅ Bulkify all custom code
  • ✅ Use efficient SOQL queries with selective filters
  • ✅ Minimize active price and product rules
  • ✅ Enable Large Quote Experience for big quotes
  • ✅ Use async processing for heavy operations
  • ✅ Monitor CPU time and heap size
  • ✅ Implement proper error handling
  • ✅ Test with realistic data volumes
  • ✅ Use platform cache for frequently accessed data
  • ❌ Don't perform DML in loops
  • ❌ Avoid complex formula fields on high-volume objects
  • ❌ Don't create unnecessary workflow rules or process builders

Governor Limits to Watch:

  • ⚠️ CPU Time: 10,000ms (synchronous), 60,000ms (asynchronous)
  • ⚠️ Heap Size: 6MB (synchronous), 12MB (asynchronous)
  • ⚠️ SOQL Queries: 100 per transaction
  • ⚠️ DML Statements: 150 per transaction
  • ⚠️ Query Rows: 50,000 per transaction

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Q: How do you troubleshoot common CPQ calculation errors?
docs.text:
A: CPQ calculation errors typically stem from pricing configuration, product rules, or data integrity issues. Systematic debugging helps identify and resolve these problems.

Common Error Types:

"Quote Calculation Failed" Error:

Symptoms:
- Quote calculator hangs or times out
- "Unable to lock row" error
- CPU time limit exceeded

Causes:
- Too many quote lines (> 1000)
- Complex price rules with nested conditions
- Recursive triggers or workflows
- Large product bundles
- Concurrent calculations on same quote

Solutions:
✅ Enable CPQ Debug Mode
✅ Review price rule evaluation order
✅ Simplify complex formulas
✅ Break large quotes into multiple quotes
✅ Use asynchronous calculation for large quotes
✅ Disable unnecessary automation

Debug Steps:
1. Enable CPQ Debug in Setup
2. Reproduce error
3. Check Debug Logs (Setup > Debug Logs)
4. Look for CPU time or heap size limits
5. Identify slow-running price rules or triggers

Price Rule Not Firing:

Symptoms:
- Expected discount not applied
- Price remains at list price
- No error message

Troubleshooting:
1. Verify rule is Active
2. Check Evaluation Scope (Calculator vs Configurator)
3. Review Evaluation Event setting
4. Verify conditions are met
5. Check evaluation order (conflicts with other rules)
6. Test conditions manually

Debugging Price Rules:

// Debug price rule execution
System.debug('=== PRICE RULE DEBUG ===');

// Check if quote line meets conditions
SBQQ__QuoteLine__c line = [
    SELECT Id, SBQQ__Quantity__c, SBQQ__Product__r.ProductCode,
           SBQQ__Discount__c
    FROM SBQQ__QuoteLine__c
    WHERE Id = :lineId
];

System.debug('Quantity: ' + line.SBQQ__Quantity__c);
System.debug('Product Code: ' + line.SBQQ__Product__r.ProductCode);
System.debug('Current Discount: ' + line.SBQQ__Discount__c);

// Manual condition check
if (line.SBQQ__Quantity__c >= 50) {
    System.debug('Condition MET: Quantity >= 50');
} else {
    System.debug('Condition NOT MET: Quantity < 50');
}

// Check for conflicting rules
List<SBQQ__PriceRule__c> activeRules = [
    SELECT Id, Name, SBQQ__EvaluationOrder__c, SBQQ__Active__c
    FROM SBQQ__PriceRule__c
    WHERE SBQQ__Active__c = true
    ORDER BY SBQQ__EvaluationOrder__c
];

for (SBQQ__PriceRule__c rule : activeRules) {
    System.debug('Active Rule: ' + rule.Name + 
                 ' (Order: ' + rule.SBQQ__EvaluationOrder__c + ')');
}

Product Configuration Issues:

Symptom: Product options not appearing in configurator

Troubleshooting:
1. Verify Product Option records exist
2. Check Product Feature is active
3. Verify option is not hidden by Product Rule
4. Check Configuration Attribute settings
5. Review Option Constraints

Debug Query:

// Check product configuration setup
Product2 product = [
    SELECT Id, Name,
           (SELECT Id, Name, SBQQ__OptionalSKU__c, 
                   SBQQ__Required__c, SBQQ__Selected__c
            FROM SBQQ__ProductOptions__r)
    FROM Product2
    WHERE Id = :productId
];

System.debug('Product: ' + product.Name);
System.debug('Number of Options: ' + product.SBQQ__ProductOptions__r.size());

for (SBQQ__ProductOption__c option : product.SBQQ__ProductOptions__r) {
    System.debug('Option: ' + option.Name + 
                 ' | Required: ' + option.SBQQ__Required__c +
                 ' | Selected: ' + option.SBQQ__Selected__c);
}

Quote Sync Issues:

Symptom: Quote changes not syncing to Opportunity

Troubleshooting:
1. Verify quote is marked as Primary
2. Check Opportunity has proper access
3. Review sync settings in CPQ Package Settings
4. Check for validation rules blocking update
5. Verify field-level security

Debug Code:

// Check quote sync configuration
SBQQ__Quote__c quote = [
    SELECT Id, SBQQ__Primary__c, SBQQ__Opportunity2__c,
           SBQQ__NetAmount__c, SBQQ__Status__c
    FROM SBQQ__Quote__c
    WHERE Id = :quoteId
];

System.debug('Is Primary: ' + quote.SBQQ__Primary__c);
System.debug('Opportunity: ' + quote.SBQQ__Opportunity2__c);
System.debug('Quote Amount: ' + quote.SBQQ__NetAmount__c);

if (quote.SBQQ__Opportunity2__c != null) {
    Opportunity opp = [
        SELECT Id, Amount, StageName
        FROM Opportunity
        WHERE Id = :quote.SBQQ__Opportunity2__c
    ];

    System.debug('Opp Amount: ' + opp.Amount);
    System.debug('Amounts Match: ' + (quote.SBQQ__NetAmount__c == opp.Amount));

    if (quote.SBQQ__NetAmount__c != opp.Amount) {
        System.debug('SYNC ISSUE: Amounts do not match');
    }
}

Discount Schedule Not Working:

Symptom: Volume discount not applied to quote line

Troubleshooting:
1. Verify Discount Schedule is linked to Product
2. Check tier boundaries are correct
3. Verify quote line quantity falls in tier
4. Check Discount Schedule type (Range vs Slab)
5. Review constraint field settings

Debug Query:

// Check discount schedule configuration
Product2 product = [
    SELECT Id, Name, SBQQ__DiscountSchedule__c,
           SBQQ__DiscountSchedule__r.Name,
           SBQQ__DiscountSchedule__r.SBQQ__Type__c
    FROM Product2
    WHERE Id = :productId
];

System.debug('Product: ' + product.Name);
System.debug('Has Discount Schedule: ' + 
             (product.SBQQ__DiscountSchedule__c != null));

if (product.SBQQ__DiscountSchedule__c != null) {
    List<SBQQ__DiscountTier__c> tiers = [
        SELECT SBQQ__LowerBound__c, SBQQ__UpperBound__c,
               SBQQ__Discount__c
        FROM SBQQ__DiscountTier__c
        WHERE SBQQ__Schedule__c = :product.SBQQ__DiscountSchedule__c
        ORDER BY SBQQ__Number__c
    ];

    System.debug('Number of Tiers: ' + tiers.size());
    for (SBQQ__DiscountTier__c tier : tiers) {
        System.debug('Tier: ' + tier.SBQQ__LowerBound__c + 
                     ' to ' + tier.SBQQ__UpperBound__c +
                     ' = ' + tier.SBQQ__Discount__c + '%');
    }
}

Approval Process Errors:

Symptom: Quote stuck in approval or approval not triggering

Troubleshooting:
1. Check approval process entry criteria
2. Verify approver is active user
3. Review approval history
4. Check for automation conflicts
5. Verify field updates after approval

Debug:

// Check approval status
List<ProcessInstance> approvals = [
    SELECT Id, Status, TargetObjectId,
           (SELECT Id, StepStatus, Comments, ActorId
            FROM Steps)
    FROM ProcessInstance
    WHERE TargetObjectId = :quoteId
    ORDER BY CreatedDate DESC
];

for (ProcessInstance approval : approvals) {
    System.debug('Approval Status: ' + approval.Status);
    for (ProcessInstanceStep step : approval.Steps) {
        System.debug('Step Status: ' + step.StepStatus);
        System.debug('Comments: ' + step.Comments);
    }
}

Data Migration Issues:

Symptom: Quotes imported but calculations incorrect

Troubleshooting:
1. Ensure all required fields populated
2. Verify Product and Price Book relationships
3. Check for missing Configuration Attributes
4. Validate price rule conditions
5. Recalculate quotes after import

Data Validation Script:

// Validate imported quotes
public class QuoteDataValidator {

    public static void validateQuotes(Set<Id> quoteIds) {
        Map<Id, List<String>> errors = new Map<Id, List<String>>();

        List<SBQQ__Quote__c> quotes = [
            SELECT Id, Name, SBQQ__Account__c, SBQQ__Opportunity2__c,
                   SBQQ__PriceBook__c,
                   (SELECT Id, SBQQ__Product__c, SBQQ__PricebookEntryId__c
                    FROM SBQQ__LineItems__r)
            FROM SBQQ__Quote__c
            WHERE Id IN :quoteIds
        ];

        for (SBQQ__Quote__c quote : quotes) {
            List<String> quoteErrors = new List<String>();

            if (quote.SBQQ__Account__c == null) {
                quoteErrors.add('Missing Account');
            }
            if (quote.SBQQ__PriceBook__c == null) {
                quoteErrors.add('Missing Price Book');
            }
            if (quote.SBQQ__LineItems__r.isEmpty()) {
                quoteErrors.add('No Quote Lines');
            }

            for (SBQQ__QuoteLine__c line : quote.SBQQ__LineItems__r) {
                if (line.SBQQ__Product__c == null) {
                    quoteErrors.add('Line missing Product');
                }
                if (line.SBQQ__PricebookEntryId__c == null) {
                    quoteErrors.add('Line missing Price Book Entry');
                }
            }

            if (!quoteErrors.isEmpty()) {
                errors.put(quote.Id, quoteErrors);
            }
        }

        // Report errors
        for (Id quoteId : errors.keySet()) {
            System.debug('Quote ' + quoteId + ' Errors:');
            for (String error : errors.get(quoteId)) {
                System.debug('  - ' + error);
            }
        }
    }
}

Common Error Messages:

Error Message Likely Cause Solution "Unable to lock row" Concurrent updates Implement retry logic "CPU time limit exceeded" Complex calculations Optimize price rules, use async "Too many SOQL queries" Non-bulkified code Bulkify triggers and code "List has no rows for assignment" Missing data Add null checks "Field is not writeable" FLS or read-only field Check permissions

Diagnostic Checklist:

  • ✅ Enable CPQ Debug Mode
  • ✅ Check Debug Logs for errors
  • ✅ Verify data integrity (Products, Price Books)
  • ✅ Review active automation (Price Rules, Product Rules)
  • ✅ Test in sandbox before production
  • ✅ Check governor limits usage
  • ✅ Verify user permissions and profiles
  • ✅ Review recent configuration changes
  • ✅ Check for system maintenance or known issues

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Q: What are the key concepts for Salesforce CPQ Specialist Certification?
docs.text:
A: The Salesforce CPQ Specialist certification validates expertise in implementing and configuring Salesforce CPQ solutions. The exam covers seven major domains.

Certification Overview:

  • Exam Format: Multiple choice and multiple select
  • Number of Questions: 60
  • Passing Score: 72%
  • Time Allotted: 105 minutes
  • Registration Fee: $200 USD (plus applicable taxes)
  • Retake Fee: $100 USD (plus applicable taxes)

Exam Domains and Weightings:

Domain 1: Products, Pricing, and Rules (35%):

Key Topics:

  • Product and bundle configuration
  • Option constraints and dependencies
  • Price Books and Price Book Entries
  • Price Rules (conditions, actions, formulas)
  • Product Rules (validation, selection, alert, filter)
  • Discount Schedules (Range vs Slab)
  • Configuration Attributes
  • Product Features and Options

Sample Questions Focus:

- How to configure a product bundle with dependencies?
- When to use Price Rules vs Discount Schedules?
- How to create validation rules for product combinations?
- Configuration attribute use cases and setup
- Price waterfall and calculation order

Key Skills to Master:

  • ✅ Create complex product bundles
  • ✅ Configure option constraints
  • ✅ Build price rules with formulas
  • ✅ Set up discount schedules
  • ✅ Implement configuration attributes
  • ✅ Troubleshoot pricing issues

Domain 2: Quoting (20%):

Key Topics:

  • Quote-to-Opportunity relationships
  • Quote Line Editor functionality
  • Quote Templates and documents
  • Quote Line Groups
  • Multi-currency quotes
  • Quote comparison
  • Approval workflows

Critical Concepts:

- Primary Quote designation
- Quote syncing with Opportunity
- Quote cloning and copying
- Document generation
- Template customization
- Quote status lifecycle

Domain 3: Subscription Management (15%):

Key Topics:

  • Subscription products configuration
  • Contract management
  • Amendments and renewals
  • Asset-based ordering
  • Co-termination
  • Evergreen subscriptions
  • Prorated pricing

Key Understanding:

Subscription Lifecycle:
1. Initial sale → Quote → Contract
2. Amendment → Update existing contract
3. Renewal → New contract period
4. Cancellation → End subscription

Co-termination:
- Align subscription end dates
- Prorate pricing for alignment
- Manage multi-product subscriptions

Domain 4: Contracting (13%):

Key Topics:

  • Contract creation from quotes
  • Contract amendments
  • Order creation
  • Contracted pricing
  • Amendment quotes
  • Service contracts

Amendment Process:

1. Find existing contract
2. Click "Amend" button
3. Add/remove/update products
4. Adjust quantities or pricing
5. Calculate proration
6. Generate amendment quote
7. Activate amendment

Domain 5: Billing (8%):

Key Topics:

  • Integration with Salesforce Billing
  • Invoice creation
  • Payment processing
  • Revenue recognition
  • Usage-based billing
  • Payment terms

Domain 6: Integrations (5%):

Key Topics:

  • CPQ APIs (Calculator, Document)
  • External system integration
  • Platform events
  • Middleware patterns
  • Data migration

Domain 7: Adoption and Analytics (4%):

Key Topics:

  • User training and adoption
  • CPQ reports and dashboards
  • Performance monitoring
  • Best practices implementation

Study Recommendations:

Hands-On Practice:

Create a working CPQ implementation including:
✅ Product catalog with bundles
✅ Price rules and discount schedules
✅ Quote templates
✅ Subscription products
✅ Amendment scenarios
✅ Approval workflows

Trailhead Modules:

  • Salesforce CPQ Basics
  • Advanced CPQ Configuration
  • CPQ for Sales Representatives
  • CPQ Admin Certification Prep

Practice Scenarios:

Scenario 1: Complex Bundle Configuration

Build a software bundle:
- Base product (required)
- Feature selection (choose 1 of 3)
- User licenses (quantity-based)
- Add-on services (optional, multiple)
- Volume discounts on licenses
- Validation: Can't select incompatible features

Scenario 2: Subscription Management

Create a subscription model:
- Annual subscription term
- Mid-term amendment (add users)
- Prorated pricing
- Renewal quote generation
- Contracted pricing for renewal

Scenario 3: Advanced Pricing

Implement pricing strategy:
- Tiered volume discounts
- Customer-specific pricing
- Bundle discounts
- Early payment discounts
- Margin enforcement (min 20%)

docs.title: Q: What is the Salesforce multi-tenant architecture and how does it affect development?
docs.text:
A: Salesforce multi-tenant architecture means multiple customers (tenants) share the same infrastructure and application code while maintaining data isolation. This fundamentally impacts how developers must write code.

Key Characteristics:

  • Shared Resources: All orgs run on shared servers with shared database tables
  • Metadata-Driven: Customizations are stored as metadata, not hard-coded
  • Governor Limits: Enforced to prevent any single tenant from monopolizing resources
  • Universal Upgrades: All customers automatically receive platform upgrades

Development Implications:

  • Must write bulkified code to handle multiple records
  • Cannot use infinite loops or unbounded queries
  • Must respect governor limits in all code
  • Cannot make assumptions about data volume

Example Impact:

// ❌ BAD: Non-bulkified code
trigger AccountTrigger on Account (before insert) {
    for (Account acc : Trigger.new) {
        // SOQL inside loop - violates bulkification
        List<Contact> contacts = [SELECT Id FROM Contact WHERE AccountId = :acc.Id];
    }
}

// ✅ GOOD: Bulkified code
trigger AccountTrigger on Account (before insert) {
    Set<Id> accountIds = new Set<Id>();
    for (Account acc : Trigger.new) {
        accountIds.add(acc.Id);
    }
    // Single SOQL query outside loop
    Map<Id, List<Contact>> contactsByAccount = new Map<Id, List<Contact>>();
    for (Contact con : [SELECT Id, AccountId FROM Contact WHERE AccountId IN :accountIds]) {
        if (!contactsByAccount.containsKey(con.AccountId)) {
            contactsByAccount.put(con.AccountId, new List<Contact>());
        }
        contactsByAccount.get(con.AccountId).add(con);
    }
}

Salesforce Edition Requirements:

  • ✅ Available in all Salesforce editions
  • ✅ Same architecture across Professional, Enterprise, Unlimited, and Developer editions

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Q: What is the difference between declarative and programmatic customization in Salesforce?
docs.text:
A: Declarative customization uses point-and-click tools without writing code, while programmatic customization involves writing Apex code, Lightning components, or Visualforce pages.

Declarative Tools:

  • Process Builder/Flow: Automate business processes
  • Formula Fields: Calculate values dynamically
  • Validation Rules: Enforce data quality
  • Page Layouts: Control field visibility and arrangement
  • Record Types: Provide different business processes
  • Workflow Rules: Simple field updates and email alerts (legacy)

Programmatic Tools:

  • Apex: Custom business logic and complex automation
  • Lightning Web Components (LWC): Modern UI components
  • Visualforce: Legacy UI framework
  • Apex Triggers: Complex record automation
  • Batch Apex: Process large data volumes

Decision Criteria:

Use Declarative When:

  • Standard functionality meets requirements
  • No complex business logic needed
  • Faster development time is priority
  • Non-developers need to maintain it

Use Programmatic When:

  • Complex calculations or logic required
  • Integration with external systems needed
  • Declarative limits are exceeded
  • Custom UI components required
  • Performance optimization needed

Best Practice:

✅ Always use declarative tools first (clicks, not code)

✅ Only write code when declarative tools cannot meet requirements

✅ Document why code was necessary instead of clicks

Governor Limits:

⚠️ Declarative: 2,000 active Flow interviews, 5,000 time-based workflows

⚠️ Programmatic: 100 SOQL queries, 150 DML statements, 10 seconds CPU time per transaction

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Q: What are the different types of relationships in Salesforce and when should each be used?
docs.text:
A: Salesforce supports four main types of relationships: Lookup, Master-Detail, Many-to-Many (Junction Objects), and External Lookup relationships.

Relationship Types:

Lookup Relationship:

  • Definition: Loosely coupled relationship between two objects
  • Cascade Delete: No automatic deletion of child records
  • Roll-Up Summary: Not available
  • Sharing: Child records have independent sharing rules
  • Use Case: Optional relationships like Account to Contact

Master-Detail Relationship:

  • Definition: Tightly coupled relationship where child depends on parent
  • Cascade Delete: Child records automatically deleted with parent
  • Roll-Up Summary: Available on master object
  • Sharing: Child inherits sharing from master
  • Use Case: Order and Order Line Items

Many-to-Many Relationship:

  • Definition: Created using junction object with two master-detail relationships
  • Implementation: Junction object connects two parent objects
  • Use Case: Students enrolled in multiple Classes

External Lookup:

  • Definition: Links to records in external objects
  • Data Location: Data stored outside Salesforce
  • Use Case: Integration with external systems

Relationship Limits:

⚠️ Maximum 2 master-detail relationships per object

⚠️ Maximum 40 total relationships per object

⚠️ Master-detail parent must be created before child

Example Implementation:

// Query with relationship
List<Account> accounts = [
    SELECT Id, Name, 
           (SELECT Id, FirstName, LastName FROM Contacts),
           (SELECT Id, Amount, CloseDate FROM Opportunities)
    FROM Account
    WHERE Industry = 'Technology'
    LIMIT 100
];

// Access related records
for (Account acc : accounts) {
    System.debug('Account: ' + acc.Name);
    System.debug('Contacts: ' + acc.Contacts.size());
    System.debug('Opportunities: ' + acc.Opportunities.size());
}

Best Practices:

✅ Use Lookup for optional relationships

✅ Use Master-Detail when child cannot exist without parent

✅ Use Junction Objects for many-to-many relationships

✅ Consider relationship limits when designing data model

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Q: What is the Salesforce Order of Execution and why is it important for developers?
docs.text:
A: The Salesforce Order of Execution is the sequence of operations that occur when a record is saved. Understanding this is critical for preventing conflicts between automation tools and ensuring predictable behavior.

Complete Order of Execution:

Phase 1 - Load & Validation:

  • Load the original record from database or initialize for insert
  • Load new values from UI or API
  • Run system validation rules
  • Execute Before triggers
  • Run custom validation rules

Phase 2 - Save & Process:

  • Save record to database (not committed)
  • Execute After triggers
  • Execute assignment rules
  • Execute auto-response rules
  • Execute workflow rules (field updates)
  • Execute escalation rules

Phase 3 - Post-Processing:

  • Execute roll-up summary fields
  • Execute Apex sharing recalculation
  • Execute criteria-based sharing rules
  • Execute Process Builder/Flow (if configured)
  • Execute entitlement rules
  • Execute cross-object workflow updates

Phase 4 - Finalization:

  • Execute post-commit logic
  • Send email notifications
  • Execute asynchronous Apex (@future, Queueable, Batch)

Critical Developer Considerations:

Before Triggers:

  • Record not yet in database
  • Can modify field values before save
  • Use for field defaulting and validation

After Triggers:

  • Record saved but not committed
  • Cannot modify current record
  • Use for related record operations

Common Pitfalls:

❌ Modifying records in After triggers (not allowed)

❌ Not accounting for workflow field updates

❌ Recursive trigger issues

❌ Mixing Process Builder and triggers on same object

Example - Handling Order of Execution:

// Trigger Handler Pattern
public class AccountTriggerHandler {

    private static Boolean isExecuting = false;

    // Prevent recursive execution
    public static void beforeInsert(List<Account> newAccounts) {
        if (isExecuting) return;
        isExecuting = true;

        for (Account acc : newAccounts) {
            // Set default values
            if (acc.Rating == null) {
                acc.Rating = 'Cold';
            }
        }

        isExecuting = false;
    }

    public static void afterInsert(List<Account> newAccounts) {
        if (isExecuting) return;
        isExecuting = true;

        // Create related records
        List<Contact> contacts = new List<Contact>();
        for (Account acc : newAccounts) {
            contacts.add(new Contact(
                AccountId = acc.Id,
                LastName = 'Default Contact',
                Email = 'contact@' + acc.Name.toLowerCase() + '.com'
            ));
        }
        insert contacts;

        isExecuting = false;
    }
}

Best Practices:

✅ Use Before triggers for field updates on current record

✅ Use After triggers for operations on related records

✅ Implement recursion prevention mechanisms

✅ Document automation interactions

✅ Test with multiple automation tools active

Governor Limits:

⚠️ Maximum trigger depth: 16 levels

⚠️ Maximum workflow field updates: 10 per record

⚠️ CPU timeout after recursive execution

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Q: What are Formula Fields and what are their limitations?
docs.text:
A: Formula Fields are read-only fields that automatically calculate values based on other fields, expressions, or values. They are evaluated at runtime and do not consume storage.

Formula Field Types:

  • Text: Concatenate or manipulate text values
  • Number: Perform mathematical calculations
  • Currency: Calculate monetary values
  • Date/DateTime: Calculate dates
  • Checkbox: Return true/false based on conditions
  • Percent: Calculate percentages

Common Use Cases:

Calculated Values:

// Calculate Opportunity Age in Days
TODAY() - DATEVALUE(CreatedDate)

// Calculate Discount Percentage
IF(Amount > 100000, 0.15, IF(Amount > 50000, 0.10, 0.05))

// Full Name Formula
FirstName & " " & LastName

// Days Until Close
CloseDate - TODAY()

Conditional Logic:

// Account Rating based on Annual Revenue
CASE(
    WHEN AnnualRevenue >= 10000000 THEN "Hot",
    WHEN AnnualRevenue >= 1000000 THEN "Warm",
    ELSE "Cold"
)

// Opportunity Health
IF(
    AND(
        Probability >= 75,
        ISBLANK(NextStep),
        CloseDate < TODAY() + 30
    ),
    "At Risk",
    "Healthy"
)

Key Limitations:

Character Limits:

⚠️ Maximum 3,900 characters in formula

⚠️ Maximum 5,000 characters when compiled

Functionality Limits:

❌ Cannot reference Long Text Area fields

❌ Cannot reference fields from unrelated objects

❌ Cannot use DML or SOQL queries

❌ Cannot reference other formula fields more than 10 levels deep

❌ Cannot reference certain system fields

Performance Considerations:

  • Cross-Object Formulas: Limited to 10 unique relationships per object
  • Evaluation Time: Calculated at query time, not stored
  • Report Performance: Many formulas can slow reports

Best Practices:

✅ Keep formulas simple and readable

✅ Use comments to document complex logic

✅ Test edge cases (null values, divide by zero)

✅ Consider using Apex for very complex logic

✅ Avoid deeply nested formulas

Advanced Functions:

// Parent Field Reference
Account.Industry

// Case Safe Navigation
CASE(Account.Type,
    "Customer", "Existing",
    "Prospect", "New",
    "Unknown"
)

// Date Math
ADDMONTHS(StartDate__c, 12)

// Text Manipulation
LEFT(Name, 50) & "..."

// Null Handling
BLANKVALUE(CustomField__c, "Default Value")

Salesforce Edition Requirements:

  • ✅ Professional Edition: Limited formula fields
  • ✅ Enterprise Edition: Unlimited formula fields
  • ✅ Unlimited Edition: Unlimited formula fields

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Q: What are Validation Rules and how do they differ from Triggers?
docs.text:
A: Validation Rules are declarative formulas that prevent invalid data from being saved. They run before triggers and return custom error messages when conditions are not met.

Validation Rule Components:

Error Condition Formula:

  • Returns TRUE when data is invalid
  • Prevents record from being saved
  • Evaluated before triggers execute

Error Message:

  • Displayed to user when validation fails
  • Can be field-specific or page-level

Error Location:

  • Top of page (general error)
  • Specific field (field-level error)

Common Use Cases:

Data Quality Enforcement:

// Require Phone when Account is Customer
AND(
    ISPICKVAL(Type, "Customer"),
    ISBLANK(Phone)
)
// Error: "Phone is required for Customer accounts"

// Close Date must be in future
CloseDate < TODAY()
// Error: "Close Date must be in the future"

// Discount cannot exceed 40%
Discount__c > 0.40
// Error: "Discount cannot exceed 40%"

Business Logic Validation:

// Amount required for Closed Won
AND(
    ISPICKVAL(StageName, "Closed Won"),
    OR(
        ISBLANK(Amount),
        Amount <= 0
    )
)
// Error: "Amount is required for Closed Won opportunities"

// Email required for Marketing contacts
AND(
    ISPICKVAL(LeadSource, "Web"),
    ISBLANK(Email)
)
// Error: "Email is required for Web leads"

Cross-Object Validation:

// Opportunity Amount must be less than Account Annual Revenue
Amount > Account.AnnualRevenue
// Error: "Opportunity amount cannot exceed Account annual revenue"

// Contact must have Account
AND(
    ISBLANK(AccountId),
    NOT(ISBLANK(Email))
)
// Error: "Account is required when Email is provided"

Validation Rules vs. Triggers:

Validation Rules (Declarative):

  • ✅ Run before triggers
  • ✅ Easier to create and maintain
  • ✅ No code required
  • ✅ Visible in UI without code review
  • ❌ Limited to formula logic
  • ❌ Cannot perform DML or queries
  • ❌ Cannot call external services

Triggers (Programmatic):

  • ✅ Can perform complex logic
  • ✅ Can query and update related records
  • ✅ Can call external services
  • ✅ More flexible error handling
  • ❌ Requires coding knowledge
  • ❌ Higher maintenance overhead
  • ❌ Runs after validation rules

Decision Matrix:

Use Validation Rules When:

  • Simple true/false logic
  • Field comparison needed
  • Cross-object field validation
  • No queries or DML required
  • Non-developers need to maintain

Use Triggers When:

  • Complex business logic required
  • Need to query related records
  • Multiple operations needed
  • Dynamic error messages required
  • Integration with external systems

Best Practices:

✅ Use validation rules for simple data quality checks

✅ Provide clear, actionable error messages

✅ Test with all user profiles

✅ Consider user experience (don't over-validate)

✅ Document business rules clearly

❌ Don't duplicate logic between validation rules and triggers

❌ Don't create overly complex formulas

Governor Limits:

⚠️ No hard limit on validation rules per object

⚠️ Formula complexity limit: 5,000 characters compiled

⚠️ Validation rules run on every record save

Example - Comprehensive Validation:

// Opportunity Stage Progression Validation
AND(
    NOT(ISNEW()),
    OR(
        AND(
            ISPICKVAL(PRIORVALUE(StageName), "Prospecting"),
            ISPICKVAL(StageName, "Closed Won")
        ),
        AND(
            ISPICKVAL(PRIORVALUE(StageName), "Qualification"),
            ISPICKVAL(StageName, "Closed Lost")
        )
    )
)
// Error: "Cannot skip stages. Progress sequentially through sales process."

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Q: What is Apex and what are its key characteristics?
docs.text:
A: Apex is Salesforce's proprietary, strongly-typed, object-oriented programming language that executes on the Salesforce platform. It's similar to Java and allows developers to add custom business logic to Salesforce applications.

Key Characteristics:

Strongly Typed:

  • Variables must be declared with specific data types
  • Type safety enforced at compile time
  • Prevents type-related runtime errors

Object-Oriented:

  • Supports classes and objects
  • Inheritance through extends keyword
  • Interfaces for polymorphism
  • Encapsulation with access modifiers

Multi-Tenant Aware:

  • Built-in governor limits enforcement
  • Automatic bulkification considerations
  • Cannot monopolize shared resources

Integrated with Database:

  • Native SOQL and SOSL support
  • Built-in DML operations
  • Automatic transaction management

Data Types:

// Primitive Types
Integer count = 100;
Long bigNumber = 1000000L;
Double price = 99.99;
Decimal precise = 123.456789;
String name = 'Salesforce';
Boolean isActive = true;
Date today = Date.today();
DateTime now = DateTime.now();
Time currentTime = Time.newInstance(14, 30, 0, 0);

// sObject Types
Account acc = new Account(Name='ACME Corp');
Contact con = new Contact(FirstName='John', LastName='Doe');
Custom_Object__c custom = new Custom_Object__c();

// Collections
List<String> names = new List<String>{'Alice', 'Bob', 'Charlie'};
Set<Id> uniqueIds = new Set<Id>();
Map<Id, Account> accountMap = new Map<Id, Account>();

// Enum
public enum Season {WINTER, SPRING, SUMMER, FALL}

Control Structures:

// If-Else Statement
if (amount > 100000) {
    discount = 0.15;
} else if (amount > 50000) {
    discount = 0.10;
} else {
    discount = 0.05;
}

// Switch Statement (Enhanced in recent versions)
switch on dayOfWeek {
    when 'Monday', 'Tuesday' {
        workload = 'Heavy';
    }
    when 'Wednesday', 'Thursday' {
        workload = 'Medium';
    }
    when 'Friday' {
        workload = 'Light';
    }
    when else {
        workload = 'Weekend';
    }
}

// For Loops
for (Integer i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
    System.debug('Count: ' + i);
}

// Enhanced For Loop
for (Account acc : accountList) {
    System.debug('Account: ' + acc.Name);
}

// SOQL For Loop (Memory Efficient)
for (List<Account> accountBatch : [SELECT Id, Name FROM Account]) {
    // Process batch of 200 records
    for (Account acc : accountBatch) {
        System.debug(acc.Name);
    }
}

// While Loop
while (counter < 10) {
    counter++;
}

// Do-While Loop
do {
    counter++;
} while (counter < 10);

Exception Handling:

try {
    Account acc = [SELECT Id FROM Account WHERE Name = 'Test' LIMIT 1];
    update acc;
} catch (QueryException e) {
    System.debug('Query failed: ' + e.getMessage());
} catch (DmlException e) {
    System.debug('DML failed: ' + e.getMessage());
} catch (Exception e) {
    System.debug('Unexpected error: ' + e.getMessage());
} finally {
    System.debug('Cleanup code here');
}

Access Modifiers:

public class MyClass {
    // Public - Accessible everywhere
    public String publicField;

    // Private - Only within this class
    private String privateField;

    // Protected - This class and subclasses
    protected String protectedField;

    // Global - Accessible across namespaces (managed packages)
    global String globalField;

    // Methods
    public void publicMethod() { }
    private void privateMethod() { }
    protected void protectedMethod() { }
    global void globalMethod() { }
}

Best Practices:

✅ Always bulkify code to handle multiple records

✅ Use collections instead of individual variables

✅ Implement proper exception handling

✅ Follow naming conventions (PascalCase for classes, camelCase for variables)

✅ Keep methods focused and single-purpose

✅ Comment complex logic

Governor Limits:

⚠️ SOQL Queries: 100 per transaction

⚠️ DML Statements: 150 per transaction

⚠️ Heap Size: 6 MB (synchronous), 12 MB (asynchronous)

⚠️ CPU Time: 10,000 ms (synchronous), 60,000 ms (asynchronous)

⚠️ SOQL Query Rows: 50,000 per transaction

Common Apex Patterns:

// Singleton Pattern
public class ConfigurationManager {
    private static ConfigurationManager instance;

    private ConfigurationManager() { }

    public static ConfigurationManager getInstance() {
        if (instance == null) {
            instance = new ConfigurationManager();
        }
        return instance;
    }
}

// Factory Pattern
public class RecordFactory {
    public static SObject createRecord(String objectType) {
        return Schema.getGlobalDescribe().get(objectType).newSObject();
    }
}

// Builder Pattern
public class AccountBuilder {
    private Account acc = new Account();

    public AccountBuilder withName(String name) {
        acc.Name = name;
        return this;
    }

    public AccountBuilder withIndustry(String industry) {
        acc.Industry = industry;
        return this;
    }

    public Account build() {
        return acc;
    }
}

docs.title: Q: What are Apex Triggers and what is the best practice for implementing them?
docs.text:
A: Apex Triggers are pieces of code that execute before or after specific DML operations (insert, update, delete, undelete) on Salesforce records. They enable custom automation that cannot be achieved through declarative tools.

Trigger Events:

Before Triggers:

  • before insert: Before new records are inserted
  • before update: Before existing records are updated
  • before delete: Before records are deleted

After Triggers:

  • after insert: After new records are inserted
  • after update: After existing records are updated
  • after delete: After records are deleted
  • after undelete: After records are restored from Recycle Bin

Trigger Context Variables:

trigger AccountTrigger on Account (before insert, before update, after insert, after update) {
    // Available in all triggers
    System.debug('isExecuting: ' + Trigger.isExecuting);
    System.debug('size: ' + Trigger.size);

    // Before triggers
    if (Trigger.isBefore) {
        // Trigger.new - List of new versions
        // Trigger.newMap - Map of new versions
        // Trigger.old - List of old versions (update/delete only)
        // Trigger.oldMap - Map of old versions (update/delete only)

        System.debug('isInsert: ' + Trigger.isInsert);
        System.debug('isUpdate: ' + Trigger.isUpdate);
    }

    // After triggers
    if (Trigger.isAfter) {
        // Trigger.new - List of new versions (read-only)
        // Trigger.newMap - Map of new versions
        // Trigger.old - List of old versions (update/delete only)
        // Trigger.oldMap - Map of old versions (update/delete only)

        System.debug('isInsert: ' + Trigger.isInsert);
        System.debug('isUpdate: ' + Trigger.isUpdate);
    }
}

❌ BAD PRACTICE - Logic in Trigger:

trigger AccountTrigger on Account (before insert, before update) {
    for (Account acc : Trigger.new) {
        if (acc.AnnualRevenue > 1000000) {
            acc.Rating = 'Hot';
        } else if (acc.AnnualRevenue > 100000) {
            acc.Rating = 'Warm';
        } else {
            acc.Rating = 'Cold';
        }
    }
}

✅ BEST PRACTICE - Trigger Handler Pattern:

// Trigger (Minimal Logic)
trigger AccountTrigger on Account (before insert, before update, after insert, after update, after delete, after undelete) {
    new AccountTriggerHandler().run();
}

// Trigger Handler
public class AccountTriggerHandler {

    public void run() {
        if (Trigger.isBefore) {
            if (Trigger.isInsert) {
                beforeInsert(Trigger.new);
            } else if (Trigger.isUpdate) {
                beforeUpdate(Trigger.new, Trigger.oldMap);
            }
        } else if (Trigger.isAfter) {
            if (Trigger.isInsert) {
                afterInsert(Trigger.new, Trigger.newMap);
            } else if (Trigger.isUpdate) {
                afterUpdate(Trigger.new, Trigger.newMap, Trigger.oldMap);
            } else if (Trigger.isDelete) {
                afterDelete(Trigger.old, Trigger.oldMap);
            } else if (Trigger.isUndelete) {
                afterUndelete(Trigger.new, Trigger.newMap);
            }
        }
    }

    private void beforeInsert(List<Account> newAccounts) {
        setDefaultRating(newAccounts);
        validateBusinessRules(newAccounts);
    }

    private void beforeUpdate(List<Account> newAccounts, Map<Id, Account> oldAccountMap) {
        updateRatingBasedOnRevenue(newAccounts, oldAccountMap);
        preventInvalidUpdates(newAccounts, oldAccountMap);
    }

    private void afterInsert(List<Account> newAccounts, Map<Id, Account> newAccountMap) {
        createDefaultContacts(newAccounts);
        sendWelcomeEmail(newAccounts);
    }

    private void afterUpdate(List<Account> newAccounts, Map<Id, Account> newAccountMap, Map<Id, Account> oldAccountMap) {
        updateRelatedOpportunities(newAccounts, oldAccountMap);
    }

    private void afterDelete(List<Account> oldAccounts, Map<Id, Account> oldAccountMap) {
        // Cleanup related records
    }

    private void afterUndelete(List<Account> newAccounts, Map<Id, Account> newAccountMap) {
        // Restore related data
    }

    // Helper Methods
    private void setDefaultRating(List<Account> accounts) {
        for (Account acc : accounts) {
            if (String.isBlank(acc.Rating)) {
                if (acc.AnnualRevenue > 1000000) {
                    acc.Rating = 'Hot';
                } else if (acc.AnnualRevenue > 100000) {
                    acc.Rating = 'Warm';
                } else {
                    acc.Rating = 'Cold';
                }
            }
        }
    }

    private void validateBusinessRules(List<Account> accounts) {
        for (Account acc : accounts) {
            if (acc.Industry == 'Banking' && String.isBlank(acc.Phone)) {
                acc.addError('Phone is required for Banking accounts');
            }
        }
    }

    private void updateRatingBasedOnRevenue(List<Account> newAccounts, Map<Id, Account> oldAccountMap) {
        for (Account acc : newAccounts) {
            Account oldAcc = oldAccountMap.get(acc.Id);
            if (acc.AnnualRevenue != oldAcc.AnnualRevenue) {
                // Update rating based on new revenue
                setDefaultRating(new List<Account>{acc});
            }
        }
    }

    private void preventInvalidUpdates(List<Account> newAccounts, Map<Id, Account> oldAccountMap) {
        for (Account acc : newAccounts) {
            Account oldAcc = oldAccountMap.get(acc.Id);
            if (oldAcc.Type == 'Customer' && acc.Type != 'Customer') {
                acc.addError('Cannot change Type for existing Customers');
            }
        }
    }

    private void createDefaultContacts(List<Account> accounts) {
        List<Contact> contacts = new List<Contact>();
        for (Account acc : accounts) {
            contacts.add(new Contact(
                AccountId = acc.Id,
                LastName = 'Default Contact',
                Email = 'contact@' + acc.Name.toLowerCase().replace(' ', '') + '.com'
            ));
        }
        if (!contacts.isEmpty()) {
            insert contacts;
        }
    }

    private void sendWelcomeEmail(List<Account> accounts) {
        // Email sending logic
    }

    private void updateRelatedOpportunities(List<Account> newAccounts, Map<Id, Account> oldAccountMap) {
        Set<Id> accountIds = new Set<Id>();
        for (Account acc : newAccounts) {
            Account oldAcc = oldAccountMap.get(acc.Id);
            if (acc.Rating != oldAcc.Rating) {
                accountIds.add(acc.Id);
            }
        }

        if (!accountIds.isEmpty()) {
            List<Opportunity> opps = [
                SELECT Id, AccountId, StageName
                FROM Opportunity
                WHERE AccountId IN :accountIds
                AND StageName NOT IN ('Closed Won', 'Closed Lost')
            ];

            for (Opportunity opp : opps) {
                // Update opportunity based on account rating
            }

            if (!opps.isEmpty()) {
                update opps;
            }
        }
    }
}

Advanced Pattern - Recursion Prevention:

public class TriggerHandler {
    private static Set<String> bypassedHandlers = new Set<String>();

    public static Boolean isBypassed(String handlerName) {
        return bypassedHandlers.contains(handlerName);
    }

    public static void bypass(String handlerName) {
        bypassedHandlers.add(handlerName);
    }

    public static void clearBypass(String handlerName) {
        bypassedHandlers.remove(handlerName);
    }

    public static void clearAllBypasses() {
        bypassedHandlers.clear();
    }
}

public class AccountTriggerHandler {
    private static Boolean isExecuting = false;
    private static Integer executionCount = 0;
    private static final Integer MAX_EXECUTIONS = 5;

    public void run() {
        // Check if handler is bypassed
        if (TriggerHandler.isBypassed('AccountTriggerHandler')) {
            return;
        }

        // Prevent infinite recursion
        if (isExecuting) {
            executionCount++;
            if (executionCount > MAX_EXECUTIONS) {
                throw new TriggerException('Maximum trigger execution depth reached');
            }
        }

        isExecuting = true;

        try {
            // Trigger logic here
        } finally {
            isExecuting = false;
        }
    }

    public class TriggerException extends Exception {}
}

Best Practices:

✅ One trigger per object

✅ Use trigger handler pattern for logic separation

✅ Keep trigger code minimal (1-10 lines)

✅ Bulkify all operations

✅ Implement recursion prevention

✅ Use meaningful method names

✅ Write comprehensive test coverage

✅ Document complex business logic

❌ Never use SOQL/DML inside loops

❌ Don't modify Trigger.new in after triggers

❌ Avoid complex logic directly in triggers

Governor Limits:

⚠️ Maximum 16 trigger levels deep

⚠️ All synchronous governor limits apply

⚠️ CPU timeout after 10 seconds

Common Pitfalls:

❌ Non-Bulkified Queries:

// BAD
for (Account acc : Trigger.new) {
    List<Contact> contacts = [SELECT Id FROM Contact WHERE AccountId = :acc.Id];
}

✅ Bulkified Queries:

// GOOD
Map<Id, List<Contact>> contactsByAccount = new Map<Id, List<Contact>>();
for (Contact con : [SELECT Id, AccountId FROM Contact WHERE AccountId IN :Trigger.newMap.keySet()]) {
    if (!contactsByAccount.containsKey(con.AccountId)) {
        contactsByAccount.put(con.AccountId, new List<Contact>());
    }
    contactsByAccount.get(con.AccountId).add(con);
}

docs.title: Q: What are Lightning Web Components (LWC) and how do they differ from Aura Components?
docs.text:
A: Lightning Web Components (LWC) is Salesforce's modern UI framework built on standard web technologies (HTML, JavaScript, CSS). It provides better performance, smaller file sizes, and uses standard web components specifications.

Key Characteristics:

Standards-Based:

  • Built on Web Components standard
  • Uses modern JavaScript (ES6+)
  • Native browser APIs
  • Better performance and security

Component Structure:

myComponent/
├── myComponent.js          // JavaScript controller
├── myComponent.html        // HTML template
├── myComponent.css         // Component styles
├── myComponent.svg         // Component icon
└── myComponent.js-meta.xml // Component metadata

Basic LWC Example:

<!-- myComponent.html -->
<template>
    <lightning-card title="Account List" icon-name="standard:account">
        <div class="slds-m-around_medium">
            <template if:true={accounts}>
                <template for:each={accounts} for:item="account">
                    <div key={account.Id} class="slds-box slds-m-bottom_small">
                        <p><strong>{account.Name}</strong></p>
                        <p>Industry: {account.Industry}</p>
                        <p>Revenue: {account.AnnualRevenue}</p>
                    </div>
                </template>
            </template>

            <template if:false={accounts}>
                <p>No accounts found.</p>
            </template>

            <template if:true={error}>
                <p class="slds-text-color_error">{error}</p>
            </template>
        </div>
    </lightning-card>
</template>

// myComponent.js
import { LightningElement, wire, track } from 'lwc';
import { ShowToastEvent } from 'lightning/platformShowToastEvent';
import getAccounts from '@salesforce/apex/AccountController.getAccounts';

export default class MyComponent extends LightningElement {
    @track accounts;
    @track error;

    // Wire service to call Apex
    @wire(getAccounts)
    wiredAccounts({ error, data }) {
        if (data) {
            this.accounts = data;
            this.error = undefined;
        } else if (error) {
            this.error = error;
            this.accounts = undefined;
            this.showErrorToast();
        }
    }

    showErrorToast() {
        const event = new ShowToastEvent({
            title: 'Error',
            message: 'Failed to load accounts',
            variant: 'error'
        });
        this.dispatchEvent(event);
    }
}

/* myComponent.css */
.slds-box {
    background-color: #f3f3f3;
    border-radius: 4px;
}

.slds-box:hover {
    background-color: #e8e8e8;
    cursor: pointer;
}

<!-- myComponent.js-meta.xml -->
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<LightningComponentBundle xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata">
    <apiVersion>60.0</apiVersion>
    <isExposed>true</isExposed>
    <targets>
        <target>lightning__AppPage</target>
        <target>lightning__RecordPage</target>
        <target>lightning__HomePage</target>
    </targets>
    <targetConfigs>
        <targetConfig targets="lightning__RecordPage">
            <objects>
                <object>Account</object>
                <object>Contact</object>
            </objects>
        </targetConfig>
    </targetConfigs>
</LightningComponentBundle>

LWC vs. Aura Components:

Performance:

  • LWC: Faster rendering, smaller bundle size
  • Aura: Slower, larger framework overhead

Learning Curve:

  • LWC: Standard JavaScript, easier to learn
  • Aura: Proprietary framework, steeper learning curve

Browser Support:

  • LWC: Modern browsers only
  • Aura: Wider browser support (including older versions)

Interoperability:

  • LWC: Can exist inside Aura components
  • Aura: Cannot exist inside LWC components

Future Support:

  • LWC: Actively developed, recommended for new development
  • Aura: Maintenance mode, no new features

Decorators:

import { LightningElement, api, track, wire } from 'lwc';

export default class MyComponent extends LightningElement {

    // @api - Public property, exposed to parent components
    @api recordId;
    @api objectApiName;

    // @track - Reactive property (auto-rerenders on change)
    @track privateProperty = [];

    // @wire - Wires data from Apex or Lightning Data Service
    @wire(getRecord, { recordId: '$recordId', fields: FIELDS })
    wiredRecord;

    // Computed property (getter)
    get computedValue() {
        return this.privateProperty.length;
    }
}

Lifecycle Hooks:

export default class MyComponent extends LightningElement {

    // Component inserted into DOM
    connectedCallback() {
        console.log('Component connected');
        // Initialize data
        // Add event listeners
    }

    // Component removed from DOM
    disconnectedCallback() {
        console.log('Component disconnected');
        // Cleanup
        // Remove event listeners
    }

    // Called when public property changes
    renderedCallback() {
        console.log('Component rendered');
        // DOM manipulation after render
    }

    // Error handling
    errorCallback(error, stack) {
        console.error('Error occurred:', error);
        console.error('Stack:', stack);
    }
}

Event Handling:

// Child Component - Fire Event
export default class ChildComponent extends LightningElement {
    handleClick() {
        const event = new CustomEvent('selected', {
            detail: { recordId: this.recordId }
        });
        this.dispatchEvent(event);
    }
}

// Parent Component - Handle Event
export default class ParentComponent extends LightningElement {
    handleSelected(event) {
        const recordId = event.detail.recordId;
        console.log('Selected record:', recordId);
    }
}

<!-- Parent Component Template -->
<template>
    <c-child-component onselected={handleSelected}></c-child-component>
</template>

Lightning Data Service:

import { LightningElement, wire, api } from 'lwc';
import { getRecord, updateRecord } from 'lightning/uiRecordApi';
import ACCOUNT_NAME_FIELD from '@salesforce/schema/Account.Name';

export default class AccountEditor extends LightningElement {
    @api recordId;

    @wire(getRecord, { recordId: '$recordId', fields: [ACCOUNT_NAME_FIELD] })
    account;

    handleNameChange(event) {
        const fields = {};
        fields[ACCOUNT_NAME_FIELD.fieldApiName] = event.target.value;
        fields['Id'] = this.recordId;

        const recordInput = { fields };

        updateRecord(recordInput)
            .then(() => {
                // Success
            })
            .catch(error => {
                // Handle error
            });
    }
}

Best Practices:

✅ Use LWC for new development

✅ Leverage standard Lightning Base Components

✅ Follow unidirectional data flow

✅ Keep components focused and reusable

✅ Use @wire for efficient data loading

✅ Implement proper error handling

✅ Use Lightning Data Service when possible

✅ Follow naming conventions

Common Patterns:

// Imperative Apex Call
import { LightningElement } from 'lwc';
import getAccountList from '@salesforce/apex/AccountController.getAccountList';

export default class AccountList extends LightningElement {
    accounts;
    error;

    async connectedCallback() {
        try {
            this.accounts = await getAccountList();
        } catch (error) {
            this.error = error;
        }
    }
}

// Navigation
import { NavigationMixin } from 'lightning/navigation';

export default class NavigationExample extends NavigationMixin(LightningElement) {
    navigateToRecord() {
        this[NavigationMixin.Navigate]({
            type: 'standard__recordPage',
            attributes: {
                recordId: this.recordId,
                objectApiName: 'Account',
                actionName: 'view'
            }
        });
    }
}

// Custom Labels
import customLabel from '@salesforce/label/c.CustomLabel';

export default class LabelExample extends LightningElement {
    label = customLabel;
}

Salesforce Edition Requirements:

  • ✅ Available in all Lightning Experience editions
  • ✅ Not available in Salesforce Classic

docs.title: Q: What are the requirements for Apex test classes and how do you write effective tests?
docs.text:
A: Apex test classes are required for deploying code to production. Salesforce requires at least 75% code coverage for deployment, but more importantly, tests should verify business logic and ensure code quality.

Test Class Basics:

@isTest
private class AccountTriggerTest {

    // Test setup method (runs once before all tests)
    @TestSetup
    static void setupTestData() {
        List<Account> accounts = new List<Account>();
        for (Integer i = 0; i < 200; i++) {
            accounts.add(new Account(
                Name = 'Test Account ' + i,
                Industry = 'Technology',
                AnnualRevenue = 100000 * i
            ));
        }
        insert accounts;
    }

    // Positive test case
    @isTest
    static void testAccountInsert_WithRevenue_SetsRatingCorrectly() {
        // Arrange
        Account acc = new Account(
            Name = 'Test High Revenue Account',
            AnnualRevenue = 2000000
        );

        // Act
        Test.startTest();
        insert acc;
        Test.stopTest();

        // Assert
        Account inserted = [SELECT Id, Rating FROM Account WHERE Id = :acc.Id];
        System.assertEquals('Hot', inserted.Rating, 'Rating should be Hot for high revenue');
    }

    // Negative test case
    @isTest
    static void testAccountUpdate_InvalidType_ThrowsError() {
        // Arrange
        Account acc = new Account(
            Name = 'Test Customer Account',
            Type = 'Customer'
        );
        insert acc;

        // Act & Assert
        acc.Type = 'Prospect';
        try {
            Test.startTest();
            update acc;
            Test.stopTest();
            System.assert(false, 'Expected exception was not thrown');
        } catch (DmlException e) {
            System.assert(e.getMessage().contains('Cannot change Type'), 
                         'Exception message should indicate type change restriction');
        }
    }

    // Bulk test case
    @isTest
    static void testAccountTrigger_BulkInsert_ProcessesAllRecords() {
        // Arrange
        List<Account> accounts = new List<Account>();
        for (Integer i = 0; i < 200; i++) {
            accounts.add(new Account(
                Name = 'Bulk Test Account ' + i,
                AnnualRevenue = 500000
            ));
        }

        // Act
        Test.startTest();
        insert accounts;
        Test.stopTest();

        // Assert
        List<Account> inserted = [SELECT Id, Rating FROM Account WHERE Name LIKE 'Bulk Test Account%'];
        System.assertEquals(200, inserted.size(), 'All 200 accounts should be inserted');
        for (Account acc : inserted) {
            System.assertEquals('Warm', acc.Rating, 'All accounts should have Warm rating');
        }
    }
}

Test Requirements:

Code Coverage:

⚠️ Minimum 75% code coverage for deployment

⚠️ 100% coverage for triggers recommended

⚠️ Every trigger must have test coverage

⚠️ All Apex classes must have test coverage

Best Practices:

✅ Test both positive and negative scenarios

✅ Test bulk operations (200+ records)

✅ Use meaningful test method names

✅ Follow Arrange-Act-Assert pattern

✅ Use @TestSetup for common test data

✅ Test governor limits

✅ Verify all business logic

✅ Test with different user profiles

Test.startTest() and Test.stopTest():

@isTest
static void testAsynchronousApex() {
    // Arrange
    Account acc = new Account(Name = 'Test Account');
    insert acc;

    // Act
    Test.startTest(); // Resets governor limits
    // Call asynchronous method
    MyAsyncClass.processRecords(acc.Id);
    Test.stopTest(); // Forces async execution to complete

    // Assert - async processing completed
    Account updated = [SELECT Id, Status__c FROM Account WHERE Id = :acc.Id];
    System.assertEquals('Processed', updated.Status__c);
}

Testing Callouts:

@isTest
private class MyWebServiceTest {

    // Mock HTTP callout
    private class MockHttpResponse implements HttpCalloutMock {
        public HttpResponse respond(HttpRequest req) {
            HttpResponse res = new HttpResponse();
            res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json');
            res.setBody('{"status":"success","data":"test"}');
            res.setStatusCode(200);
            return res;
        }
    }

    @isTest
    static void testWebServiceCall() {
        // Arrange
        Test.setMock(HttpCalloutMock.class, new MockHttpResponse());

        // Act
        Test.startTest();
        String result = MyWebService.makeCallout('https://api.example.com/data');
        Test.stopTest();

        // Assert
        System.assertNotEquals(null, result);
        System.assert(result.contains('success'));
    }
}

Testing with Different Users:

@isTest
static void testWithStandardUser() {
    // Create test user
    Profile p = [SELECT Id FROM Profile WHERE Name = 'Standard User' LIMIT 1];
    User testUser = new User(
        Alias = 'testuser',
        Email = 'testuser@example.com',
        EmailEncodingKey = 'UTF-8',
        LastName = 'Testing',
        LanguageLocaleKey = 'en_US',
        LocaleSidKey = 'en_US',
        ProfileId = p.Id,
        TimeZoneSidKey = 'America/Los_Angeles',
        Username = 'testuser' + DateTime.now().getTime() + '@example.com'
    );
    insert testUser;

    // Run test as specific user
    System.runAs(testUser) {
        // Test code here
        Account acc = new Account(Name = 'Test Account');
        insert acc;

        // Assertions
        System.assertNotEquals(null, acc.Id);
    }
}

Test Data Factory:

@isTest
public class TestDataFactory {

    public static Account createAccount(String name, Boolean doInsert) {
        Account acc = new Account(
            Name = name,
            Industry = 'Technology',
            AnnualRevenue = 1000000
        );
        if (doInsert) {
            insert acc;
        }
        return acc;
    }

    public static List<Account> createAccounts(Integer count, Boolean doInsert) {
        List<Account> accounts = new List<Account>();
        for (Integer i = 0; i < count; i++) {
            accounts.add(new Account(
                Name = 'Test Account ' + i,
                Industry = 'Technology',
                AnnualRevenue = 100000 * i
            ));
        }
        if (doInsert) {
            insert accounts;
        }
        return accounts;
    }

    public static Contact createContact(Id accountId, Boolean doInsert) {
        Contact con = new Contact(
            AccountId = accountId,
            FirstName = 'Test',
            LastName = 'Contact',
            Email = 'test@example.com'
        );
        if (doInsert) {
            insert con;
        }
        return con;
    }
}

// Usage in test class
@isTest
static void testAccountCreation() {
    // Arrange
    Account acc = TestDataFactory.createAccount('Test Account', true);

    // Act & Assert
    System.assertNotEquals(null, acc.Id);
}

Testing Exceptions:

@isTest
static void testException_NullPointer() {
    // Arrange
    String nullString = null;

    // Act & Assert
    try {
        Test.startTest();
        Integer length = nullString.length(); // Will throw NullPointerException
        Test.stopTest();
        System.assert(false, 'Should have thrown exception');
    } catch (NullPointerException e) {
        System.assert(true, 'Correctly caught NullPointerException');
    }
}

Governor Limit Testing:

@isTest
static void testGovernorLimits() {
    // Arrange
    List<Account> accounts = TestDataFactory.createAccounts(200, true);

    // Act
    Test.startTest();
    // Perform operations
    MyBatchClass batch = new MyBatchClass();
    Database.executeBatch(batch, 200);
    Test.stopTest();

    // Assert governor limits
    System.debug('SOQL Queries: ' + Limits.getQueries() + '/' + Limits.getLimitQueries());
    System.debug('DML Statements: ' + Limits.getDmlStatements() + '/' + Limits.getLimitDmlStatements());
    System.debug('Heap Size: ' + Limits.getHeapSize() + '/' + Limits.getLimitHeapSize());

    // Verify within limits
    System.assert(Limits.getQueries() < Limits.getLimitQueries(), 'SOQL queries exceeded');
    System.assert(Limits.getDmlStatements() < Limits.getLimitDmlStatements(), 'DML statements exceeded');
}

Common Testing Mistakes:

❌ Not testing bulk operations

❌ Using hard-coded IDs

❌ Not testing negative scenarios

❌ Creating test data in every method

❌ Not verifying all assertions

❌ Testing only happy path

❌ Ignoring code coverage quality

Best Testing Patterns:

@isTest
private class ComprehensiveTestClass {

    // Test with different user
    @isTest

        // System.runAs()
    }

}

Test Coverage Report:

docs.title: Q: What are the best practices for debugging Apex code in Salesforce?
docs.text:
A: Debugging in Salesforce involves using Debug Logs, System.debug statements, Developer Console, and understanding log levels to efficiently troubleshoot issues.

Debug Log Basics:

Setting Up Debug Logs:

  1. Setup → Debug Logs
  2. Click New
  3. Select User to trace
  4. Set expiration (maximum 24 hours)
  5. Click Save

Log Categories and Levels:

Categories:
- Database
- Workflow
- Validation
- Callout
- Apex Code
- Apex Profiling
- Visualforce
- System

Levels (from least to most verbose):
- NONE
- ERROR
- WARN
- INFO
- DEBUG
- FINE
- FINER
- FINEST

System.debug() Statements:

public class DebugExample {

    public static void processAccounts() {
        // Basic debug
        System.debug('Starting account processing');

        // Debug with log level
        System.debug(LoggingLevel.INFO, 'Processing started at ' + DateTime.now());
        System.debug(LoggingLevel.ERROR, 'Critical error occurred');
        System.debug(LoggingLevel.WARN, 'Warning: Low memory');

        // Debug variables
        Integer recordCount = 0;
        System.debug('Record count: ' + recordCount);

        // Debug objects
        Account acc = new Account(Name = 'Test');
        System.debug('Account details: ' + acc);

        // Debug collections
        List<Account> accounts = [SELECT Id, Name FROM Account LIMIT 10];
        System.debug('Accounts retrieved: ' + accounts.size());
        System.debug('Account list: ' + accounts);

        // Debug with JSON
        System.debug('Account JSON: ' + JSON.serialize(acc));

        // Debug in loops
        for (Account a : accounts) {
            System.debug('Processing account: ' + a.Name + ' (ID: ' + a.Id + ')');
        }

        // Debug governor limits
        System.debug('SOQL Queries used: ' + Limits.getQueries() + '/' + Limits.getLimitQueries());
        System.debug('DML Statements: ' + Limits.getDmlStatements() + '/' + Limits.getLimitDmlStatements());
        System.debug('CPU Time: ' + Limits.getCpuTime() + '/' + Limits.getLimitCpuTime());
        System.debug('Heap Size: ' + Limits.getHeapSize() + '/' + Limits.getLimitHeapSize());
    }
}

Analyzing Debug Logs:

Log Analysis Panel in Developer Console:

EXECUTION_STARTED
CODE_UNIT_STARTED: [EXTERNAL]|[EXTERNAL]
USER_DEBUG: [1]|DEBUG|Starting account processing
SOQL_EXECUTE_BEGIN: [2]|Aggregations:0|SELECT Id, Name FROM Account LIMIT 10
SOQL_EXECUTE_END: [2]|Rows:10
USER_DEBUG: [3]|DEBUG|Accounts retrieved: 10
CUMULATIVE_LIMIT_USAGE
  SOQL queries: 1 out of 100
  DML statements: 0 out of 150
CODE_UNIT_FINISHED
EXECUTION_FINISHED

Common Debug Patterns:

// 1. Entry/Exit Logging
public void myMethod(String param) {
    System.debug('>>> Entering myMethod with param: ' + param);
    try {
        // Method logic
        System.debug('Processing completed successfully');
    } catch (Exception e) {
        System.debug('### ERROR: ' + e.getMessage());
        System.debug('### Stack trace: ' + e.getStackTraceString());
        throw e;
    } finally {
        System.debug('<<< Exiting myMethod');
    }
}

// 2. Conditional Debugging
public void processData(List<Account> accounts) {
    Boolean debugMode = true; // Toggle for detailed logging

    if (debugMode) {
        System.debug('=== Starting processData ===');
        System.debug('Input size: ' + accounts.size());
    }

    for (Account acc : accounts) {
        if (debugMode) {
            System.debug('Processing: ' + acc.Name);
        }
        // Processing logic
    }

    if (debugMode) {
        System.debug('=== Finished processData ===');
    }
}

// 3. Performance Debugging
public void performanceTest() {
    Long startTime = System.currentTimeMillis();
    System.debug('Start time: ' + startTime);

    // Code to measure
    List<Account> accounts = [SELECT Id, Name FROM Account LIMIT 1000];

    Long endTime = System.currentTimeMillis();
    System.debug('End time: ' + endTime);
    System.debug('Execution time: ' + (endTime - startTime) + ' ms');

    // Check limits
    System.debug('CPU time used: ' + Limits.getCpuTime() + ' ms');
    System.debug('Heap size: ' + Limits.getHeapSize() + ' bytes');
}

// 4. Data Validation Debugging
public void validateData(Account acc) {
    System.debug('=== Validating Account ===');

    System.debug('Name: ' + (String.isBlank(acc.Name) ? 'MISSING' : acc.Name));
    System.debug('Phone: ' + (String.isBlank(acc.Phone) ? 'MISSING' : acc.Phone));
    System.debug('Industry: ' + (acc.Industry == null ? 'NULL' : acc.Industry));

    if (String.isBlank(acc.Name)) {
        System.debug('ERROR: Name is required');
    }
}

Developer Console Features:

Checkpoint Debugging:

1. Open Developer Console
2. File > Open > Apex Class
3. Set breakpoints by clicking line numbers
4. Execute > Debug > Start Checkpoint Debugging
5. Run operation that triggers code
6. View variable values at checkpoints

Query Editor:

// Test SOQL queries
SELECT Id, Name, Industry, AnnualRevenue
FROM Account
WHERE Industry = 'Technology'
ORDER BY AnnualRevenue DESC
LIMIT 10

Anonymous Execution:

// Debug > Open Execute Anonymous Window
// Paste code and execute

// Test trigger behavior
Account acc = new Account(Name = 'Debug Test', AnnualRevenue = 2000000);
insert acc;

System.debug('Account created: ' + acc.Id);
Account inserted = [SELECT Id, Name, Rating FROM Account WHERE Id = :acc.Id];
System.debug('Rating: ' + inserted.Rating);

Advanced Debugging Techniques:

// Custom Debug Class
public class DebugHelper {

    private static final Boolean DEBUG_ENABLED = true;

    public static void log(String message) {
        if (DEBUG_ENABLED) {
            System.debug(LoggingLevel.INFO, '### ' + message);
        }
    }

    public static void logError(String message, Exception e) {
        System.debug(LoggingLevel.ERROR, '### ERROR: ' + message);
        System.debug(LoggingLevel.ERROR, '### Exception: ' + e.getMessage());
        System.debug(LoggingLevel.ERROR, '### Stack: ' + e.getStackTraceString());
    }

    public static void logLimits() {
        System.debug('### GOVERNOR LIMITS ###');
        System.debug('SOQL: ' + Limits.getQueries() + '/' + Limits.getLimitQueries());
        System.debug('DML: ' + Limits.getDmlStatements() + '/' + Limits.getLimitDmlStatements());
        System.debug('CPU: ' + Limits.getCpuTime() + '/' + Limits.getLimitCpuTime());
        System.debug('Heap: ' + Limits.getHeapSize() + '/' + Limits.getLimitHeapSize());
    }

    public static void logObject(String label, SObject obj) {
        System.debug('### ' + label + ': ' + JSON.serializePretty(obj));
    }

    public static void logCollection(String label, List<SObject> records) {
        System.debug('### ' + label + ' (Size: ' + records.size() + ')');
        for (Integer i = 0; i < Math.min(5, records.size()); i++) {
            System.debug('  [' + i + ']: ' + records[i]);
        }
        if (records.size() > 5) {
            System.debug('  ... and ' + (records.size() - 5) + ' more');
        }
    }
}

// Usage
DebugHelper.log('Processing started');
DebugHelper.logObject('Account', acc);
DebugHelper.logLimits();

Log Filtering:

// In Developer Console Logs tab:
// Use filters to find specific messages

// Filter examples:
USER_DEBUG          // Show only debug statements
SOQL_EXECUTE        // Show SOQL queries
DML_BEGIN           // Show DML operations
EXCEPTION_THROWN    // Show exceptions
FATAL_ERROR         // Show fatal errors

Best Practices:

✅ Use descriptive debug messages with context

✅ Include variable values in debug statements

✅ Log entry and exit of important methods

✅ Check governor limits periodically

✅ Use appropriate log levels (ERROR, WARN, INFO, DEBUG)

✅ Remove or comment out debug statements before deployment

✅ Use structured logging (prefixes like ###, ===, >>>)

✅ Log exceptions with full stack traces

Common Debugging Scenarios:

// Null Pointer Exception
try {
    System.debug('Account name length: ' + acc.Name.length());
} catch (NullPointerException e) {
    System.debug('ERROR: Account or Name is null');
    System.debug('Account: ' + acc);
}

// List Index Out of Bounds
if (!accounts.isEmpty()) {
    System.debug('First account: ' + accounts[0]);
} else {
    System.debug('WARNING: Account list is empty');
}

// SOQL No Rows Exception
List<Account> accounts = [SELECT Id FROM Account WHERE Name = :searchName];
if (accounts.isEmpty()) {
    System.debug('No accounts found with name: ' + searchName);
} else {
    System.debug('Found ' + accounts.size() + ' accounts');
}

// DML Exception
try {
    insert accounts;
} catch (DmlException e) {
    System.debug('DML failed: ' + e.getMessage());
    System.debug('Failed index: ' + e.getDmlIndex(0));
    System.debug('Failed record: ' + accounts[e.getDmlIndex(0)]);
}

Governor Limit Debugging:

public void monitorLimits() {
    Limits.LimitContext context = Limits.getContext();
    System.debug('=== LIMIT MONITORING ===');
    System.debug('SOQL: ' + Limits.getQueries() + '/' + Limits.getLimitQueries());
    System.debug('SOQL Rows: ' + Limits.getQueryRows() + '/' + Limits.getLimitQueryRows());
    System.debug('DML: ' + Limits.getDmlStatements() + '/' + Limits.getLimitDmlStatements());
    System.debug('DML Rows: ' + Limits.getDmlRows() + '/' + Limits.getLimitDmlRows());
    System.debug('CPU: ' + Limits.getCpuTime() + '/' + Limits.getLimitCpuTime());
    System.debug('Heap: ' + Limits.getHeapSize() + '/' + Limits.getLimitHeapSize());
    System.debug('Callouts: ' + Limits.getCallouts() + '/' + Limits.getLimitCallouts());
}
