docs.title: Q: Your company sells software bundles: Basic (Product A), Professional (Products A+B), Enterprise (Products A+B+C). When a rep selects "Enterprise Bundle," all three products should auto-populate on the opportunity with correct pricing. How do you build this?
docs.text:
A: This requires Product Bundles with Price Books and automation using Flow or Apex to add bundle components.

Solution Architecture:

Configuration Steps:

Step 1: Create Product Records

Navigate to: Setup → Products → Products

Individual Products: 

Product A - Core Software
- Product Code: CORE-001
- Product Family: Software
- Active: Yes

Product B - Advanced Features  
- Product Code: ADV-002
- Product Family: Add-On
- Active: Yes

Product C - Enterprise Features
- Product Code: ENT-003
- Product Family: Add-On
- Active: Yes

Bundle Products: 

Basic Bundle
- Product Code: BUNDLE-BASIC
- Product Family: Bundle
- Is Bundle: Yes (custom checkbox)

Professional Bundle
- Product Code: BUNDLE-PRO
- Product Family: Bundle
- Is Bundle: Yes

Enterprise Bundle
- Product Code: BUNDLE-ENT
- Product Family: Bundle
- Is Bundle: Yes

Step 2: Create Custom Object for Bundle Configuration

Object Name: Product_Bundle_Item__c

Fields: 

Bundle_Product__c (Master-Detail to Product2)
Component_Product__c (Lookup to Product2)
Quantity__c (Number)
Sequence__c (Number) - Display order
Discount_Percentage__c (Percent) - Bundle discount
Is_Optional__c (Checkbox)

Bundle Configuration Records:

Basic Bundle Items: 

Bundle: Basic Bundle → Component: Product A, Qty: 1, Sequence: 1

Professional Bundle Items: 

Bundle: Professional Bundle → Component: Product A, Qty: 1, Sequence: 1
Bundle: Professional Bundle → Component: Product B, Qty: 1, Sequence: 2

Enterprise Bundle Items: 

Bundle: Enterprise Bundle → Component: Product A, Qty: 1, Sequence: 1
Bundle: Enterprise Bundle → Component: Product B, Qty: 1, Sequence: 2
Bundle: Enterprise Bundle → Component: Product C, Qty: 1, Sequence: 3

Step 3: Configure Price Books

Standard Price Book: 

Product A: $10,000/year
Product B: $5,000/year
Product C: $8,000/year
Basic Bundle: $9,000/year (10% discount)
Professional Bundle: $13,500/year (10% discount)
Enterprise Bundle: $20,700/year (10% discount)

Custom Price Books (Optional): - Partner Price Book - Volume Discount Price Book - Educational Price Book

Step 4: Create Apex Class for Bundle Processing

public class ProductBundleService {

    // Add bundle to opportunity
    public static List<OpportunityLineItem> addBundleToOpportunity(
        Id opportunityId, Id bundleProductId, Decimal quantity) {

        List<OpportunityLineItem> lineItems = new List<OpportunityLineItem>();

        // Get opportunity details
        Opportunity opp = [
            SELECT Id, Pricebook2Id 
            FROM Opportunity 
            WHERE Id = :opportunityId
        ];

        // Get bundle components
        List<Product_Bundle_Item__c> bundleItems = [
            SELECT Component_Product__c, Quantity__c, Sequence__c, 
                   Discount_Percentage__c, Is_Optional__c
            FROM Product_Bundle_Item__c
            WHERE Bundle_Product__c = :bundleProductId
            ORDER BY Sequence__c
        ];

        // Get price book entries for components
        Set<Id> componentProductIds = new Set<Id>();
        for (Product_Bundle_Item__c item : bundleItems) {
            componentProductIds.add(item.Component_Product__c);
        }

        Map<Id, PricebookEntry> productToPbeMap = getPricebookEntries(
            opp.Pricebook2Id, 
            componentProductIds
        );

        // Create opportunity line items for each component
        for (Product_Bundle_Item__c bundleItem : bundleItems) {
            if (!bundleItem.Is_Optional__c) {
                PricebookEntry pbe = productToPbeMap.get(bundleItem.Component_Product__c);

                if (pbe != null) {
                    OpportunityLineItem oli = new OpportunityLineItem(
                        OpportunityId = opportunityId,
                        PricebookEntryId = pbe.Id,
                        Quantity = bundleItem.Quantity__c * quantity,
                        UnitPrice = pbe.UnitPrice,
                        Discount = bundleItem.Discount_Percentage__c,
                        Bundle_Parent__c = bundleProductId, // Custom field
                        Sequence__c = bundleItem.Sequence__c
                    );
                    lineItems.add(oli);
                }
            }
        }

        // Insert line items
        if (!lineItems.isEmpty()) {
            insert lineItems;
        }

        return lineItems;
    }

    // Get pricebook entries
    private static Map<Id, PricebookEntry> getPricebookEntries(
        Id pricebookId, Set<Id> productIds) {

        Map<Id, PricebookEntry> productToPbeMap = new Map<Id, PricebookEntry>();

        List<PricebookEntry> entries = [
            SELECT Id, Product2Id, UnitPrice, IsActive
            FROM PricebookEntry
            WHERE Pricebook2Id = :pricebookId
            AND Product2Id IN :productIds
            AND IsActive = true
        ];

        for (PricebookEntry pbe : entries) {
            productToPbeMap.put(pbe.Product2Id, pbe);
        }

        return productToPbeMap;
    }

    // Remove bundle from opportunity
    public static void removeBundleFromOpportunity(Id bundleProductId, Id opportunityId) {
        List<OpportunityLineItem> lineItemsToDelete = [
            SELECT Id
            FROM OpportunityLineItem
            WHERE OpportunityId = :opportunityId
            AND Bundle_Parent__c = :bundleProductId
        ];

        if (!lineItemsToDelete.isEmpty()) {
            delete lineItemsToDelete;
        }
    }

    // Calculate bundle total
    public static Decimal calculateBundleTotal(Id bundleProductId, Id pricebookId) {
        Decimal total = 0;

        List<Product_Bundle_Item__c> bundleItems = [
            SELECT Component_Product__c, Quantity__c, Discount_Percentage__c
            FROM Product_Bundle_Item__c
            WHERE Bundle_Product__c = :bundleProductId
        ];

        Set<Id> componentIds = new Set<Id>();
        for (Product_Bundle_Item__c item : bundleItems) {
            componentIds.add(item.Component_Product__c);
        }

        Map<Id, PricebookEntry> pbeMap = getPricebookEntries(pricebookId, componentIds);

        for (Product_Bundle_Item__c item : bundleItems) {
            PricebookEntry pbe = pbeMap.get(item.Component_Product__c);
            if (pbe != null) {
                Decimal itemTotal = pbe.UnitPrice * item.Quantity__c;
                Decimal discount = item.Discount_Percentage__c != null ? 
                    item.Discount_Percentage__c / 100 : 0;
                itemTotal = itemTotal * (1 - discount);
                total += itemTotal;
            }
        }

        return total;
    }
}

Step 5: Create Lightning Web Component for Bundle Selection

// bundleSelector.js
import { LightningElement, api, wire, track } from 'lwc';
import { ShowToastEvent } from 'lightning/platformShowToastEvent';
import { getRecord } from 'lightning/uiRecordApi';
import addBundleToOpportunity from '@salesforce/apex/ProductBundleService.addBundleToOpportunity';

const FIELDS = ['Opportunity.Pricebook2Id'];

export default class BundleSelector extends LightningElement {
    @api recordId; // Opportunity Id
    @track selectedBundle;
    @track quantity = 1;
    @track isLoading = false;

    bundleOptions = [
        { label: 'Basic Bundle', value: 'BUNDLE-BASIC' },
        { label: 'Professional Bundle', value: 'BUNDLE-PRO' },
        { label: 'Enterprise Bundle', value: 'BUNDLE-ENT' }
    ];

    @wire(getRecord, { recordId: '$recordId', fields: FIELDS })
    opportunity;

    handleBundleChange(event) {
        this.selectedBundle = event.detail.value;
    }

    handleQuantityChange(event) {
        this.quantity = event.detail.value;
    }

    handleAddBundle() {
        if (!this.selectedBundle) {
            this.showToast('Error', 'Please select a bundle', 'error');
            return;
        }

        this.isLoading = true;

        addBundleToOpportunity({
            opportunityId: this.recordId,
            bundleProductId: this.selectedBundle,
            quantity: this.quantity
        })
        .then(() => {
            this.showToast('Success', 'Bundle added successfully', 'success');
            this.isLoading = false;
            // Refresh the page
            eval("$A.get('e.force:refreshView').fire();");
        })
        .catch(error => {
            this.showToast('Error', error.body.message, 'error');
            this.isLoading = false;
        });
    }

    showToast(title, message, variant) {
        const event = new ShowToastEvent({
            title: title,
            message: message,
            variant: variant
        });
        this.dispatchEvent(event);
    }
}

<!-- bundleSelector.html -->
<template>
    <lightning-card title="Add Product Bundle" icon-name="standard:product">
        <div class="slds-p-around_medium">
            <lightning-combobox
                name="bundle"
                label="Select Bundle"
                value={selectedBundle}
                placeholder="Choose a bundle"
                options={bundleOptions}
                onchange={handleBundleChange}
            ></lightning-combobox>

            <lightning-input
                type="number"
                label="Quantity"
                value={quantity}
                min="1"
                onchange={handleQuantityChange}
            ></lightning-input>

            <div class="slds-m-top_medium">
                <lightning-button
                    variant="brand"
                    label="Add Bundle to Opportunity"
                    onclick={handleAddBundle}
                    disabled={isLoading}
                ></lightning-button>
            </div>

            <div if:true={isLoading}>
                <lightning-spinner
                    alternative-text="Loading"
                    size="small"
                ></lightning-spinner>
            </div>
        </div>
    </lightning-card>
</template>

Step 6: Create Flow Alternative (No-Code Solution)

Flow Name: Add Product Bundle

Screen 1: Select Bundle - Radio buttons for bundle selection - Number input for quantity

Decision: Which Bundle Selected?

Branch 1: Basic Bundle - Get Records: Bundle configuration for Basic - Loop through components - Create Opportunity Line Items

Branch 2: Professional Bundle - Get Records: Bundle configuration for Professional - Loop through components - Create Opportunity Line Items

Branch 3: Enterprise Bundle - Get Records: Bundle configuration for Enterprise - Loop through components - Create Opportunity Line Items

Final Screen: Success message

Step 7: Create Custom Button on Opportunity

Button Name: Add Product Bundle Display Type: Detail Page Button Behavior: Display in existing window with sidebar Content Source: Lightning Component (bundleSelector)

Step 8: Create Validation Rules

// Prevent manual product addition if bundle exists
AND(
    ISCHANGED(Product2Id),
    NOT(ISBLANK(Bundle_Parent__c)),
    $Profile.Name != 'System Administrator'
)

Error Message: "Cannot modify bundle components directly. Remove bundle and re-add."

// Ensure bundle products have all components
AND(
    ISPICKVAL(Product2.Product_Family__c, 'Bundle'),
    ISBLANK(Bundle_Parent__c)
)

Error Message: "Bundle must be added using the Add Product Bundle button."

Step 9: Create Reports for Bundle Analysis

Bundle Sales Report: - Opportunities with Products - Filter: Product Family = "Bundle" - Group by: Product Name, Close Date - Show: Amount, Quantity, Win Rate

Bundle Component Analysis: - Products sold - Filter: Bundle Parent is not null - Show: Which bundle components sell most frequently

Key Considerations:

  • Price Book Management: Maintain bundle prices separately from components
  • Discount Strategy: Apply bundle-level discounts vs component discounts
  • Product Activation: Ensure all components are active
  • Quantity Handling: Support variable quantities for bundles
  • Bundle Modifications: Allow sales to customize bundles if needed

Advanced Features:

Optional Components: - Mark components as optional in bundle configuration - Allow sales to add/remove optional items - Adjust pricing dynamically

Tiered Pricing: - Volume discounts for larger quantities - Annual vs monthly pricing - Multi-year commits with additional discounts

Bundle Upgrades: - Automation to upgrade from Basic → Professional → Enterprise - Prorate pricing for mid-term upgrades - Track upgrade path for renewal management

Governor Limits:

⚠️ Products per Pricebook: 10,000 products per price book ⚠️ Line Items per Opportunity: 2,000 line items maximum ⚠️ Price Books: 3,000 active price books maximum ⚠️ SOQL Queries: Bulkified queries in trigger context

Salesforce Edition Requirements:

  • ✅ Professional Edition: Products and price books
  • ✅ Enterprise Edition: Multiple price books, products
  • ✅ Unlimited Edition: All features
  • ❌ Essentials: Products not available

Best Practices:

✅ Use custom objects to configure bundles declaratively ✅ Create reusable Apex service class for bundle operations ✅ Build Lightning component for better user experience ✅ Maintain separate price book entries for bundles ✅ Document bundle composition for sales team ✅ Create product selector guide for reps ✅ Monitor bundle vs individual product sales ✅ Review bundle pricing quarterly ✅ Test thoroughly with different quantities ✅ Provide clear error messages to users

docs.title: Q: Create an abandoned opportunity workflow: If opportunity stage hasn't changed in 30 days and probability <50%, send escalation email to manager and create high-priority task for rep. How do you build this?
docs.text:
A: This requires time-based automation using Scheduled Flow with date-based criteria to identify and escalate stagnant opportunities.

Solution Architecture:

Configuration Steps:

Step 1: Create Custom Fields

Last_Stage_Change_Date__c (Date)
- Formula: IF(ISCHANGED(StageName), TODAY(), Last_Stage_Change_Date__c)
- Track when stage last changed

Days_In_Current_Stage__c (Number)
- Formula: TODAY() - Last_Stage_Change_Date__c
- Calculate days since last stage change

Is_Stagnant__c (Checkbox)
- Formula: AND(Days_In_Current_Stage__c > 30, Probability < 0.50, NOT(IsClosed))
- Identify stagnant opportunities

Escalation_Count__c (Number)
- Track number of escalations

Last_Escalation_Date__c (Date)
- Track most recent escalation

Step 2: Create Scheduled Flow

Flow Name: Escalate Stagnant Opportunities

Schedule: Daily at 8:00 AM

Flow Logic:

Get Records: 

Object: Opportunity
Filter Conditions:
- Is_Stagnant__c = True
- IsClosed = False
- Last_Escalation_Date__c < TODAY() - 7 (prevent daily spam)
OR Last_Escalation_Date__c = null

Order By: Days_In_Current_Stage__c DESC

Loop Through Opportunities:

For each stagnant opportunity:

Action 1: Get Manager Information 

Get Records: User
Filter: Id = {!Opportunity.Owner.ManagerId}
Store in: ManagerUser

Action 2: Create High Priority Task 

Object: Task
Fields:
- Subject: "URGENT: Follow up on stagnant opportunity - " + {!Opportunity.Name}
- Priority: High
- Status: Not Started  
- ActivityDate: TODAY() + 2
- WhoId: {!Opportunity.Owner.ContactId}
- WhatId: {!Opportunity.Id}
- OwnerId: {!Opportunity.OwnerId}
- Description: "This opportunity has been in " + {!Opportunity.StageName} + 
               " stage for " + {!Opportunity.Days_In_Current_Stage__c} + 
               " days without progress. Please take immediate action."

Action 3: Send Email to Manager 

Send Email Action:
Recipient: {!ManagerUser.Email}
Email Template: Stagnant_Opportunity_Manager_Alert
Record ID: {!Opportunity.Id}

Additional To: {!Opportunity.Owner.Email}

Action 4: Update Opportunity 

Update Records:
- Escalation_Count__c = {!Opportunity.Escalation_Count__c} + 1
- Last_Escalation_Date__c = TODAY()
- Escalation_Status__c = "Escalated to Manager"

Action 5: Post to Chatter 

Post to Chatter:
Target: Opportunity Record
Message: "@" + {!ManagerUser.Name} + " - This opportunity has been stagnant for " +
         {!Opportunity.Days_In_Current_Stage__c} + " days. Owner: @" + 
         {!Opportunity.Owner.Name}

Step 3: Create Email Templates

Manager Alert Template (HTML):

<messaging:emailTemplate subject="Action Required: Stagnant Opportunity Alert" 
                        recipientType="User" 
                        relatedToType="Opportunity">
<messaging:htmlEmailBody>
    <p>Hello {!Receiving_User.FirstName},</p>

    <p style="color: #d73000; font-weight: bold;">
        An opportunity owned by one of your team members requires immediate attention.
    </p>

    <table style="border: 1px solid #ccc; padding: 10px;">
        <tr>
            <td><strong>Opportunity:</strong></td>
            <td><a href="{!Opportunity.Link}">{!Opportunity.Name}</a></td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
            <td><strong>Account:</strong></td>
            <td>{!Opportunity.Account}</td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
            <td><strong>Owner:</strong></td>
            <td>{!Opportunity.Owner}</td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
            <td><strong>Amount:</strong></td>
            <td>{!Opportunity.Amount}</td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
            <td><strong>Stage:</strong></td>
            <td>{!Opportunity.StageName}</td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
            <td><strong>Probability:</strong></td>
            <td>{!Opportunity.Probability}%</td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
            <td><strong>Days Stagnant:</strong></td>
            <td style="color: #d73000; font-weight: bold;">
                {!Opportunity.Days_In_Current_Stage__c} days
            </td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
            <td><strong>Close Date:</strong></td>
            <td>{!Opportunity.CloseDate}</td>
        </tr>
    </table>

    <p><strong>Recommended Actions:</strong></p>
    <ul>
        <li>Review opportunity with sales rep</li>
        <li>Identify blockers preventing progress</li>
        <li>Update close date if needed</li>
        <li>Consider marking as Closed Lost if no longer viable</li>
    </ul>

    <p>A high-priority task has been created for the opportunity owner.</p>

    <p>Best regards,<br/>
    Salesforce Sales Management System</p>
</messaging:htmlEmailBody>
</messaging:emailTemplate>

Rep Notification Template:

<p>Hi {!Opportunity.Owner.FirstName},</p>

<p>Your opportunity <a href="{!Opportunity.Link}">{!Opportunity.Name}</a> 
has been in the {!Opportunity.StageName} stage for 
{!Opportunity.Days_In_Current_Stage__c} days.</p>

<p><strong>Please take immediate action:</strong></p>
<ul>
    <li>Contact the customer to assess interest level</li>
    <li>Update the opportunity stage or close date</li>
    <li>Document next steps in the activity timeline</li>
    <li>If no longer viable, mark as Closed Lost</li>
</ul>

<p>Your manager has been notified and a high-priority task has been created.</p>

Step 4: Create Apex Class for Complex Escalation Logic

public class OpportunityEscalationService {

    // Main method to process stagnant opportunities
    public static void processStagnantOpportunities() {
        List<Opportunity> stagnantOpps = getStagnantOpportunities();

        if (!stagnantOpps.isEmpty()) {
            createEscalationTasks(stagnantOpps);
            sendEscalationEmails(stagnantOpps);
            updateOpportunityEscalationStatus(stagnantOpps);
            postChatterUpdates(stagnantOpps);
            logEscalationHistory(stagnantOpps);
        }
    }

    // Query stagnant opportunities
    private static List<Opportunity> getStagnantOpportunities() {
        Date thirtyDaysAgo = Date.today().addDays(-30);
        Date sevenDaysAgo = Date.today().addDays(-7);

        return [
            SELECT Id, Name, StageName, Amount, Probability, CloseDate,
                   OwnerId, Owner.ManagerId, Owner.Name, Owner.Email,
                   Owner.Manager.Name, Owner.Manager.Email,
                   AccountId, Account.Name,
                   Days_In_Current_Stage__c, Escalation_Count__c,
                   Last_Stage_Change_Date__c
            FROM Opportunity
            WHERE IsClosed = false
            AND Probability < 0.50
            AND Last_Stage_Change_Date__c <= :thirtyDaysAgo
            AND (Last_Escalation_Date__c < :sevenDaysAgo OR Last_Escalation_Date__c = null)
            ORDER BY Days_In_Current_Stage__c DESC
            LIMIT 200
        ];
    }

    // Create tasks for reps
    private static void createEscalationTasks(List<Opportunity> opportunities) {
        List<Task> tasksToCreate = new List<Task>();

        for (Opportunity opp : opportunities) {
            Task escalationTask = new Task(
                Subject = 'URGENT: Follow up on stagnant opportunity - ' + opp.Name,
                Priority = 'High',
                Status = 'Not Started',
                ActivityDate = Date.today().addDays(2),
                OwnerId = opp.OwnerId,
                WhatId = opp.Id,
                Description = buildTaskDescription(opp)
            );
            tasksToCreate.add(escalationTask);
        }

        if (!tasksToCreate.isEmpty()) {
            insert tasksToCreate;
        }
    }

    // Build task description
    private static String buildTaskDescription(Opportunity opp) {
        return 'This opportunity has been in the ' + opp.StageName + 
               ' stage for ' + opp.Days_In_Current_Stage__c + 
               ' days without progress.\n\n' +
               'Account: ' + opp.Account.Name + '\n' +
               'Amount: $' + opp.Amount + '\n' +
               'Probability: ' + opp.Probability + '%\n' +
               'Close Date: ' + opp.CloseDate + '\n\n' +
               'REQUIRED ACTIONS:\n' +
               '1. Contact customer to assess current interest level\n' +
               '2. Identify any blockers preventing progress\n' +
               '3. Update opportunity stage or close date\n' +
               '4. Document next steps\n' +
               '5. If no longer viable, mark as Closed Lost\n\n' +
               'This escalation has been sent to your manager.';
    }

    // Send escalation emails
    private static void sendEscalationEmails(List<Opportunity> opportunities) {
        List<Messaging.SingleEmailMessage> emails = new List<Messaging.SingleEmailMessage>();

        // Get email template
        EmailTemplate template = [
            SELECT Id 
            FROM EmailTemplate 
            WHERE DeveloperName = 'Stagnant_Opportunity_Manager_Alert' 
            LIMIT 1
        ];

        for (Opportunity opp : opportunities) {
            if (opp.Owner.ManagerId != null) {
                // Email to manager
                Messaging.SingleEmailMessage managerEmail = new Messaging.SingleEmailMessage();
                managerEmail.setTargetObjectId(opp.Owner.ManagerId);
                managerEmail.setWhatId(opp.Id);
                managerEmail.setTemplateId(template.Id);
                managerEmail.setSaveAsActivity(false);
                emails.add(managerEmail);

                // Email to rep
                Messaging.SingleEmailMessage repEmail = new Messaging.SingleEmailMessage();
                repEmail.setTargetObjectId(opp.OwnerId);
                repEmail.setWhatId(opp.Id);
                repEmail.setTemplateId(template.Id);
                repEmail.setSaveAsActivity(false);
                emails.add(repEmail);
            }
        }

        if (!emails.isEmpty()) {
            Messaging.sendEmail(emails);
        }
    }

    // Update escalation status
    private static void updateOpportunityEscalationStatus(List<Opportunity> opportunities) {
        List<Opportunity> oppsToUpdate = new List<Opportunity>();

        for (Opportunity opp : opportunities) {
            Opportunity oppUpdate = new Opportunity(
                Id = opp.Id,
                Escalation_Count__c = (opp.Escalation_Count__c != null ? 
                    opp.Escalation_Count__c + 1 : 1),
                Last_Escalation_Date__c = Date.today(),
                Escalation_Status__c = 'Escalated to Manager'
            );
            oppsToUpdate.add(oppUpdate);
        }

        if (!oppsToUpdate.isEmpty()) {
            update oppsToUpdate;
        }
    }

    // Post Chatter updates
    private static void postChatterUpdates(List<Opportunity> opportunities) {
        List<FeedItem> posts = new List<FeedItem>();

        for (Opportunity opp : opportunities) {
            String message = '@[' + opp.Owner.ManagerId + '] - ' +
                           'This opportunity has been stagnant for ' +
                           opp.Days_In_Current_Stage__c + ' days. ' +
                           'Owner: @[' + opp.OwnerId + ']\n\n' +
                           'Amount: $' + opp.Amount + '\n' +
                           'Stage: ' + opp.StageName + '\n' +
                           'Probability: ' + opp.Probability + '%';

            FeedItem post = new FeedItem(
                ParentId = opp.Id,
                Body = message,
                Type = 'TextPost'
            );
            posts.add(post);
        }

        if (!posts.isEmpty()) {
            insert posts;
        }
    }

    // Log escalation history
    private static void logEscalationHistory(List<Opportunity> opportunities) {
        List<Opportunity_Escalation_Log__c> logs = new List<Opportunity_Escalation_Log__c>();

        for (Opportunity opp : opportunities) {
            Opportunity_Escalation_Log__c log = new Opportunity_Escalation_Log__c(
                Opportunity__c = opp.Id,
                Escalation_Date__c = Date.today(),
                Days_Stagnant__c = opp.Days_In_Current_Stage__c,
                Stage_at_Escalation__c = opp.StageName,
                Amount_at_Escalation__c = opp.Amount,
                Escalation_Reason__c = 'No stage change for 30+ days',
                Escalated_To__c = opp.Owner.ManagerId
            );
            logs.add(log);
        }

        if (!logs.isEmpty()) {
            insert logs;
        }
    }
}

Step 5: Create Schedulable Class

global class OpportunityEscalationScheduler implements Schedulable {

    global void execute(SchedulableContext sc) {
        OpportunityEscalationService.processStagnantOpportunities();
    }
}

// Schedule to run daily at 8 AM
OpportunityEscalationScheduler scheduler = new OpportunityEscalationScheduler();
String cronExp = '0 0 8 * * ?';
System.schedule('Daily Opportunity Escalation', cronExp, scheduler);

Step 6: Create Dashboard

Dashboard Name: Stagnant Opportunity Management

Components: 1. Stagnant Opportunities Count (Gauge) - Show total stagnant opportunities

  1. Stagnant Opportunities by Owner (Bar Chart)

  2. Group by Owner, count opportunities

  3. Stagnant Opportunities by Stage (Donut Chart)

  4. Show which stages have most stagnant deals

  5. Days Stagnant Trend (Line Chart)

  6. Show average days stagnant over time

  7. Escalation Activity (Table)

  8. Show recent escalations with status

  9. At-Risk Revenue (Metric)

  10. Sum of amounts for stagnant opportunities

Key Considerations:

  • Notification Frequency: Prevent spam with cooldown period (7 days)
  • Escalation Levels: Consider multiple escalation tiers (30, 60, 90 days)
  • Exclusions: Exclude opportunities awaiting customer response
  • Manager Coverage: Handle reps without managers assigned
  • Closed Opportunities: Exclude closed won/lost from processing

Advanced Features:

Multi-Tier Escalation: 

- 30 days → Manager notification
- 45 days → VP notification
- 60 days → Automatic close lost if no action

Smart Escalation: - Consider deal size in escalation urgency - Factor in customer engagement history - Check for recent activities before escalating

Automated Remediation: - Auto-extend close date for stagnant deals - Suggest actions based on stage - Auto-create customer outreach campaigns

Governor Limits:

⚠️ Scheduled Jobs: Maximum 100 scheduled Apex jobs ⚠️ Batch Size: Process 200 records per execution ⚠️ Email Sends: 5,000 single emails per day ⚠️ Chatter Posts: Consider bulk vs individual posts

Best Practices:

✅ Use formula fields for real-time calculations ✅ Implement cooldown period to prevent spam ✅ Create detailed email templates for clarity ✅ Log all escalations for historical analysis ✅ Monitor escalation effectiveness with dashboards ✅ Train managers on escalation response procedures ✅ Review escalation criteria quarterly ✅ Provide clear action items in notifications ✅ Track time-to-resolution for escalated opportunities

docs.title: 🎯 Overview
docs.text:
Salesforce provides a comprehensive analytics ecosystem that enables organizations to transform raw data into actionable insights. The platform combines native reporting tools with advanced analytics through Tableau CRM (formerly Einstein Analytics) and full Tableau integration, offering solutions for every level of analytical sophistication.

Key Components:

  • Tableau CRM (Einstein Analytics): Salesforce-native analytics platform with AI-powered insights
  • Tableau Desktop & Server: Enterprise-grade business intelligence and visualization platform
  • Native Salesforce Reports & Dashboards: Built-in reporting tools for standard analytics
  • Einstein Discovery: AI and machine learning for predictive analytics
  • Embedded Analytics: Integration capabilities for seamless user experience

Value Proposition:

  • Unified Data View: Single source of truth across all business functions
  • AI-Powered Insights: Automated pattern detection and predictive analytics
  • Mobile-First Design: Access analytics anywhere, anytime
  • Seamless Integration: Native connectivity with Salesforce data and processes
  • Scalability: From departmental dashboards to enterprise-wide analytics

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: 📊 Tableau CRM (Einstein Analytics)
docs.text: Tableau CRM is Salesforce's native analytics platform, designed specifically for CRM data analysis with embedded AI capabilities. It provides a complete analytics workflow from data preparation to insight delivery.

docs.title: Core Components
docs.text:
Datasets:

  • Definition: Structured, optimized data collections prepared for analysis
  • Data Transformation: Built-in tools for cleaning, enriching, and transforming data
  • Data Synchronization: Automated updates from Salesforce objects and external sources
  • External Integration: Connect to databases, cloud storage, and third-party applications
  • Recipe-Based Prep: Visual data preparation workflows without coding

Lenses:

  • Purpose: Interactive data exploration and ad-hoc analysis tool
  • Quick Visualizations: Drag-and-drop interface for instant charts and graphs
  • Filtering & Grouping: Dynamic data segmentation and aggregation
  • Save as Dashboard: Convert exploratory analysis into shareable dashboards
  • Iteration: Rapid prototyping before final dashboard creation

Dashboards:

  • Interactive Visualizations: Multiple widgets with cross-filtering capabilities
  • User-Driven Exploration: Enable end users to drill down and discover insights
  • Mobile Optimization: Responsive design for phones and tablets
  • Sharing & Collaboration: Distribution via links, embedding, or scheduled delivery
  • Access Control: Row-level security and user-specific filtering

Apps:

  • Pre-Built Templates: Industry-specific analytics solutions (Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, etc.)
  • Custom App Creation: Build domain-specific analytics applications
  • App Exchange: Marketplace for third-party analytics solutions
  • Packaging: Bundle dashboards, lenses, and datasets for distribution

docs.title: Einstein Discovery
docs.text:
Automated Insights:

  • Pattern Detection: Automatically identify trends, outliers, and anomalies in data
  • Correlation Analysis: Discover relationships between variables without manual hypothesis testing
  • Natural Language Stories: AI-generated narratives explaining key findings
  • Smart Recommendations: Suggested actions based on data patterns
  • Continuous Learning: Models improve as more data becomes available

Predictive Analytics:

  • Regression Models: Predict continuous outcomes (revenue, deal size, customer lifetime value)
  • Classification Models: Predict categorical outcomes (win/loss, churn risk, lead conversion)
  • Time Series Forecasting: Project future trends based on historical patterns
  • Model Accuracy Metrics: R-squared, RMSE, precision, recall, and F1 scores
  • Feature Importance: Identify which factors drive predictions

What-If Scenarios:

  • Variable Manipulation: Adjust input values to see impact on predictions
  • Optimization: Identify optimal values for maximizing or minimizing outcomes
  • Sensitivity Analysis: Understand how changes affect results
  • Decision Support: Compare multiple scenarios side-by-side
  • Action Recommendations: Prescriptive guidance on best next steps

docs.title: SAQL (Salesforce Analytics Query Language)
docs.text:
Query Capabilities:

  • Advanced Filtering: Complex conditions with AND, OR, NOT logic
  • Aggregations: SUM, AVG, COUNT, MIN, MAX, MEDIAN, PERCENTILE
  • Grouping: Multi-level grouping with rollups and subtotals
  • Calculated Fields: Create derived metrics and dimensions on the fly
  • Window Functions: Running totals, moving averages, rank, and partition operations

Data Manipulation:

  • Projections: Select specific fields and create aliases
  • Joins: Combine multiple datasets with inner, left, and full joins
  • Unions: Concatenate datasets vertically
  • Cogroup: Advanced join operation for complex data relationships
  • Flatten: Unnest nested structures for analysis

docs.title: Data Integration Options
docs.text:
Salesforce Data Sync:

  • Object Selection: Choose which standard and custom objects to include
  • Field Mapping: Map Salesforce fields to dataset columns
  • Relationships: Preserve parent-child and lookup relationships
  • Incremental Refresh: Sync only changed records for efficiency
  • Real-Time Updates: Near real-time data availability (within minutes)

External Data Connectors:

  • Databases: Oracle, SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL, Snowflake, BigQuery
  • Cloud Storage: AWS S3, Azure Blob Storage, Google Cloud Storage
  • SaaS Applications: Workday, NetSuite, SAP, Oracle ERP
  • Data Warehouses: Redshift, Azure Synapse, Databricks
  • Streaming Data: Apache Kafka, AWS Kinesis for real-time ingestion

File Uploads:

  • CSV Files: Drag-and-drop upload with automatic field detection
  • Data Validation: Check for format errors and data quality issues
  • Schedule Updates: Automate regular file imports via SFTP or APIs
  • Large File Support: Handle datasets up to 100M rows
  • Append vs Replace: Choose between adding to existing data or full refresh

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: 🖥️ Tableau Desktop & Server
docs.text: Tableau provides enterprise-grade business intelligence capabilities with unlimited data source connectivity and advanced visualization options.

docs.title: Tableau Desktop
docs.text:
Visualization Types:

  • Basic Charts: Bar, column, line, area, pie, and scatter plots
  • Statistical Charts: Box plots, histograms, heat maps, and tree maps
  • Geographic Maps: Symbol maps, filled maps, density maps, and flow maps
  • Advanced Charts: Gantt charts, bullet graphs, waterfall charts, and funnel charts
  • Custom Visualizations: Build unique chart types using calculated fields and dual axes

Data Connection Architecture:

Live Connection                    Extract Connection
├─ Real-time queries              ├─ In-memory data engine
├─ No data duplication            ├─ Scheduled refreshes
├─ Always current                 ├─ Faster query performance
├─ Database performance dependent ├─ Offline capability
└─ Ideal for small datasets       └─ Ideal for large datasets

Data Preparation Features:

  • Join Operations: Inner, left, right, full outer, cross joins with visual interface
  • Union Operations: Combine tables vertically with automatic field matching
  • Data Blending: Merge data from different sources without physical joins
  • Pivoting: Transform columns to rows or rows to columns
  • Splitting: Divide fields based on delimiters or patterns
  • Aggregation: Pre-aggregate data for performance optimization

Calculation Types:

  • Basic Calculations: Arithmetic, string manipulation, date functions
  • Table Calculations: Running totals, percent of total, moving averages, rank, percentile
  • Level of Detail (LOD) Expressions: FIXED, INCLUDE, EXCLUDE for granular control
  • Parameters: User-controlled values for dynamic analysis
  • Sets: Custom groupings based on conditions or manual selection

docs.title: Tableau Server/Cloud
docs.text:
Publishing & Collaboration:

  • Workbook Publishing: Deploy dashboards to server for organization-wide access
  • Version Control: Track changes, restore previous versions, and manage updates
  • Commenting: Threaded discussions on visualizations for collaboration
  • Subscriptions: Email or Slack notifications with dashboard snapshots
  • Data-Driven Alerts: Automated notifications when metrics cross thresholds

Security Architecture:

  • Row-Level Security: Filter data based on user attributes and permissions
  • User Filters: Dynamic filters that adapt to logged-in user
  • Permission Hierarchy: Project, workbook, view, and data source permissions
  • Data Source Security: Control who can view, edit, or download data
  • SSL/TLS Encryption: Secure data transmission and storage
  • Active Directory Integration: Leverage existing authentication systems

Governance & Administration:

  • Content Management: Organize workbooks and data sources in projects
  • Usage Analytics: Track views, user engagement, and performance metrics
  • Performance Monitoring: Identify slow dashboards and optimize queries
  • Metadata Management: Document data sources, calculations, and lineage
  • Backup & Recovery: Automated backups and disaster recovery procedures
  • Load Balancing: Distribute workload across multiple servers for scalability

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: 🔗 Salesforce-Tableau Integration
docs.text: The integration between Salesforce and Tableau creates a powerful unified analytics environment, enabling seamless data flow and embedded visualizations.

docs.title: Direct Integration Methods
docs.text:
Salesforce Connector:

  • Native Connection: Built-in connector optimized for Salesforce data structures
  • Object Access: Connect to all standard and custom objects with metadata
  • Relationship Preservation: Maintain lookup and master-detail relationships
  • Formula Fields: Access calculated fields and roll-up summaries
  • Historical Data: Query archived data and field history tracking

Live Salesforce Data:

  • Real-Time Queries: Execute queries directly against Salesforce in real-time
  • API Optimization: Uses Salesforce SOAP and REST APIs efficiently
  • Row Limits: Respects Salesforce API governor limits
  • Incremental Refresh: Fetch only changed records to minimize API calls
  • Query Performance: Optimize filters and aggregations for faster results

Pre-Built Dashboards:

  • Sales Cloud Analytics: Pipeline, forecasting, territory, and activity dashboards
  • Service Cloud Analytics: Case management, agent performance, and SLA tracking
  • Marketing Cloud Analytics: Campaign ROI, lead funnel, and attribution
  • Commerce Cloud Analytics: Order trends, customer behavior, and product performance
  • Quick Start Templates: Accelerate deployment with industry best practices

docs.title: Data Synchronization Strategies
docs.text:
Automated Refresh:

  • Schedule Configuration: Daily, hourly, or custom refresh intervals
  • Off-Peak Scheduling: Run refreshes during low-usage periods
  • Failure Notifications: Email alerts when refreshes fail
  • Refresh History: Track success/failure rates and performance trends
  • Parallel Refreshes: Execute multiple refreshes simultaneously

Incremental Updates:

  • Change Tracking: Identify modified records since last refresh
  • Delta Loading: Transfer only changed data to reduce processing time
  • Time-Based Filters: Use LastModifiedDate or SystemModstamp fields
  • Performance Benefits: 10-100x faster than full refreshes for large datasets
  • Data Consistency: Ensure referential integrity during incremental loads

Full Refresh:

  • Complete Data Reload: Replace entire dataset with current data
  • Data Cleanup: Remove deleted records and fix corruption
  • Structural Changes: Handle schema modifications (new fields, changed types)
  • Monthly Cadence: Recommended frequency for full refreshes
  • Validation: Compare row counts and checksums before/after

docs.title: Embedding Options
docs.text:
Tableau Dashboards in Salesforce:

  • Lightning Components: Native Lightning Web Components for Tableau views
  • Visualforce Pages: Embed Tableau views in classic Salesforce pages
  • Canvas Integration: Full-screen Tableau experience within Salesforce
  • Context Passing: Pass Salesforce record IDs to filter Tableau dashboards
  • Single Sign-On (SSO): Seamless authentication without separate login

Einstein Analytics Embedding:

  • Record Pages: Embed analytics directly on Account, Opportunity, Case pages
  • Lightning App Pages: Create custom pages with embedded analytics
  • Home Pages: Display key metrics on Salesforce home dashboard
  • Console Integration: Embed analytics in service console for agents
  • Mobile Support: Responsive embedded analytics for Salesforce mobile app

Technical Implementation:

Embedding Architecture:
├─ Trusted Authentication
├─ SAML SSO Configuration
├─ Connected Apps Setup
├─ JavaScript API Integration
├─ Responsive iframe Sizing
└─ Parameter Passing (Record ID, User Context)

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: 📈 Native Salesforce Reports & Dashboards
docs.text: Salesforce provides built-in reporting capabilities for standard analytics without requiring separate tools or licenses.

docs.title: Report Types
docs.text:
Tabular Reports:

  • Structure: Simple list of records in rows with columns
  • Use Cases: Contact lists, opportunity pipelines, case queues
  • Limitations: No grouping or subtotals
  • Sorting: Multi-column sorting with ascending/descending options
  • Export: CSV, Excel, or printable formats

Summary Reports:

  • Structure: Records grouped by one or more fields with subtotals
  • Aggregations: Sum, average, min, max, count for numeric fields
  • Grouping Levels: Up to 3 levels of grouping
  • Charts: Add visual representations above report data
  • Use Cases: Sales by region, cases by status, leads by source

Matrix Reports:

  • Structure: Records grouped by both rows and columns
  • Two-Dimensional Analysis: Compare metrics across multiple dimensions
  • Grand Totals: Row, column, and overall totals
  • Use Cases: Revenue by product and region, cases by priority and type
  • Complexity: Most flexible but slowest report type

Joined Reports:

  • Structure: Multiple report blocks with different object relationships
  • Cross-Object Analysis: Combine unrelated data in single report
  • Independent Filters: Each block has its own filter criteria
  • Shared Grouping: Group all blocks by common field
  • Use Cases: Compare opportunities, leads, and cases side-by-side

docs.title: Dashboard Components
docs.text:
Component Types:

  • Charts: Bar, line, pie, donut, funnel, scatter, gauge charts
  • Metrics: Single number displays with conditional formatting
  • Tables: Display detailed records or summary data
  • Visualforce Pages: Custom visualizations built with code
  • Lightning Components: Modern custom components with rich interactivity

Dashboard Features:

  • Dynamic Dashboards: Show user-specific data based on running user
  • Cross-Filtering: Click chart elements to filter other components
  • Drill-Down: Click dashboard elements to view underlying report details
  • Auto-Refresh: Schedule dashboard data refreshes (hourly, daily, weekly)
  • Mobile Optimization: Responsive layouts for mobile devices
  • Export: Save dashboard as PDF or image

Formula Functions:

Common Report Formulas:
├─ PARENTGROUPVAL(): Reference parent group values
├─ PREVGROUPVAL(): Reference previous group values
├─ Bucketing: Group numeric/picklist values into ranges
├─ Conditional Formatting: Color-code based on thresholds
└─ Cross-Object Formulas: Calculate across related objects

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: 🤖 Einstein Analytics Features
docs.text: Einstein Analytics brings artificial intelligence and machine learning capabilities to Salesforce analytics, enabling predictive and prescriptive insights.

docs.title: AI-Powered Insights
docs.text:
Automated Pattern Detection:

  • Trend Analysis: Identify upward, downward, or cyclical trends automatically
  • Seasonality Detection: Recognize recurring patterns (monthly, quarterly, yearly)
  • Outlier Identification: Flag unusual data points that deviate from normal patterns
  • Segment Discovery: Automatically find meaningful customer or product segments
  • Statistical Significance: Determine if patterns are meaningful or random noise

Anomaly Detection:

  • Real-Time Monitoring: Continuously scan metrics for unusual behavior
  • Baseline Establishment: Learn normal patterns from historical data
  • Alert Thresholds: Configure sensitivity for anomaly detection
  • Root Cause Analysis: Identify factors contributing to anomalies
  • Use Cases: Fraud detection, quality control, system monitoring

Predictive Forecasting:

  • Time Series Models: ARIMA, exponential smoothing, and neural network approaches
  • Confidence Intervals: Quantify uncertainty in predictions
  • Scenario Planning: Model different future scenarios
  • Forecast Accuracy: Track prediction accuracy over time
  • Model Retraining: Automatically update models with new data

Clustering Analysis:

  • Customer Segmentation: Group customers by behavior, demographics, or value
  • K-Means Clustering: Partition data into distinct groups
  • Hierarchical Clustering: Create nested groupings with similarity trees
  • Cluster Profiling: Describe characteristics of each cluster
  • Actionable Segments: Target marketing or service strategies by cluster

docs.title: Embedded Analytics
docs.text:
Integration Points:

  • Lightning Record Pages: Show relevant analytics on every record
  • Lightning App Pages: Build custom analytics applications
  • Lightning Home Pages: Display KPIs and dashboards on home screen
  • Utility Bar: Access analytics sidebar on any Salesforce page
  • Mobile App: Full analytics experience in Salesforce mobile

Component Types:

  • Wave Dashboard Component: Embed complete dashboards
  • Wave Chart Component: Display single chart or metric
  • Wave Report Component: Show tabular data with filtering
  • Custom Lightning Components: Build bespoke analytics experiences
  • Einstein Discovery Insights: Display predictions and recommendations

Context-Aware Analytics:

  • Record Context: Automatically filter analytics by current record
  • User Context: Personalize analytics based on user role and permissions
  • Dynamic Filters: Apply page context to embedded dashboards
  • Action Buttons: Trigger Salesforce workflows from analytics
  • Deep Linking: Navigate from analytics to detailed records

docs.title: Mobile Analytics
docs.text:
Mobile Optimization:

  • Touch Interactions: Swipe, pinch-to-zoom, and tap gestures
  • Responsive Design: Layouts adapt to phone and tablet screen sizes
  • Simplified Visualizations: Charts optimized for small screens
  • Progressive Loading: Load critical data first, details on demand
  • Gesture Navigation: Intuitive swiping between dashboard pages

Offline Capabilities:

  • Data Caching: Store dashboard data locally for offline access
  • Sync When Connected: Update cached data when network available
  • Offline Indicators: Clear visual cues when viewing cached data
  • Selective Caching: Choose which dashboards to make available offline
  • Storage Management: Control cache size and retention policies

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: 💼 Common Use Cases
docs.text: Salesforce analytics solutions address a wide range of business challenges across sales, service, marketing, and finance functions.

docs.title: Sales Analytics
docs.text:
Pipeline Analysis:

  • Pipeline Health: Monitor deal velocity, conversion rates, and stage progression
  • Bottleneck Identification: Find stages where deals stall or drop out
  • Coverage Ratio: Compare pipeline value to quota targets
  • Aging Analysis: Track how long opportunities remain in each stage
  • Predictive Close Dates: AI-powered predictions of when deals will close

Win/Loss Analysis:

  • Win Rate Metrics: Overall and by product, region, competitor
  • Loss Reason Tracking: Categorize and analyze why deals are lost
  • Competitive Intelligence: Understand competitor strengths and weaknesses
  • Deal Size Patterns: Identify factors that influence deal value
  • Improvement Recommendations: Data-driven coaching opportunities

Sales Forecasting:

  • Bottoms-Up Forecasting: Aggregate opportunity projections
  • Top-Down Targets: Set and track against strategic goals
  • Forecast Accuracy: Compare predictions to actual results
  • Scenario Modeling: Best case, worst case, and most likely scenarios
  • Territory Planning: Allocate quotas based on market potential

Territory Performance:

  • Quota Attainment: Track progress toward individual and team quotas
  • Activity Metrics: Calls, meetings, emails by rep and territory
  • Customer Coverage: Ensure adequate attention to all accounts
  • Resource Allocation: Identify territories needing more support
  • Compensation Analysis: Link performance to commission structure

docs.title: Service Analytics
docs.text:
Case Metrics:

  • Volume Trends: Track case creation and closure rates over time
  • Backlog Management: Monitor open case inventory and aging
  • Priority Distribution: Ensure high-priority cases receive attention
  • Channel Analysis: Compare performance across phone, email, chat, portal
  • Escalation Tracking: Monitor cases requiring management intervention

Agent Performance:

  • Case Resolution Time: Average and median time to close
  • First Contact Resolution: Percentage resolved without follow-up
  • Customer Satisfaction: CSAT and NPS scores by agent
  • Productivity Metrics: Cases handled per hour/day
  • Knowledge Usage: Track which articles help solve cases

SLA Compliance:

  • SLA Violation Rates: Percentage of cases meeting SLA targets
  • Time to First Response: Measure against SLA thresholds
  • Time to Resolution: Track total resolution time
  • SLA Risk Monitoring: Predict which cases may violate SLA
  • Entitlement Verification: Ensure cases receive proper service levels

First Call Resolution:

  • FCR Rate: Percentage of cases resolved on initial contact
  • FCR by Issue Type: Identify categories with low FCR
  • Knowledge Gap Analysis: Find topics needing better documentation
  • Training Opportunities: Target coaching based on FCR performance
  • Cost Savings: Calculate financial impact of improved FCR

docs.title: Marketing Analytics
docs.text:
Campaign ROI:

  • Cost per Lead: Marketing spend divided by leads generated
  • Lead Conversion Rate: Percentage of leads becoming opportunities
  • Revenue Attribution: Track revenue back to specific campaigns
  • Multi-Touch Attribution: Credit multiple campaigns in buyer journey
  • Budget Optimization: Reallocate spend to highest-performing campaigns

Lead Conversion Funnel:

  • Stage Conversion Rates: MQL to SQL, SQL to Opportunity, Opportunity to Closed Won
  • Velocity Metrics: Time spent in each funnel stage
  • Leakage Analysis: Identify where leads drop out of funnel
  • Source Performance: Compare lead quality by source (organic, paid, events, etc.)
  • Nurture Campaign Effectiveness: Measure impact of drip campaigns

Customer Journey Mapping:

  • Touchpoint Analysis: All interactions across marketing, sales, and service
  • Path to Purchase: Common sequences leading to conversion
  • Drop-Off Points: Where customers exit the journey
  • Cross-Channel Behavior: How customers interact across channels
  • Journey Optimization: Identify improvements to accelerate conversion

Channel Performance:

  • Channel ROI: Compare performance of email, social, search, display, etc.
  • Engagement Metrics: Click rates, time on site, bounce rates by channel
  • Attribution Modeling: First-touch, last-touch, linear, time-decay models
  • Cross-Channel Synergies: How channels work together
  • Budget Allocation: Optimal spend mix across channels

docs.title: Financial Analytics
docs.text:
Revenue Analysis:

  • Revenue Trends: Year-over-year, quarter-over-quarter growth
  • Product Mix: Revenue contribution by product line
  • Geographic Performance: Revenue by region, country, territory
  • Customer Segmentation: Revenue by industry, size, or custom segments
  • Recurring vs One-Time: Subscription and maintenance revenue tracking

Profitability Metrics:

  • Gross Margin: Revenue minus cost of goods sold
  • Operating Margin: Profitability after operating expenses
  • Customer Profitability: Profit per customer or account
  • Product Profitability: Margin analysis by product or service
  • Cost Structure Analysis: Fixed vs variable cost breakdown

Budget vs Actual:

  • Variance Analysis: Compare actual spend to budgeted amounts
  • Drill-Down Capability: Investigate significant variances
  • Forecast Accuracy: How well budget predictions match reality
  • Rolling Forecasts: Update projections based on current trends
  • Department Performance: Budget adherence by cost center

Cash Flow Analysis:

  • Accounts Receivable Aging: Track outstanding invoices
  • Days Sales Outstanding: Average time to collect payment
  • Payment Trends: On-time vs late payment patterns
  • Cash Conversion Cycle: Time from purchase to cash collection
  • Working Capital Management: Optimize cash, receivables, and payables

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: ✅ Best Practices
docs.text: Implementing these best practices ensures successful analytics deployment and sustained value delivery.

docs.title: Data Quality
docs.text:
Data Cleanliness:

  • Standardization: Consistent formats for names, addresses, phone numbers
  • Validation Rules: Prevent bad data entry at the source
  • Deduplication: Merge duplicate records before analysis
  • Completeness Checks: Ensure required fields are populated
  • Data Governance: Establish data ownership and stewardship

Data Consistency:

  • Naming Conventions: Consistent field and object naming across organization
  • Picklist Management: Standardize option values and prevent proliferation
  • Formula Standardization: Use consistent calculation methodologies
  • Cross-System Alignment: Match definitions across Salesforce and other systems
  • Documentation: Maintain data dictionary with field definitions

docs.title: User Adoption
docs.text:
Training & Enablement:

  • Role-Based Training: Customize training to user needs and skill levels
  • Hands-On Practice: Provide sandbox environments for learning
  • Quick Reference Guides: One-page cheat sheets for common tasks
  • Video Tutorials: Short, focused videos on specific features
  • Office Hours: Regular Q&A sessions with analytics experts

Change Management:

  • Executive Sponsorship: Visible support from senior leadership
  • Champions Network: Identify and empower power users in each department
  • Communication Plan: Regular updates on new features and capabilities
  • Success Stories: Share examples of analytics-driven wins
  • Feedback Loops: Continuously gather and act on user feedback

docs.title: Performance Optimization
docs.text:
Query Optimization:

  • Filter Early: Apply filters before joins and aggregations
  • Indexed Fields: Use indexed fields in filter conditions
  • Limit Rows: Return only necessary data, use pagination for large datasets
  • Avoid Complex Calculations: Pre-calculate fields in ETL when possible
  • Cache Results: Enable result caching for frequently accessed queries

Dashboard Design:

  • Minimize Components: Fewer components load faster
  • Optimize Queries: Each component should use efficient queries
  • Lazy Loading: Load data only when component becomes visible
  • Aggregated Data: Use summary tables instead of detailed data
  • Scheduled Refreshes: Pre-calculate dashboard data off-peak hours

docs.title: Security & Governance
docs.text:
Access Controls:

  • Principle of Least Privilege: Grant minimum necessary access
  • Row-Level Security: Filter data based on user attributes
  • Field-Level Security: Hide sensitive fields from unauthorized users
  • Sharing Rules: Extend access appropriately using sharing rules
  • Regular Access Reviews: Audit permissions quarterly

Governance Framework:

  • Naming Conventions: Standard prefixes, suffixes, and formats
  • Development Lifecycle: Separate dev, test, and production environments
  • Version Control: Track changes to reports and dashboards
  • Documentation Standards: Require documentation for all analytics assets
  • Approval Processes: Formal review before production deployment

docs.title: Mobile Optimization
docs.text:
Design for Mobile:

  • Simplified Layouts: Fewer components, larger touch targets
  • Vertical Scrolling: Design for single-column layouts
  • Touch-Friendly: Minimum 44x44 pixel touch targets
  • Progressive Disclosure: Show summary first, details on demand
  • Offline Support: Make critical dashboards available offline

Performance Considerations:

  • Minimize Data Transfer: Reduce payload size for mobile networks
  • Image Optimization: Compress images and use appropriate formats
  • Lazy Loading: Load data as user scrolls
  • Caching Strategy: Cache data locally to reduce network calls
  • Battery Efficiency: Minimize background processing and animations

docs.title: Storytelling with Data
docs.text:
Clear Insights:

  • Start with the Answer: Lead with key finding, then supporting details
  • Visual Hierarchy: Use size, color, and position to guide attention
  • Consistent Design: Maintain color schemes and layouts across dashboards
  • Contextual Information: Provide comparisons to prior periods or benchmarks
  • Call to Action: Make recommendations, don't just present data

Effective Visualizations:

  • Choose Right Chart Type: Match visualization to data and message
  • Remove Clutter: Eliminate unnecessary grid lines, legends, and labels
  • Color with Purpose: Use color to highlight important information
  • Label Clearly: Ensure axes, legends, and data points are understandable
  • Tell a Story: Organize dashboards to guide users through narrative

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: 🔬 Advanced Analytics Capabilities
docs.text: Advanced analytics techniques enable sophisticated analysis beyond traditional reporting.

docs.title: Predictive Analytics
docs.text:
Regression Models:

  • Linear Regression: Predict continuous outcomes based on linear relationships
  • Logistic Regression: Predict binary outcomes (yes/no, win/loss)
  • Multiple Regression: Use multiple predictor variables
  • Polynomial Regression: Model non-linear relationships
  • Regularization: Ridge, Lasso, Elastic Net to prevent overfitting

Classification Models:

  • Decision Trees: Rule-based classification with interpretable results
  • Random Forests: Ensemble of decision trees for improved accuracy
  • Gradient Boosting: Sequential tree building to minimize errors
  • Neural Networks: Deep learning for complex pattern recognition
  • Support Vector Machines: Find optimal decision boundaries

Time Series Forecasting:

  • ARIMA: Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average models
  • Exponential Smoothing: Weight recent observations more heavily
  • Prophet: Facebook's forecasting tool for business time series
  • LSTM Networks: Deep learning for sequence prediction
  • Ensemble Methods: Combine multiple forecasting techniques

Model Evaluation:

Regression Metrics:
├─ R-squared: Proportion of variance explained
├─ RMSE: Root Mean Square Error
├─ MAE: Mean Absolute Error
└─ MAPE: Mean Absolute Percentage Error

Classification Metrics:
├─ Accuracy: Overall correct predictions
├─ Precision: True Positives / (True Positives + False Positives)
├─ Recall: True Positives / (True Positives + False Negatives)
├─ F1 Score: Harmonic mean of precision and recall
└─ AUC-ROC: Area Under Receiver Operating Characteristic curve

docs.title: Prescriptive Analytics
docs.text:
Optimization Recommendations:

  • Linear Programming: Optimize resource allocation subject to constraints
  • Integer Programming: Optimization with discrete decision variables
  • Goal Programming: Satisfy multiple, potentially conflicting objectives
  • Network Optimization: Route planning, supply chain design
  • Dynamic Programming: Sequential decision optimization

What-If Analysis:

  • Scenario Comparison: Evaluate multiple alternative futures
  • Sensitivity Analysis: Understand impact of changing assumptions
  • Simulation: Monte Carlo methods to model uncertainty
  • Goal Seeking: Find inputs needed to achieve target output
  • Constraint Analysis: Identify binding constraints and slack

Decision Support:

  • Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis: Evaluate alternatives across multiple dimensions
  • Cost-Benefit Analysis: Quantify financial impact of decisions
  • Risk Assessment: Probability and impact of different outcomes
  • Recommendation Engines: AI-powered next-best-action suggestions
  • Automated Actions: Trigger workflows based on analytical insights

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: ⚖️ Comparison: Tableau CRM vs Tableau
docs.text: Understanding the differences between Tableau CRM and full Tableau helps organizations choose the right tool for their needs.

docs.title: Feature Comparison Matrix
docs.text: Feature Tableau CRM (Einstein Analytics) Tableau Desktop/Server Primary Use Case Salesforce-native CRM analytics Enterprise business intelligence Data Sources Primarily Salesforce, limited external Any data source (500+ connectors) User Interface Salesforce Lightning embedded Standalone desktop/web application Learning Curve Moderate (Salesforce knowledge helpful) Steeper (specialized BI training) AI/ML Capabilities Einstein Discovery (built-in) TabPy, R, Python integration (custom) Licensing Model Per user ($75-$150/month) Per user ($70-$150/month) Deployment Cloud-based (Salesforce infrastructure) Desktop, Server, or Cloud Mobile Experience Excellent (Salesforce mobile app) Good (dedicated mobile app) Embedding Native Salesforce embedding Web-based embedding with API Data Prep Recipe-based visual data prep Tableau Prep Builder Query Language SAQL (Salesforce-specific) Calculated fields, LOD expressions Governance Salesforce security model Tableau Server security model Performance Optimized for Salesforce data Optimized for any data source

docs.title: When to Choose Tableau CRM
docs.text:
Ideal Scenarios:

  • Salesforce-Centric Organization: 80%+ of analytical data resides in Salesforce
  • CRM Use Cases: Sales, service, marketing analytics focused on CRM data
  • Embedded Analytics: Desire to embed analytics directly in Salesforce workflows
  • AI-First Approach: Want built-in predictive analytics without custom coding
  • Unified Platform: Prefer single-vendor solution for CRM and analytics
  • Rapid Deployment: Need quick time-to-value with pre-built apps

Advantages:

  • Seamless Salesforce integration with automatic metadata refresh
  • No separate login or context switching for end users
  • Einstein Discovery included for predictive analytics
  • Mobile experience integrated with Salesforce mobile app
  • Pre-built apps and dashboards for common CRM use cases
  • Easier administration with unified Salesforce security model

docs.title: When to Choose Tableau
docs.text:
Ideal Scenarios:

  • Multi-Source Analytics: Need to combine data from many disparate sources
  • Complex Visualizations: Require advanced chart types and custom visualizations
  • Large-Scale BI: Enterprise-wide analytics across all departments
  • Data Warehouse-Centric: Primary data source is cloud data warehouse (Snowflake, Redshift, BigQuery)
  • Advanced Users: Analysts and data scientists who need maximum flexibility
  • Non-Salesforce Data: Majority of data comes from systems other than Salesforce

Advantages:

  • Unlimited data source connectivity (500+ native connectors)
  • Most powerful and flexible visualization capabilities
  • Larger user community and extensive training resources
  • Better performance with very large datasets (billions of rows)
  • Advanced statistical and geospatial analysis
  • More mature platform with longer track record

docs.title: Hybrid Approach
docs.text:
Best of Both Worlds:

Many organizations deploy both Tableau CRM and Tableau in a complementary fashion:

  • Tableau CRM: For CRM users (sales reps, service agents, marketers) who need embedded analytics
  • Tableau: For analysts, executives, and operations teams who need cross-functional insights
  • Integration Points: Use Tableau Server to blend Salesforce data with other sources, then embed results in Salesforce

Technical Integration:

  • Data Layer: Use Tableau Prep to create analytics-ready datasets from Salesforce and other sources
  • Consumption Layer: Serve different user populations with appropriate tools
  • Single Sign-On: Unified authentication across both platforms
  • Unified Governance: Coordinate security and access policies

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Salesforce CPQ (Configure, Price, Quote) and Revenue Cloud represent a comprehensive solution for managing the complete quote-to-cash and revenue lifecycle. These powerful tools enable organizations to automate complex pricing scenarios, streamline quote generation, and ensure compliance with modern revenue recognition standards.

Key Benefits:

  • Accelerated Sales Cycles: Reduce quote generation time from days to minutes
  • Pricing Accuracy: Eliminate manual pricing errors with automated calculations
  • Revenue Compliance: Built-in support for ASC 606 and IFRS 15 standards
  • Subscription Management: Complete lifecycle management for recurring revenue models
  • Scalability: Handle complex product catalogs and pricing structures

Market Position:

CPQ and Revenue Cloud solutions are essential for modern B2B organizations, particularly those with:

  • Complex product configurations
  • Subscription-based business models
  • Multi-tier pricing structures
  • High-volume quoting requirements
  • Compliance and audit needs

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: CPQ Core Components
docs.text: Salesforce CPQ consists of several integrated components that work together to streamline the quoting process from product selection through contract execution.

docs.title: Product Configuration
docs.text:
The product configuration engine enables sales teams to build complex product bundles while enforcing business rules and constraints.

Configuration Capabilities:

  • Product Bundles: Group related products with parent-child relationships
  • Option Constraints: Define dependencies and exclusions between products
  • Configuration Rules: Automate product selection based on business logic
  • Product Features: Organize options into logical feature categories
  • Dynamic Pricing: Adjust pricing based on configuration choices

Configuration Attributes:

  • Configuration type (Bundle, Option, Component)
  • Quantity rules and constraints
  • Feature categories and grouping
  • Hidden vs. visible options
  • Required vs. optional components

docs.title: Pricing & Discounting
docs.text:
A sophisticated pricing engine that handles complex pricing scenarios across multiple dimensions.

Pricing Mechanisms:

  • Price Books: Organize pricing by market, region, or customer segment
  • Price Rules: Automate pricing calculations based on conditions
  • Volume-Based Pricing: Tier pricing based on quantity thresholds
  • Contracted Pricing: Customer-specific negotiated rates
  • Discount Schedules: Time-based and volume-based discount structures
  • Approval Workflows: Route discounts exceeding thresholds for approval

Pricing Formula Components:

  • List price and cost price
  • Partner and distributor pricing
  • Markup and margin calculations
  • Currency conversion handling
  • Promotional pricing

docs.title: Quote Generation
docs.text:
Create professional, accurate quotes with extensive customization capabilities.

Quote Features:

  • Quote Templates: Branded, professional document templates
  • Multi-Currency Quotes: Automatic currency conversion and management
  • Quote Line Editor: Intuitive interface for managing quote lines
  • Amendment Quotes: Modify existing agreements seamlessly
  • Renewal Quotes: Automated generation for subscription renewals

Quote Line Fields:

  • Product details and descriptions
  • Quantity and pricing information
  • Discount amounts and percentages
  • Start and end dates
  • Subscription terms
  • Custom fields for specific requirements

docs.title: Guided Selling
docs.text:
Intelligent product recommendations that help sales teams identify the right solutions.

Guided Selling Components:

  • Product Recommendations: AI-powered suggestions based on context
  • Cross-Sell and Upsell: Identify additional revenue opportunities
  • Configuration Wizard: Step-by-step product selection
  • Product Selection Rules: Filter available products based on criteria
  • Search and Filter: Advanced product catalog navigation

docs.title: Revenue Cloud Components

docs.title: Billing
docs.text:
Comprehensive billing management that supports diverse revenue models.

Billing Capabilities:

  • Invoice Generation: Automated invoice creation from orders
  • Payment Processing: Integration with payment gateways

  • Usage-Based Billing: Meter and bill actual consumption

docs.title: Revenue Recognition
docs.text:
Ensure compliance with modern revenue recognition standards while automating complex calculations.

  • Performance Obligations: Track and manage contract obligations

Recognition Methods:

  • Percentage of completion
  • Deliverable-based recognition
  • Custom recognition rules

docs.title: Subscription Management

Complete lifecycle management for subscription-based business models.

Subscription Features:

  • Amendments and Renewals: Mid-term changes and contract extensions
  • Evergreen Subscriptions: Auto-renewing contracts
  • Co-termination: Align subscription end dates
  • Proration: Calculate charges for partial periods

Subscription Actions:

  • Remove products

  • Change quantities

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Salesforce Experience Cloud (formerly Community Cloud) enables organizations to create branded digital experiences for customers, partners, and employees using Salesforce data and functionality. It provides a comprehensive platform for building self-service portals, partner relationship management systems, and employee collaboration spaces.

Experience Cloud leverages the power of the Salesforce platform to deliver secure, scalable, and customizable digital experiences that connect users with the data, processes, and people they need. The platform supports multiple experience types, each tailored to specific audience needs and business objectives.

Key Capabilities:

  • Branded Digital Experiences: Create custom-branded portals that reflect your organization's identity
  • Self-Service Functionality: Empower users to find answers, manage accounts, and resolve issues independently
  • Seamless Integration: Connect with Salesforce CRM, Service Cloud, Marketing Cloud, and external systems
  • Mobile Responsiveness: Deliver consistent experiences across desktop, tablet, and mobile devices
  • Scalability: Support thousands of external users with enterprise-grade performance

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Experience Types
docs.text: Experience Cloud supports three primary experience types, each designed for specific user audiences and business scenarios.

docs.title: Customer Community
docs.text:
Customer Communities provide self-service portals that enable customers to access information, resolve issues, and manage their relationships with your organization independently.

Core Capabilities:

  • Self-Service Portals: Allow customers to find answers and resolve issues without contacting support
  • Case Management: Enable customers to create, track, and update support cases
  • Knowledge Base Access: Provide searchable articles, FAQs, and documentation
  • Order Tracking: Give customers visibility into order status and history
  • Account Management: Allow customers to update profiles, manage contacts, and view account information

Benefits:

  • Reduced support costs through self-service
  • Improved customer satisfaction with 24/7 access
  • Faster issue resolution
  • Enhanced customer engagement

docs.title: Partner Community
docs.text:
Partner Communities facilitate collaboration between your organization and channel partners, distributors, and resellers, streamlining partner relationship management.

Core Capabilities:

  • Deal Registration: Enable partners to register opportunities and track approval status
  • Lead Distribution: Automatically route and distribute leads to appropriate partners
  • Co-Selling Collaboration: Facilitate joint selling efforts between internal teams and partners
  • Partner Onboarding: Streamline partner enrollment and training processes
  • Performance Tracking: Provide partners with visibility into sales metrics and incentives

Benefits:

  • Increased partner engagement and productivity
  • Streamlined partner operations
  • Improved visibility into partner performance
  • Enhanced collaboration and communication

docs.title: Employee Community
docs.text:
Employee Communities create internal collaboration spaces that connect employees with information, tools, and colleagues across the organization.

Core Capabilities:

  • Internal Collaboration: Enable teams to share files, ideas, and updates
  • Knowledge Sharing: Create centralized repositories for company knowledge and best practices
  • Team Workspaces: Provide dedicated spaces for projects, departments, or initiatives
  • Recognition Programs: Celebrate employee achievements and milestones
  • HR Services: Deliver HR resources, benefits information, and self-service tools

Benefits:

  • Enhanced employee engagement and communication
  • Improved knowledge sharing and collaboration
  • Streamlined access to HR and IT services
  • Stronger organizational culture

docs.title: Core Features
docs.text: Experience Cloud provides a comprehensive set of features for building, customizing, and managing digital experiences.

docs.title: Site Builder
docs.text:
The Lightning Experience Site Builder provides a visual, drag-and-drop interface for creating and customizing Experience Cloud sites without extensive coding.

Key Features:

  • Lightning Web Components (LWC): Leverage modern, performant component framework

  • Template Customization: Modify existing templates or create custom designs
  • SEO Optimization: Configure meta tags, URLs, and sitemap generation

  • Custom Lightning Web Components

docs.title: Branding & Theming
docs.text:
Create consistent, on-brand experiences that reflect your organization's visual identity.

  • Mobile Optimization: Ensure branding translates effectively to mobile devices

docs.title: User Management

Access Control:

  • Sharing Rules: Configure data visibility and access permissions
  • Guest User Access: Enable unauthenticated access to public content

User Provisioning:

  • Self-registration with email verification
  • Admin-assisted user creation
  • Bulk user import via Data Loader
  • Just-in-time (JIT) provisioning via SSO

docs.title: Security & Sharing
docs.text: Experience Cloud implements robust security controls to protect organizational data while enabling external user access.

docs.title: External Sharing
docs.text:
Configure how external users access and share Salesforce records within Experience Cloud.

Sharing Mechanisms:

  • Sharing Sets: Define which records external users can access based on field values
  • External Organization-Wide Defaults: Set baseline access levels for external users
  • Community-Specific Sharing Rules: Create experience-specific record access rules
  • Record Access for External Users: Manage individual record permissions

Sharing Set Configuration:

  • Map user fields to record fields for automatic access
  • Support multiple sharing sets per experience
  • Real-time sharing calculation
  • Audit sharing access for compliance

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Secure user authentication with multiple options for identity verification and access control.

Authentication Methods:

  • Self-Registration: Allow users to create accounts with email verification
  • Social Sign-On: Enable login via Google, Facebook, LinkedIn, and other providers
  • Single Sign-On (SSO): Integrate with enterprise identity providers via SAML or OAuth
  • Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA): Require additional verification for sensitive operations
  • Password Policies: Enforce strong password requirements and expiration rules

SSO Configuration:

  • SAML 2.0 support for enterprise identity providers
  • OAuth 2.0 for API and mobile authentication
  • Just-in-time user provisioning
  • Session management and timeout controls
  • Identity provider-initiated and service provider-initiated flows

Security Best Practices:

  • Enable MFA for all external users
  • Implement IP restrictions for sensitive experiences
  • Use SSO for enterprise-grade authentication
  • Regularly audit user access and permissions
  • Monitor login anomalies and suspicious activity
